articles.title: CELEBRATING 100 YEARS

paras.en: MEDINA, OH (January 6, 2025) – Carlisle Brake & Friction (CarlisleCBF), a global leader in brake and friction technology and part of the CentroMotion family of brands, has reached a momentous milestone – its 100th anniversary.
Since its founding in 1925, the company has lived up to its tagline, "Braking New Ground," by consistently pioneering innovative solutions that have propelled industries forward.

"For 100 years, Carlisle has been synonymous with groundbreaking innovation and unwavering reliability in the braking industry," says Tom Vanderlaan, Chief Commercial Officer (CCO) of CentroMotion. "This milestone is a testament to the dedication of our employees, the trust of our customers, and the enduring strength of our products. As we celebrate our centennial, we reaffirm our commitment to continuous innovation, strong partnerships, and giving back to the communities we serve."
A Century of Innovation in Motion Control

For a century, CarlisleCBF has been at the forefront of motion control, pushing the boundaries of performance with its industry-leading brakes and friction materials. Through unwavering commitment to R&D, the company has earned the trust of customers worldwide, establishing itself as a cornerstone of reliability.
Celebrating 100 Years of Braking New Ground: A Digital Celebration

To commemorate this historic milestone, CarlisleCBF is launching a comprehensive digital celebration. This virtual experience will allow customers, employees and industry partners to delve into the company’s rich history, groundbreaking innovations and commitment to excellence through historical photographs and stories.

A core aspect of the celebration is fostering a sense of community. CarlisleCBF invites customers, employees and industry partners to join the journey by visiting their dedicated anniversary webpage, www.CarlisleCBF.com, and following their story on social media.
The webpage and social media channels will serve as a virtual time capsule, showcasing CarlisleCBF's rich history, ground-breaking milestones and product innovations.

To encourage participation and celebrate the impact CarlisleCBF has had, a social media campaign is launching with the hashtag #CarlisleCBF100. Participants are encouraged to share stories, photos and memories that illustrate how CarlisleCBF products have impacted their lives or businesses. The most engaging submissions will be featured on the company's social media channels and website.
By combining digital storytelling with interactive social media, CarlisleCBF aims to create a lasting legacy for its first century of service, while fostering a spirit of community and appreciation.

Carlisle Brake & Friction, a CentroMotion brand, is a globally recognized leader in the development and manufacture of highly innovative brake and friction system solutions to service a diverse range of motion control applications. The comprehensive nature of CarlisleCBF's brake system expertise includes hydraulic control products, industrial brake assemblies, and wet and dry friction material for brake, clutch, and transmission applications, as well as aftermarket replacement products. Our full-system product offering, supported by our industry-experience staff of experts, provides our customers with brake system solutions that set them apart from their competition. www.carlislecbf.com

articles.title: Michigan Auto Body Association Celebrates Inaugural Open House
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: The Michigan Auto Body Association (MABA) held its inaugural event, an open house hosted by America’s Most Wanted 4×4, on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026. The afternoon program ran from 1 to 6 p.m. and drew members, prospective members and vendors eager to learn what the new association is all about.
MABA announced its official founding as a statewide professional association and its affiliation with the Society of Collision Repair Specialists (SCRS) late last year.

The day opened with a “meet the board” session, where attendees asked board members why the association was formed, how the bard came together and where MABA is headed. As an affiliate of SCRS, MABA then welcomed Aaron Schulenburg, executive director of SCRS, for a virtual introduction. Schulenburg welcomed MABA and its members to the SCRS partnership and highlighted benefits popular with independent collision repairers, including SCRS’s health care program and 401(k) offering.

Stephanie Sheppard of CARS Co-Op followed with an overview of another MABA member benefit, one designed to help Michigan collision repairers save money on day-to-day purchases. Host America’s Most Wanted 4×4 then led attendees on a tour of its facility and shared the story of its rapid growth in a specialized segment of the industry.
MABA was co-founded by Don Speace and Dustin DeLongpre of Axalta.

“This was a dream come true,” said Speace. “As we followed up with and helped our customers, we kept hearing the same thing over and over: Michigan needs a voice. We need someone representing our collision repair industry here in Michigan, like our colleagues have in other states. So here we are! Dustin and I did the background work and helped form the founding board based on what leaders across our industry told us. With a lot of hard work, we launched the association just a couple of months ago, and here we are today.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “I think the industry had a very successful event today,” said Jason Taylor, chair of MABA. “Members, member candidates and vendors all came out to see what MABA is about, and from the conversations I’ve had, they were impressed. When it was time to meet the board, they had questions we need to follow up on, and that’s exactly what we were hoping for. We want to hear from our industry and learn what we need to do to make things happen. In that respect, this was a very good start.”

“This event showed both the desire and the need within our industry,” said Joe Townsend, treasurer of MABA. “A number of vendors quickly stepped up as sponsors, giving back to the industry in a way they trust will make it better. I’m very appreciative and pleased with today’s turnout. We had more than 100 registrants in just over a month since we announced the event, with only a few last-minute no-shows. That speaks volumes.”
Attendee questions gave the board clear direction. Brian Johnson, vice chair of MABA, pointed to one that stood out: how will MABA decide which legislation to pursue when points of view differ?

“We don’t have that answer at this moment, but it will definitely be discussed at our next board meeting,” said Johnson. “We’ve been focused on putting our infrastructure in place: meeting the legal requirements of running an association, building budgets, setting goals and making it a priority to secure a strong lobbyist to represent us in Lansing. Now it’s time to get into the details, so hearing these questions was exciting.”

Taylor added that another question, how will members be kept up to date and given a voice, “reinforced what the board has said all along. We need to include our members and keep them educated and informed. Frankly, that’s why we’re here.”
Secretary Scott Webster was encouraged by how closely shop owners engaged with the presentations.

“We worked through a few technical difficulties, but afterward I saw attendees sitting down with Stephanie from CARS Co-Op to ask questions,” said Webster. “That kind of engagement reassures us that we’re doing the right thing for the right reasons.” He added with a laugh, “I enjoyed networking with my peers, and even more, enjoying a meeting without having to take the minutes for a change.”
The open house wrapped up with pizza, beverages and time for attendees to network.

MABA plans to build on the open house’s momentum with more events in the first quarter of 2027. Dates, locations and programs will be announced in the coming weeks. Collision repair professionals, vendors and industry partners are encouraged to watch for updates at michiganaba.org and on MABA’s social media channels, and to reach out about membership and sponsorship opportunities.

articles.title: SCRS Recognizes Car-O-Liner as RDE, OEM Summit Sponsor at SEMA 2026
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: The Society of Collision Repair Specialists (SCRS) is recognizing Car-O-Liner, part of the Total Shop Solutions family of Snap-on brands, as a sponsor of the Repairer Driven Education (RDE) series and the OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit during the 2026 SEMA Show Nov. 3-6 in Las Vegas.

“Precise measurement and proper repair procedures are the foundation of a safe repair, and that only becomes more true as vehicles grow more sophisticated,” said Doug Bortz, sales manager, North America for Car-O-Liner. “Supporting SCRS and the RDE series is one way we help repairers keep pace. We’re proud to return as sponsors, and we look forward to seeing the industry come together in Las Vegas to learn from the people building these vehicles.”
Car-O-Liner will exhibit in the Snap-on booth in the Upper South Hall, booth no. 32017.
OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit Schedule

The OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit takes place Thursday, Nov. 5 from 12:30-4:30 p.m. The three-session program follows vehicle safety from national objectives through vehicle engineering and into the collision repair process, and SCRS encourages attendees to experience the sessions as a connected series.

The afternoon opens with “The National Safety Objective: Safer Vehicles, Safer Roads” from 12:30-1:30 p.m., featuring National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) Deputy Administrator Lee White. White will present the agency’s vehicle and roadway safety priorities, emerging transportation technologies and data-driven research, then join SCRS Executive Director Aaron Schulenburg for a one-on-one conversation on the role of repair in maintaining vehicle safety.

From 2–3 p.m., “Engineering the Safety Benefit: From Requirement to Real-World Performance” brings together safety and ADAS engineering leaders from General Motors, Rivian and Ford Motor Company. Panelists will explain how automakers translate safety objectives into vehicle technologies, establish performance requirements and evaluate whether those technologies produce measurable real-world benefits. Panelists include Michael Carpenter and Jameson Collins of General Motors, Byung Joo (BJ) Kim of Rivian and Jeremy Nelson of Ford Motor Company.

Engineers from General Motors, Ford and Rivian will examine what today’s sensors can do, what can affect their performance and how engineering requirements become repair procedures and calibration strategies. articles.title: Total Loss Auto Claims Weigh on Insurance Customer Satisfaction
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: How satisfied are auto insurance customers in that moment of truth when they need to file a claim? According to the recently released JD Power 2026 U.S. Auto Claims Satisfaction Study, that depends on whether the damage is repairable or not.

This year, overall customer satisfaction with the auto insurance claims process improves 4 points (on a 1,000-point scale) when damages are repairable but declines 12 points when vehicles are deemed a total loss, marking a third consecutive year of declining satisfaction for total loss claims. Overall, 26% of auto insurance claims were classified as total losses in 2026, up from just 16% four years ago as vehicle repairs become more costly, more customers keep their vehicles on the road longer and higher deductibles remove smaller repairs from the claim process.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “A complex mix of trends are conspiring to make this an incredibly challenging market environment for managing auto insurance claims customer satisfaction,” said Mark Garrett, director of global insurance intelligence at JD Power. “On the positive side, rates are coming down and repair cycle times have improved dramatically, so customers who can have their vehicles fixed are showing high levels of satisfaction with the claims experience. However, persistent affordability challenges have many customers keeping vehicles longer or making changes to their policy, such as dropping rental coverage or taking on higher insurance deductibles. Additionally, many customers are upside down on their auto loans, which means the payoff in a total loss scenario can be less than they owe on their vehicles. All of these can make for a poor customer experience in the event of a total loss.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The following are some key findings of the 2026 study:

- Overall satisfaction split based on vehicle repairability: The overall auto claims customer satisfaction score is 700, which is unchanged from last year. Satisfaction scores diverge sharply, however, depending on whether the vehicle is able to be repaired. Overall satisfaction improves 4 points year over year when vehicles are repaired and declines 12 points year over year when vehicles are deemed a total loss. Satisfaction with total losses has continued to trend down for a third consecutive year, declining 46 points since 2023.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - Effects of total losses exacerbated by macroeconomic trends: More than one-fourth (26%) of auto insurance claims resulted in a total loss in 2026, up from just 16% four years ago. Total loss customer satisfaction scores are lowest (490) when the amount paid by the insurer does not cover the amount the customer still owes on their vehicle loan. Among total loss customers with loans on their vehicles, 25% received payouts that were less than what they owed on their vehicle.

- Repair cycle times improve significantly: When vehicles can be repaired, the likelihood of getting them repaired quickly is getting much easier. Claim volumes are down sharply, so shops have more capacity for repair work, resulting in average repair cycle times of just 15.3 days through the first quarter of 2026, a reduction of 10 days from the first quarter of 2024.

- Room to improve on cross-channel communications: Overall customer satisfaction scores are highest (804) when customers completely agree that their insurer provided a seamless experience across channels. Satisfaction scores are lowest (390) when customers disagree with that statement, which often results from not understanding explanations, using multiple channels to ask questions or digital tools not working as expected. Currently, insurers are delivering a seamless cross-channel experience just 54% of the time, one of the lowest-performing key performance indicators in the study.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Amica ranks highest in overall customer satisfaction with a score of 775. Nationwide (743) ranks second and Automobile Club of Southern CA (AAA) (740) ranks third.

The U.S. Auto Claims Satisfaction Study examines the auto claims experiences of customers from the largest insurance providers throughout the U.S. across eight dimensions (in order of importance): trust; fairness of settlement; people; time to settle claim; communication; ease of resolving claim; ease of starting claim; and digital channels. The 2026 study is based on responses from 8,261 auto insurance customers who settled a claim within the past nine months prior to participating in the survey. It was fielded from September 2025 through August 2026. The study excludes claimants whose vehicle incurred only glass/windshield damage or was stolen, or who only filed a roadside assistance claim.

articles.title: Dipstick Replacement Sensors: How They Work
articles.author: Andrew Markel

paras.en: GM has taken a lot of guff recently for eliminating the dipstick on some of their newer V8 engines and replacing it with a sensor. Let’s talk about how those sensors actually work, and how and when they measure the oil level.

It’s not like, for example, a brake master cylinder that has a float and a level that turns on the light on the dash when it reaches a certain level. These sensors are ultrasonic. In other words, it’s sending out a sound wave into the oil pan and determining the oil level that way.

How does it know when to measure the level of oil in the oil pan? If you’re using a dipstick, the vehicle would be parked, it probably wouldn’t be running, and that’s when you’re checking the oil level. The sensor works the same way: It’s only measuring the oil level at certain instances. Let’s say it’s in Park when you first start up. Let’s say you’re sitting at a traffic light; that is when it’s measuring the level.
For more on sensors and how they work, including oxygen and TPMS sensors, watch the video above.

articles.title: The Effect of Thin Brake Fluid on Vehicle Systems
articles.author: Christian Hinton

paras.en: Lower-viscosity brake fluid plays a growing role in modern brake systems. Today’s vehicles require brake fluid to move quickly through hydraulic control units that support ABS, stability control, traction control and several ADAS braking functions.
Modern brake systems use faster valves, tighter internal passages and more frequent automatic brake interventions than systems used 20 years ago.

As a result, many late-model vehicles require lower-viscosity brake fluid. The goal is to maintain efficient fluid movement at low temperatures so the hydraulic unit can build and release pressure quickly.
Lower-Viscosity Brake Fluid Supports Faster Response

The ABS hydraulic unit is used, not only during panic stops, but for electronic stability control, traction control, adaptive cruise control, collision mitigation braking and automatic emergency braking.

Inside the hydraulic control unit, brake fluid moves through small valves and narrow passages. Lower viscosity allows pressure to increase and decrease faster, helping the system make quicker and more precise braking corrections.
Brake fluid condition is also important. Moisture contamination can increase viscosity, lower the boiling point and raise corrosion risk.
Technicians should use the exact brake fluid specified by the vehicle manufacturer and replace it according to the proper service information.

articles.title: Breaking Free a Seized Wheel Bearing Hub
articles.author: BCA Bearings by NTN

paras.en: A wheel bearing hub unit that is seized into a suspension knuckle can turn a routine repair into a struggle. The hub may be retained by bolts, but corrosion between the hub and knuckle can hold it in place after every fastener is removed. Understanding what formed that bond helps you choose an effective removal method and avoid damaging the knuckle, axle, or nearby components.
When a steel hub seizes in a knuckle bore, oxygen and moisture have reacted with metal at the interface. For iron in the steel, a simplified rust-forming reaction is:

The iron hydroxide then changes into hydrated iron oxides—the reddish-brown corrosion commonly called rust. These corrosion products take up more space than the original metal. As they build up in the narrow clearance between the hub and knuckle, they can wedge the two parts together. But, the oxides are very reactive and brittle.

The joint may also involve dissimilar metals. Many hubs are made of steel, while some knuckles are aluminum. In the presence of moisture, these metals can form a galvanic cell that accelerates corrosion. De-icers and road salt can make the problem worse in areas that receive snow. When a steel hub is mounted in an aluminum knuckle, galvanic corrosion can occur alongside rust on the steel hub, so it may not be accurate to describe the entire bond as iron oxide. BCA Bearings identifies galvanic corrosion at steel hub and aluminum knuckle interfaces as a common cause of hubs becoming difficult to separate.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The goal of removal is to break the mechanical bond created by corrosion products. Vibration, impact or movement can crack them. Heat can create stress at the interface, while penetrants may reduce friction and help the parts move once a gap opens. Dedicated rust removers can react chemically with corrosion, but they may also attack the base metal or nearby finishes.

During the vehicle inspection, look for other corrosion damage. Dust shields and parking brake components inside the rotor hat can be perforated by rust and corrosion. Spotting this damage during the inspection can help you avoid delays while waiting for replacement parts.
What heat and chemicals can—and can’t—do

Heat does not reverse the rust reaction. It does not turn iron oxide back into iron. Instead, heating and cooling create differential expansion and contraction between the hub, knuckle, and corrosion layer. That movement can stress and crack brittle deposits. If the outer part of the joint expands more than the inner part, the temporary increase in clearance can help the components move.

Where you apply heat matters. The knuckle surrounds the hub, so heating the knuckle near the bore can expand the bore; however, uncontrolled torch heat can damage or distort the knuckle and nearby ball joints, seals, sensors, brake parts, or suspension components. BCA recommends against torch heating the knuckle and suggests an induction heater for localized heat at the wheel end.

If you plan to use heat, follow the vehicle and tool manufacturers’ instructions, and apply it only where you can control its effects. Be aware of wiring for the wheel speed sensor and brake pad wear sensor, as well as suspension bushings that could be damaged by heat. You are not trying to melt the hub unit. The goal is to use controlled heating and expansion to help break the corrosion bond.

Penetrants work differently. Most penetrating oils do not chemically dissolve iron oxide. They can seep into small clearances, lubricate contact surfaces and reduce friction as the hub begins to move. A light tap or controlled vibration may help the fluid reach the interface. Give it time to soak, and reapply as needed.

Rust removers, often acid-based, are designed to react with or dissolve corrosion. They may be useful on accessible parts after removal, but they are not automatically safe to use on an assembled hub and knuckle. Check product compatibility with aluminum, coatings, seals and nearby components. Keep penetrants and other flammable products away from open flames and hot surfaces, and follow label directions before applying heat.

When selecting a penetrant, make sure it is a penetrant and not a lubricant. Penetrants are formulated to wick into areas between the hub unit and knuckle. Also, penetrants do not catch fire or damage rubber and plastic materials like ball joint boots. If any penetrant contaminates the brake pads or rotor, clean it off immediately with a solvent.
Most of all, take your time and read the directions with these products. Also, use in a well-ventilated area because some of the ingredients can cause health problems.

Always begin with the vehicle safely supported and the service procedure for that application in hand. In recent years there have been a lot of tools introduced to remove hub units faster. They can range from a simple bar the attaches to the flange that you can strike with a sledge hammer, to application specific tools that use hydraulics to force the hub unit out of the bore. But, all of these tool do the same thing, they help to breakdown oxides between the hub and knuckle.

An air hammer can help, but technique matters more than simply increasing force or buying a larger air hammer. The key is to use a suitable blunt attachment on the hub’s mounting flange or ears to make the hub rotate slightly in the knuckle. Avoid driving the tool between the hub and knuckle as a wedge; that can gouge the bore or break the casting. BCA recommends using the air hammer to rotate the hub flange relative to the knuckle, while keeping the tool off the knuckle. Once the hub moves, continue around the flange and pull it out squarely.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: A hub puller, hub shocker, or forcing-screw tool applies controlled extraction force. Use the correct adapters for the vehicle and make sure the tool is centered and aligned for a straight pull. Increase force gradually, checking for movement and repositioning only as the tool instructions allow..

Another tip is to look at the service information for the procedures and recommended tools. Some OEMs might include an flat part of the knuckle that can be used by a puller or forcing screw to remove the hub unit.

After removal, clean corrosion from the bore and mounting face without removing base metal. Inspect for cracks, gouging, or deformation, then install the replacement hub according to the vehicle procedure and specified torque.

You can add a light coating of moly anti-seize to the bore of the knuckle to decrease the chances of future corrosion. Avoid getting any anti-seize on the bolt holes of the knuckle. Any lubricant can change the torque value of a fastener.
The most important step to removing a stuck hub unit is to review the service information and TSB. Often, the service procedure will be amended to include information on procedures and special tools.

If you’re unable to free the hub unit from the knuckle, don’t take it personally. One of the most important skills gained through experience is knowing when to stop trying to remove a hub unit with heat, brute force or chemicals. In some cases, recommending replacement of the knuckle along with the hub unit is more productive and makes for a better repair.

Aftermarket replacement knuckles are available, and some lines cover applications where hub units can be especially difficult to remove. Experience also helps you recognize which applications are most likely to cause frustration.
Wheel End Service: Do You Have These Tools?

Over the past decade, tool companies have introduced new wheel end service tool and have improved existing tools. These next generation tools can be used on their own or together to make your next hub unit job easier.

Hub Strikers: A hub striker is a solid metal bar that bolts to the hub flange and provides a striking point outside the wheel well. This helps reduce the risk of hitting the fender while using a sledgehammer. Hub strikers can work well on some Gen 2 and Gen 3 hub units that use orbital forming to retain the flange and set bearing preload. Depending on the application, they can make removal much faster.

Lug Nuts and Washers: Another tool you can use to hammer on the hub unit is an old brake rotor with the same lug pattern. Secure the rotor to the flange with lug nuts and washers. The rotor provides a solid surface to strike with your hammer.

Forcing Screws: A forcing screw uses a threaded rod or fastener to apply force between the hub flange and the knuckle, pushing the hub outward. Some applications allow a suitable bolt to be used as a forcing screw, but it must have adequate thread engagement and bear against a solid part of the knuckle. Purpose-built tool sets use a plate that attaches to the hub, often at the wheel studs, and a forcing screw to push the hub out. Use the correct setup for the vehicle and keep the force aligned with the hub.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Slide Hammer: A slide hammer can attach to the hub flange and apply repeated outward force as the hammer is moved along its shaft. It can be effective when the knuckle does not provide a suitable surface for a forcing screw. Use an appropriate hub adapter and keep the hammer’s path clear of the body and nearby components.

Air Hammer: An air hammer can help break the corrosion bond by vibrating or rotating the hub flange relative to the knuckle. Use a suitable attachment and work around the flange without striking or gouging the knuckle. Tool size alone does not determine effectiveness; consider the hammer’s stroke, operating rate, air supply, and how well you can control it. More force is not always better. BCA recommends using the air hammer to rotate the hub flange rather than wedging the tool between the hub and knuckle.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Hydraulic Press: On some vehicles, you may need to remove the knuckle to free the hub. Success depends on using the correct fixtures and adapters to support the knuckle securely and keep the press load aligned. Special press plates are available for some applications. Protect the knuckle, dust shield, and machined surfaces from damage, and follow the tool manufacturer’s instructions.

Heat: Heat can help loosen the joint through differential expansion and contraction; it does not reverse the corrosion reaction. Options include a propane or MAP-Pro torch and an induction heater. A torch can supply sufficient heat, but it is difficult to control and can damage CV-joint, tie-rod, and ball-joint boots, along with other nearby parts. An induction heater uses an electromagnetic field to heat metal, and many units include a flexible coil that can be positioned around the hub or knuckle. Use only a heating method and location appropriate for the application. BCA cautions against torch-heating the knuckle and recommends localized induction heating for wheel-end work.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Chemicals: Penetrants are formulated to flow into tight clearances and reduce friction at the hub-to-knuckle interface. Some use solvents or other additives, but most penetrating oils do not dissolve rust. Apply the product as directed and allow time for it to soak in. Tapping or gently working the hub can help the penetrant reach the joint. Rust removers are different: many react chemically with corrosion, but they may also attack the base metal, coatings, or nearby finishes. Check product compatibility before use.

articles.title: FORVIA Partners With Raiqon to Advance AI Engineering
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: FORVIA, a global automotive supplier, and Raiqon GmbH have formed a strategic partnership to advance artificial intelligence in automotive engineering. Raiqon specializes in scalable AI solutions for regulated engineering environments.

The partnership focuses on applying artificial intelligence (AI) to requirements engineering, a critical step in product development. This process involves defining, analyzing and managing technical requirements. Depending on product complexity, development projects can involve up to 15,000 individual requirements.
FORVIA Integrates AI Into Engineering Processes

FORVIA will deploy the solution within its secure IT environment using Raiqon’s multi-agent AI platform. The platform integrates data from multiple engineering applications. The companies are adapting the solution to the specific needs of FORVIA HELLA and Faurecia Clarion Electronics.

The platform automates key activities across the development process, including requirement analysis, identification of similarities and reuse of previous assessments. It also detects inconsistencies and automatically creates missing links.
By reducing manual effort, the solution allows engineers to focus on new requirements while increasing productivity.

“Artificial Intelligence is becoming a key enabler of innovation and competitiveness in the automotive industry,” said Martin Fischer, CEO of FORVIA. “Through our partnership with Raiqon, and as part of our IGNITE transformation journey, we are accelerating the digital transformation of our engineering processes, empowering our teams to work more efficiently while maintaining the highest standards of quality, safety and compliance. articles.title: ZF Expands ProVia Commercial Vehicle Parts Range
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: Ten years after its launch, ZF Aftermarket is expanding its ProVia brand’s commercial vehicle spare parts portfolio. The brand offers cost-effective repair solutions for workshops, distributors, fleet operators and truck drivers. The expansion supports vehicle uptime while addressing the needs of aging vehicle fleets.
ZF Plans to Triple ProVia Parts Range by 2027

The anniversary year marks a new phase in the development of the ProVia brand. The company recently added transmission spare parts to its established portfolio. Existing product ranges include air braking, air processing, ECAS, driveline control and trailer products. The expansion continues, with clutches and air compressors set to follow.

By 2027, ZF Aftermarket plans to triple its ProVia range, adding more than 830 part numbers. The expansion will focus primarily on pneumatics and driveline-related products, prioritizing compressors, clutches and further extensions to the transmission portfolio. The company will initially launch the program across Europe, IMEA and APAC in 2026, followed by North and South America.
ProVia Offers Repair Options for Aging Commercial Vehicles

Commercial vehicle operators increasingly need cost-effective repair options that extend vehicle life while maintaining quality, safety and reliability. ProVia addresses this need with aftermarket spare parts that combine cost efficiency with dependable performance.

ZF Aftermarket develops ProVia parts according to original equipment (OE) production quality standards and dedicated ProVia aftermarket specifications. The company bases these specifications on original equipment manufacturer (OEM) requirements and benchmark testing.

The quality approach includes advanced supplier qualification, repeatable and approved production processes and 100% end-of-line testing before packaging. The company also conducts in-house validation tests to confirm performance and longevity. ZF Aftermarket applies certifications such as ISO, TÜV, SAE or ECE where required.
This approach supports the expansion into additional product categories, giving customers more options to maintain commercial vehicles efficiently and cost-effectively.

“Over the past ten years, ProVia has helped customers keep commercial vehicles on the road with reliable, cost-efficient spare parts. As the market continues to demand practical solutions for aging fleets, we are expanding the range in the areas that matter most to workshops, distributors, fleet operators and the truck drivers who depend on vehicle uptime every day – from transmission parts to clutches and air compressors. This is how ProVia delivers trusted value while supporting vehicle uptime,” says Aleksander Rabinovitch, head of Business Line Commercial Vehicles, ZF Aftermarket.

The addition of transmission spare parts gives customers more options to maintain vehicle performance while managing lifecycle costs. ProVia parts serve as direct replacement solutions, with fit and function that support efficient repairs in demanding workshop environments.

The growing ProVia portfolio gives distributors additional competitively priced spare parts that combine quality with affordability. Workshops gain components that support straightforward installation and efficient repair processes.

Fleet operators and independent truck drivers gain access to cost-efficient repair solutions that help reduce maintenance costs. These components also support vehicle uptime and help keep vehicles operational longer.
The expanded ProVia range addresses commercial vehicle aftermarket needs, including parts reliability, availability, safety and cost.

articles.title: 'It isn't under control at all': Live Science readers respond to whether AI is making them lazy
articles.author: Kenna Hughes-Castleberry

paras.en: While people use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help with tasks like learning new skills or answering questions, a new study suggests that these benefits may come with a downside.

The findings, presented at the 2026 Conference on Language Modeling in San Francisco earlier this month, revealed that people who used AI assistance for reading comprehension or math problems were more likely to struggle or give up when the AI assistance was removed. The results suggest that relying too much on AI could lower people's motivations to overcome challenging situations.
In the wake of this study, Live Science recently polled its readers on whether they felt AI was making them less motivated after using it.
More than 140 readers voted in the poll, with 30% of voters picking "No, I don't use AI at all, so this situation doesn't apply to me."

"If AI were only a tool, controlled by those who use it I might give it a try," said one commenter in response. "But it isn't under control at all. It gets into your bank accounts and moves money without authorization. It encourages suicide and self-harm. It is addictive and makes people lazy. I know someone who uses it to answer questions and while it is detailed, it makes her lazier, asking one question and getting the answer without her searching for it. AI Is a danger. It should not be allowed."

articles.title: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune could destroy each other sooner than we thought, simulations hint
articles.author: Abha Jain

paras.en: When the sun inevitably dies, not even the outer solar system will be safe from the resulting chaos, new research hints.Scientists have long thought the outer solar system — which comprises the four giant planets Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — would mostly retain its present-day appearance for hundreds of billions of years to come. But a new study suggests that the outer giants may develop weirdly shaped orbits as the sun runs out of fuel, causing the planets to cross paths and destroy themselves through collisions within three billion years of the sun's transformation into a red giant.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The findings, published Sept. 21 in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, could change our understanding of what kinds of exoplanets orbit certain stars.

In about 5 billion years, the sun will balloon outward as a red giant after exhausting all of the hydrogen in its core. During this red giant phase, our star will swell to 100 times its present-day size, gobbling up Mercury, Venus and possibly even Earth in the process, Nathan Kaib, a planetary scientist at the University of Oklahoma who wasn't involved in the new research, told Live Science in an email. Following this violent swelling, the sun will crumple into a collapsed core called a white dwarf.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Until now, scientists thought the four outer planets would escape this phase relatively unscathed. A 1998 simulation-based study suggested that the gas the sun spews from its outer layers will push this planetary quartet outward, doubling the radius of each planet's orbit. Only the gravitational impact of a runaway star could destabilize this new order, and such events are thought to occur only once every billion billion years.

These predictions hinged on the assumption that the sun will eject its outer layers smoothly. However, recent observations of stars suggest a jerkier loss of mass, with gas clouds lofted by plumes of plasma in the sun — as though our star were spitting out mass blobs. "They're kind of like coronal mass ejections, except much larger," Jim Fuller, a professor of theoretical astrophysics at Caltech and co-author of the new study, told Live Science in an email.

Each "blob" pushes the star backward, similar to how a fired bullet causes a gun to recoil. Although every push is small, moving the sun just a few feet per second, many pushes can, over time, impart the equivalent of an enormous kick that alters the sun's speed by several hundred feet per second. In fact, astronomers have already seen white dwarfs suffer such kicks in other star systems.

When Fuller, who studied these kicks, described them to Konstantin Batygin, a professor of planetary science at Caltech and the study's first author, Batygin "realized this would have important consequences for the evolution of our own solar system," Fuller said. That's because the kicks change the sun's gravitational pulls on everything around it.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

To determine how the sun's mass loss would influence the giant planets, Batygin created computer-based simulations of the sun and the outer planets. The researchers considered three scenarios: if the sun lost its mass smoothly, if it spit out distinct mass blobs during its entire time evolving as a red giant, and if the sun spewed the blobs only during its last stages. The researchers also varied each ejected blob's mass.

The first scenario produced results similar to those of previous studies, with the outer solar system retaining almost all of its features for billions of years. In contrast, the other two cases had drastically different results. Using 672 simulations, the researchers found that if the sun lost mass in blobs, the giant planets would be thrown into chaos, switching places, developing weirdly oval-shaped orbits, and even getting ejected out of the solar system entirely. Most dramatically, in 96% of the simulations with the heaviest ejected mass packets, the planets get destroyed as they crashed into each other.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: These developments also happened much more rapidly — less than a few hundred million years after the sun transformed into a white dwarf, or even during the red giant phase, in the most extreme scenarios.

The study's findings hint that analogues of the present-day outer solar system around white dwarf stars are less likely to exist than previously thought. Kaib noted that the study's results suggest that planets with oval-shaped orbits should dominate instead. It's thought that habitable planets could exist around white dwarfs, but this study's findings show that our understanding of those distant star systems may be incomplete, and that such worlds may, in reality, be unstable.

Batygin, K., Fuller, J., & Adams, F. C. (2026). Terminal instability of the solar system triggered by stochastic solar mass loss. The Astrophysical Journal Letters, 1009(2), L22. https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/aea290

She did a masters degree in biology, specializing in neuroscience, from the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, India, and is almost through with a bachelor's degree in archaeology from the University of Leicester, UK. She's also a self-taught space enthusiast, and so loves writing about topics in astronomy, archaeology and neuroscience.

articles.title: Neuroscientists reveal method to train people to have lucid dreams — and it involves virtual reality and mediation
articles.author: Kamal Nahas

paras.en: Lucid dreaming — in which the dreamer is aware that they are dreaming and can sometimes influence the dream's trajectory — is a skill that can be honed, a new study finds. And the researchers found that doing this is surprisingly easy, after training participants to do exactly that using virtual reality (VR) twice a week for just one month.

The study's results could have practical benefits, said Daniel Morris, a cognitive neuroscientist at Northwestern University who studies dreams and was not involved with the work. "Lucid dreaming can benefit people with nightmares by allowing them to transform their nightmares into positive dreams and feel greater agency in their dreams," Morris told Live Science in an email.

Before this study, published Sept. 28 in the journal Frontiers in Psychology, neuroscientists tried to induce lucid dreaming with various methods. These included meditation exercises and so-called reality checks, in which participants ask themselves while awake whether unusual phenomena they encounter — such as people wearing odd Halloween costumes — are real or if they're dreaming. The idea is that they will ask themselves the same question in their sleep during bizarre dreams.
However, "for most people, our day-to-day lives may not feel 'dream-like,'" Morris said, explaining why reality checks have had mixed results and don't reliably trigger lucid dreaming.
Since dream-like scenarios are rare in waking life, the neuroscientists behind the new study used VR simulations of bizarre situations to complement reality-check exercises.

The team, based at the University of Trento in Italy, recruited university students and asked them to meditate and then perform the VR training. The meditation was intended to increase students' awareness of what they were thinking about in a given moment. Each time they encountered bizarre happenings in the VR environment, such as objects or people violating laws of physics or rapid switches from one scene to another, they performed reality checks.

After the training, participants went home and were asked to keep a dream diary that they wrote in every morning. They also filled out daily questionnaires, citing the number of dreams they recalled and how many they remembered being lucid.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

The participants experienced lucid dreams four times more often than participants did in a second group that did reality checks without performing any meditation or VR training. The study also included another comparison group, in which participants carried out reality checks during realistic rather than dream-like VR simulations; these participants were over eight times less likely to report lucid dreams. This latter comparison ensured that the results were not caused solely by the use of VR, the researchers said.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: It was particularly surprising to find that such little training with the dream-like VR simulations was needed to develop lucid dreaming as a skill, said study co-author Nicola De Pisapia, a neuroscientist at the University of Trento. His team ran the experiment for only a month because any longer would have been too demanding for the participants, De Pisapia noted.

Study co-author Andrea Signorelli, a doctoral student in De Pisapia's lab, thinks the VR intervention is at the heart of why the approach worked. People often don't realize that they're dreaming because the dreams "fool" your senses and feel realistic in the moment, he explained.

"Virtual reality is the technology to fool you on stereoscopic vision and auditory information," he said. The term "stereoscopic" refers to techniques that create 3D illusions from 2D images by mimicking how human eyes see.
"It's basically the most immersive technology that we have at the moment," making it a good intervention for reality check exercises, Signorelli said.

The team also compared the number of lucid dreams participants reported against their total number of recalled dreams, which revealed an interesting pattern. On average, participants in each group recalled more dreams after starting the experiment than they did beforehand. However, the dream-simulating VR group recalled the fewest dreams overall after entering the experiment, even though they had the highest number of lucid dreams.

Signorelli speculated that perhaps it takes a lot of energy to have lucid dreams, which could divert resources away from recalling other dreams. Morris argued that, alternatively, participants in the lucid-dream VR group "may have been less motivated to report non-lucid dreams than the control groups." So there may have been some bias in the reporting.

The study had some limitations, such as its small sample size of 38 participants. Plus, neither of the two control groups were asked to meditate, so it is impossible to say whether the meditations or the dreamlike VR sessions had more influence over lucid dreaming in the test group.
The team is now doing a follow-up study in which the meditation part has been removed, Signorelli said, to reveal whether the VR dream scenarios are the critical factor, as suspected.

Signorelli said that he would like to see lucid-dream training tailored for each individual. For example, the VR simulations could be personalized to simulate a recurrent nightmare that a given person experiences, training them to recognize triggers specific to that dream, he said.
"Other future research could explore the potential therapeutic benefits of this intervention for people with nightmares, anxiety, or PTSD [post-traumatic stress disorder]," Morris suggested.

Kamal Nahas is a freelance contributor based in Oxford, U.K. His work has appeared in New Scientist, Science and The Scientist, among other outlets, and he mainly covers research on evolution, health and technology. He holds a PhD in pathology from the University of Cambridge and a master's degree in immunology from the University of Oxford. He currently works as a microscopist at the Diamond Light Source, the U.K.'s synchrotron. When he's not writing, you can find him hunting for fossils on the Jurassic Coast.

articles.title: Crows Can Make Decisions Based on Visual Information at Lightning Speed—Roughly Twice as Fast as Humans Can, Study Suggests

paras.en: Crows are famously intelligent animals; they use tools, host funerals and remember people’s faces. Past research hints they can even count to four and understand basic geometry.

Now, a new study suggests the jet-black birds can make decisions based on visual information incredibly fast—possibly at twice the speed of humans. The findings, described in the journal Science on October 22, can provide insights into crows’ evolutionary history.
Crow brains certainly move “in the fast lane,” study co-author Andreas Nieder, an animal physiologist at the University of Tübingen in Germany, tells the Transmitter’s Sarah Thau.

In the study, Nieder and Philipp Schmidbauer, a neuroscientist also at the University of Tübingen, worked with two carrion crows named Iggy and Lemmy. Each would sit in front of a touchscreen showing a cluster of dots in the center. Some dots started moving in one direction—either left or right—while the others shifted randomly as distractors. When the movement began, the birds tapped the left or right side of the screen as fast as possible to indicate which way the associated dots were traveling. Getting the answer right earned them a tasty treat: a mealworm, Pien Huang reports for NPR’s “All Things Considered.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The birds performed the task thousands of times. In some trials, nearly all the dots moved in concert. Other times, just a tiny fraction did, making it tough for the birds to choose the correct side.

The crows took an average of 235 milliseconds to indicate their correct decision, which is about a fifth of a second. That’s roughly twice as fast as monkeys and humans can do similar tasks without sacrificing accuracy, according to past research.

What’s more, “even when the patterns of motion were hard to recognize, the crows’ decisions were still better than random choices,” Schmidbauer says in a statement. “And with clear signals, they achieved an accuracy of nearly 100 percent.”

As the crows made their lightning-speed decisions, the Nieder and Schmidbauer also recorded activity in the animals’ brains. They specifically monitored nerve cell, or neuronal, activity in the nidopallium caudolaterale, a region similar to the primate prefrontal cortex, which is important for higher-order thinking and decision-making.

The team found that neurons in the birds’ brain area were firing signals as soon as 70 milliseconds after the crows viewed the visual stimulus. Neuronal activity increased as a crow’s decision took shape, until reaching a “decision threshold,” after which the animal tapped the screen to indicate its choice. Past research suggests that primates’ brains follow the same pattern, hinting that the two distinct types of animals rely on a similar neuronal process.
“The bigger implication is that a brain does not need a mammalian neocortex to perform sophisticated computations,” Nieder tells Live Science’s Kenna Hughes-Castleberry.

Neuroscientist Mike Colombo, of the University of Otago in New Zealand, agrees. The findings show “it’s not about the architecture; it’s the circuitry that matters, and [crows and primates] the same circuitry,” says Colombo, who wasn’t involved in the study, to NPR.

So why is the same neuronal circuitry making crows faster? It might have something to do with the demands of a bird’s lifestyle. Their vision is essential for the navigational complexities of flight, rapid beak movement and predator detection, for example. In other words, avians may have been forced to evolve rapid visual processing and motor responses.

Still, researchers don’t know how widespread this speedy trait might be among birds, says Aaron Blaisdell, a neuroscientist at the University of California, Los Angeles who also did not participate in the study, to the Transmitter. Is it “something that’s avian versus mammal, or is it something about crows specifically?”

articles.title: Three in Four Former NFL Players Who Died From 2008 Through 2023 May Have Had CTE, a Brain Disease Caused by Repeated Head Injuries

paras.en: American football is famously a dangerous sport. In August, a study found that at least one in four recently deceased former NFL players had a brain disease called chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE, forcing a conversation around safety in the sport.

The actual image might be even starker. New work by some of the same researchers suggests that three in four of the retired professional athletes who died from 2008 through 2023 likely had CTE. The findings were published in the journal JAMA Network Open on October 28.

“More than 20 million men alive today in the U.S. have played football, so understanding how many of them have CTE is an important public health question,” says study co-author Yorghos Tripodis, a biostatistician at Boston University, to Youri Benadjaoud and Betsy-Ann Assoumou at ABC News.

CTE is a progressive brain disease likely caused by repeated head injuries. Symptoms are thought to include mood swings, memory loss, depression and dementia, but CTE can only be diagnosed after death. That’s because one definitive sign is the buildup of the protein tau, also implicated in Alzheimer’s disease, which causes the brain to atrophy. The autopsy-dependent diagnosis has long skewed CTE research, given that families are more likely to donate brains of former athletes who showed symptoms of the disease.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Tripodis and colleagues tried to adjust for selection bias. They analyzed the medical records of 2,362 former NFL players—in the league for an average of five years—who died between January 2008 and December 2023. Most of them were not brain donors. But by looking for documentation of dementia or other cognitive issues, the scientists found that those showing potential behavioral signs of CTE were around five times more likely to have their brains donated for research.

Then, the researchers found that out of 387 brain donors, nearly 94 percent had CTE. Adjusting that percentage for the donation bias yielded the estimate that 74.5 percent of former NFL players in the cohort died with CTE. For comparison, less than 1 percent of brains from members of the general population in research banks show signs of CTE, Tripodis tells Jackie Flynn Mogensen at Scientific American.
What’s more, roughly one in four ex-football players had dementia, the team calculates, a figure that is likely an underestimate.

Zachary Binney, an epidemiologist at Emory University who wasn’t involved in the study, tells Carolyn Y. Johnson and John Branch at the New York Times that the research was “pretty rigorous, and the methods seem reasonable and valid.”
“It is higher than I would have guessed previously,” he adds. “But this paper has a larger data set and applies stronger methods than previous work.”

When asked about the findings, the NFL pointed to its response to the August study, report Diana Anos and Nadia Kounang at CNN. “The NFL continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts,” the organization said.

Julie Stamm, a neuroscientist at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, tells CNN that the NFL could do more to protect players, such as banning tackles during practice. “If the NFL says that, the youth levels, the younger levels, they’ll listen, and that will go a long way in decreasing the overall number of impacts over a lifetime that these individuals sustain, which is what we’ve seen increases the risk for CTE,” says Stamm, who wasn’t involved in the study.

Still, studying CTE remains difficult. Researchers can’t know how many living football players are walking around with the undiagnosed brain disease. But Tripodis hopes the latest study will increase investment in its research, as well as inform families and players about the risks involved in football.

“CTE is a preventable disease. We find, in study after study, that the more blows to the head over your lifetime, the higher the risk of CTE,” Tripodis tells Scientific American. “If you reduce exposure to repetitive head impacts, then you reduce the risk of CTE.”

articles.title: Where Is England's Oldest Pub? An Archaeologist Drilled Into 600-Year-Old Timbers to Answer the Contentious Question

paras.en: Across England, dozens of historic taverns claim to have poured pints longer than any of their competitors. Yet according to a recent forensic investigation, nearly all those ancient founding dates are myths brewed by shrewd landlords rather than historical reality.

The findings follow a comprehensive architectural survey by James Wright, a buildings archaeologist working with Historic England. By analyzing surviving medieval timbers and cross-referencing historic documents, Wright tested the validity of more than two dozen establishments that claim the mantle of England’s oldest pub.
“Not one of the claimants to be the oldest pub (and there are over two dozen of them) are even vaguely close to being so in reality,” Wright tells the Guardian’s Helena Horton.

To separate legend from architectural fact, Wright relied on dendrochronology, the science of dating through the growth rings of wooden timbers. He believes he has identified the true titleholder of England’s earliest surviving purpose-built inn: the George Inn in Norton St. Philip, Somerset.
“The architectural history of the George Inn’s stone and timber suggests that this building has been in continuous service for over 600 years,” he tells the Guardian.

“Because we know medieval carpenters didn’t muck around at all, that they would fell the timber when it was green and they would build almost immediately afterwards, the actual date of felling gives us the near-date of construction,” Wright explains in a video for Historic England. “We’re not guessing at its age … Now that’s the difference between a local legend and a national treasure.”
Charo Havermans, a pub historian, echoes the importance of this method. “The strongest claims are when the history meets the science,” she tells the BBC’s Chris Lockyer and Pippa Rifka.

The analysis determined that the George Inn’s lower stone walls were constructed in the late 14th century by Carthusian monks from the nearby Hinton Priory. The monks expanded the inn during the early 15th century, adding an imposing timber-framed facade and roof framed with oak cut down between 1430 and 1432.

During the Middle Ages, inns differed from everyday alehouses, which sold ale, and taverns, which served wine, per the Telegraph. Purpose-built inns were substantial commercial hubs designed to provide beds, food and stables for traveling merchants.

The George Inn served as a central storehouse for the priory’s wool trade and hosted merchants attending regional wool fairs, generating vital lodging fees, storage dues and sales tolls for the monks.
- In 1668, diarist Samuel Pepys stayed overnight at the George Inn, noting that it was already “a very old house.”
- In 1685, the Duke of Monmouth, the illegitimate son of Charles II, commandeered the inn as his headquarters during his ill-fated rebellion.
- Following Monmouth’s defeat, the inn’s dining hall served as a courtroom for George Jeffreys, the infamous “Hanging Judge,” who sentenced local rebels during the Bloody Assizes.

In crowning the George Inn, Wright debunked several famous long-standing contenders. Ye Olde Fighting Cocks in St. Albans, Hertfordshire, has frequently claimed an origin year of 793. However, archival research reveals that the octagonal timber structure was originally built as a monastic dovecote around 1400 and was not licensed as an alehouse until roughly 1807; its early medieval date appeared on a 20th-century tourist postcard.
Similarly, the Bingley Arms near Leeds claims a founding date of 953 and an entry in the Domesday Book of 1086. Yet its structure dates to the 18th century.
“There are no pubs mentioned—at all—in the Domesday Book, so any pub claiming to be in it is having you on,” Wright tells the Guardian.
Even Nottingham’s Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem, which advertises an 1189 crusade-era pedigree, only first appears in licensing records (under the name “the Pilgrim”) in 1751.

Pinpointing the definitive champion has proven so fraught that Guinness Book of World Records retired its entry for England’s oldest pub in 2000, conceding that tracking unbroken historical hospitality across centuries had become impossible to adjudicate, per the BBC.

Nevertheless, for surviving buildings specifically constructed as inns that have continuously served travelers, Wright found that only about a dozen medieval structures survive across England. Alongside early rivals like the King’s Head in Shrewsbury and the New Inn in Gloucester, the George Inn stands alone at the front of the line, its 600-year-old timbers anchoring it firmly as a living artifact of English history.

articles.title: I Spent 30 Minutes With Apple’s CEO. Now I Know Why John Ternus Got the Job
articles.author: Steven Levy

paras.en: The brief ceremony introducing the new Macbook Pro this week was as low-key as the presenter, Apple’s new CEO John Ternus. He stepped onto the low stage at a Los Angeles event space with zero fanfare, said hi, and queued up a video showing the first touchscreen Mac. Then he released the modest crowd of journalists and creators to get hands-on with the new laptop and roam between eye-popping demos of music producers, filmmakers, photographers, and fashion designers using the laptop. Ternus, who at 51 is on the younger side of Apple’s top management, has been CEO for less than two months. But this launch and a series of other recent announcements have made one thing clear. With this new guy—if a 25-year Apple veteran could be considered new—it’s all about the products. Perhaps fittingly, the biggest noise of the presentation came when Ternus revealed that the new device restores the illumination to the Apple logo. Maybe that’s a symbol that in the age of AI, Apple is beaming out the message that hardware still rules.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: A few minutes after the presentation, I sat down with Ternus, for the second time in two days. Steve Jobs used to grant me an audience after his famous keynotes, too. Ternus isn’t Jobs, of course, nor is he supposed to be. But who is he?

I first met Ternus in 2015, when I spent a day with him at Apple’s Input Design Lab, a testing facility in Cupertino. He’d risen to VP for Mac, iPad, Ecosystem, and Audio Engineering, and he struck me as affable and knowledgeable. (He spent four years right out of college at a virtual reality company, but he’s been at Apple ever since.) The peg to my story at the time was how this unknown manager conducted a Javert-like investigation to fix the weird sound a redesigned mouse made when sliding on a table.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: That attention to detail was a legacy of Jobs’ perfectionism, which Tim Cook sustained as the next CEO. In the decade when Ternus overlapped with Jobs, he says he had only “a handful of interactions” with the founder. “But I've always felt like sort of a student of Steve's teachings,” Ternus said. “And then being able to work very closely with Tim, I’ve been very lucky.”

Ternus has so far been defined by his product prowess. “John innately has a great sense for great products, and that’s what Apple is,” says Greg Joswiak, Apple’s SVP of worldwide marketing and a 40-year company veteran. “You can’t teach that.” In one sense Ternus’ ascension is similar to that of Microsoft’s Satya Nadella, another lifer promoted to the top post. But Nadella was called upon to fix a broken organization, while Apple has been on a multi-decade run. Ternus is explicit that he will be an engine of continuity. That word is key to his selection, and above all explains why Tim Cook and the rest of Apple’s board was so comfortable with the choice.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The extent to which Ternus is a deep Apple insider became clear when I probed him on his views on being a corporate leader. I asked him which non-Apple CEOs he admires, and he was stumped. “I haven't really thought about that,” he said. I asked whether any business books had an impact on him. “Not really,” he said. “Of course I’ve read books, but there's so much to be learned from the people I get to work with.” Indeed, every time I tried to pin down Ternus on what mark he wants to make at Apple, he deflected the question and told me how he will continue Apple’s commitment to internal collaboration.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Ternus’ key collaborator is probably Johny Srouji, the architect of the company’s custom silicon, an initiative that’s driven many of the company’s innovations in the past decade. Srouri says that their relationship will be even closer, as Apple has merged its hardware engineering and technology organizations with Srouji at the top, reporting to Ternus. “John is going to be a great CEO,” he said. “He's a product guy at heart, but Apple's secret weapon is the DNA, the culture, which is not going to change. Remember, John has been here for 25 years. It’s not like he's going to come and everything's going to be different.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Being Apple’s CEO encompasses much more than products—there’s a $100 billion business in services, a huge infrastructure, and the general mishegoss of running a giant corporation. I asked Ternus what it’s like to take on a massively expanded portfolio. “One of the amazing privileges of this job is getting to learn so many new things,” he said. “I have been and will continue to learn and go deeper into different areas. But, you know, I do love product. I'm super passionate about it.”

Like it or not, the CEO of a $4 trillion company has to be involved in policy and politics. It has been widely reported that as executive chair, Cook will still conduct some of Apple’s high-level policy duties, including the equivalent of stuffing gold-plated binkies in the presidential mouth. Ternus implies that the reality is more nuanced. “Tim is available to help wherever I ask him, and it's great to have him in that role,” he said. “He obviously has a ton of relationships he's developed over the years, and of course, I'm building new relationships in this role as well.” One relationship he has yet to build: the president. Ternus has yet to meet Donald Trump.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Then there’s the one thing that could possibly disrupt the way Apple has run its business for the past 50 years. Ternus is taking over the company during what may be the biggest technological shift ever. I suggested to Ternus that history may judge him on how he handles AI. I spelled out for him a couple of narratives people spin about Apple. One is that Apple has been hobbled by a failure to develop its AI product Siri, and even after an update it’s still in catch-up mode. The other is that Apple is smart to avoid the high cost of developing a frontier model and that the strategy of organically putting AI into its products, with a focus on privacy, will pay off in the long run.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “Everyone has an opinion—I really like where we’re at,” he said. “I would hope people recognize that the work we do is building incredible products that make their lives better. We’re absolutely going to leverage AI to do that. We don't want to ship AI for AI's sake. When we're doing it right, people won’t have to think about whether it was AI that made this happen or more traditional software. What matters is, did we build something that they really love?”

That assumes that AI, as powerful as it is, will wind up as a “normal” technology, organically integrated into our current gadget-sphere. Another school of thought is that AI is an apocalyptic disruptor that will shred the current ecosystem. In that vision, all those cool apps Apple supports will be subsumed by AI-concocted agents generated from prompts, or even autonomously. Ternus doesn’t buy that scenario. “That could make life really easy, I suppose, but the creation of products is a deeply human and personal thing, something that we love to do,” he said.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: When I asked whether he’s in favor of AI regulation, he replied, “We all read the stories and think about it from a cybersecurity standpoint—clearly these models are very capable of doing things. Our focus is on making sure that our products are secure and safe, and protecting the users' information.”

His non-answer shows that he might well be on the way to mastering political communication. But policy will never be the focus of John Ternus. He is, and probably always will be, the product-guy CEO. Before we ended our conversation, Ternus had one question for me: “What did you think of the logo?”

articles.title: People Are Creating ‘Survival Guides’ to Cope With the ‘AO3 Apocalypse’
articles.author: Ej Dickson

paras.en: In a major blow to both the terminally online and the criminally horny, the fan fiction website Archive of Our Own (AO3) has temporarily shut down due to a “security incident,” according to an update posted on the site.

On October 29, an admin for AO3 posted that the website was “down for maintenance.” The statement said that it could take up to four weeks for service to be fully restored, though it was possible the site would be back up in a “degraded state” sooner, with some of its features disabled.

Though the original statement did not specify the reasons for the closure, subsequent updates said that a “security incident” had taken place, though “we are still in the early stages of response [and] determining its scope.” While the statement said that AO3 did not believe that its user database had been stolen, it urged users to exercise caution and change their passwords for the site.

Run by the Organization for Transformative Works, a nonprofit dedicated to preserving fandom communities on the internet, AO3 was founded in 2007 in part due to concerns about censorship and corporate interests overtaking fandom spaces. The website has 11 million users, according to a 2026 press release, and hosts more than 18 million original works. The explosive popularity of the gay hockey romance Heated Rivalry TV series generated a surge of new interest last year, resulting in the publication of tens of thousands of stories featuring the show’s main characters, Shane Hollander and Ilya Rozanov, on the platform.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Those reliant on AO3 for their daily dose of Destiel- or Dramione-inspired smut are not taking the news well. “No ao3 for possibly 4 weeks SOMEONE DO SOMETHING,” one Heated Rivalry fan account posted on X, tagging not just AO3 itself but also the official X accounts for the FBI, the CIA, and, for some reason, Uber Support. Other fans are compiling Google Docs of links to downloaded stories, touting them as “survival guides” for the “AO3 apocalypse” and organizing them by fictional character pairings, or ships. (Be warned, however: One such doc is difficult to load due to “heavy traffic” on the file.)
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Others commented on the timing of the outage, pointing out that it coincides with “No Nut November,” the internet-based challenge that encourages people to abstain from masturbation throughout the month. “AO3 taking no nut november a little too seriously,” one person wrote.

A representative for the Organization for Transformative Works did not immediately respond to a request for comment. But the chaos inspired by the site’s shutdown underscores the prominence of fan fiction in everyday lives, driving mainstream publishing trends and generating hundreds of millions of views. It also serves as the engine for the burgeoning vertical video industry, with streaming platforms constantly scouring fan fiction websites for works to adapt.
“All life forms dependent on AO3 are literally withering right now,” one fan wrote. “This is our 9/11.”

articles.title: $1M Powerball ticket spent two months in oblivious winner's wallet

paras.en: Oct. 30 (UPI) -- A Michigan man said he was carrying a Powerball ticket around in his wallet for nearly two months before he discovered it was a $1 million winner.

Wyoming resident Michael Vander Lugt, 54, told Michigan Lottery officials he bought a ticket for the Aug. 8 Powerball drawing from Big Top Market in Wyoming and tucked it away in his wallet with his other lottery tickets.
He said the ticket remained in his wallet for nearly two months without being checked.

"I recently stopped at the party store to get a pop but realized when checking out that I didn't have enough cash on me," Vander Lugt said. "Rather than use my card, I handed the cashier a few Powerball tickets from my wallet that I knew I had won at least a few bucks on."
The clerk had a surprise in store for the player.

"She scanned each of the tickets and said one came back with a message to file a claim at the lottery office, so I looked up the winning numbers for that drawing when I got in my car. I recognized the numbers as soon as I saw them and started freaking out! I can't believe I had this ticket in my wallet for nearly two months not knowing it was worth $1 million," Vander Lugt said.
His ticket had matched the five white balls from the drawing: 05-09-35-54-63.
Vander Lugt said his prize money will go toward paying off his mortgage and investing.

articles.title: Miami Heat unveil revamped Dwyane Wade statue

paras.en: MIAMI, Oct. 30 (UPI) -- The Miami Heat unveiled a revamped Dwyane Wade statue Friday in front of the Kaseya Center in Miami.

Wade's initial statue was unveiled in 2024. The work immortalized one of Wade's most memorable performances, when he hit a game-winning buzzer-beater in a win over the Chicago Bulls, jumped on top of a court-side table and screamed "This is my house" in 2009 in Miami.
But the face on the 8-foot bronze statue drew widespread criticism because it bore little resemblance to the 2023 Hall of Fame inductee, who won three titles with the NBA franchise.
"I heard the jokes," Wade wrote on his Substack page. "I saw the memes. I read the reactions. Everybody had an opinion about whether it actually looked like me."
Wade worked with the original artists for a year to plan for the remodeled work, which includes a redesigned head.
"So, eventually, I had to ask myself a pretty simple question: If people don't feel that connection when they look at the face, why wouldn't we try to make it better?" he wrote.
"So, we listened and had honest conversations with everyone involved, and we all agreed to make adjustments to the head."

Wade, 44, spent parts of 15 seasons with the Heat. The No. 5 overall pick by the Heat in the 2003 NBA Draft is the franchise leader in many statistical categories, including games played, points, assists and steals.
"I hope when people see it now, they see a better likeness of me," Wade wrote. "But more than that, I hope they see themselves. Because it may be my likeness, but it will always be our house."

articles.title: Watch: Swiss researchers unveil robot hand that walks on its fingers

paras.en: Oct. 30 (UPI) -- A team of researchers in Switzerland released details of a project perfect for the spooky season: a disembodied robot hand that uses its fingers to walk.
The team from ETH Zurich's Soft Robotics Lab released videos and a pre-print paper detailing their work on the robotic hand, which they compared to Thing, the autonomous hand from The Addams Family.
Amirhossein Kazemipour, a doctoral candidate at the Soft Robotics Lab, said the robot hand's ability to walk unaided makes it unique.

"Getting a robotic hand to walk is actually pretty challenging," he said in a video released by the school. "You know, it's fingers aren't all the same, so it has to learn how to coordinate all of them while remaining balanced."

Kazemipour explained the team used machine learning to teach the robot to walk. Instead of programming it with every possible movement individually, they had the robot practice walking in a computer simulation to learn which movements help it to best achieve its goals.

"The bigger question isn't 'How can we make a hand walk,' it's 'How can we make robots more adaptable so that they can find new ways to use their bodies and interact with the world?'" Kazemipour said.
The research team also shared a video showing the hand's ability to walk on different surfaces, get itself up after falling over, push objects and even use a computer keyboard.

"It might look a bit spooky, but I think there is actually a pretty meaningful lesson from this. We can have robots made for different purposes," said Robert Katzschmann, an assistant professor at ETH Zurich. "A big robot can go into one space, a small hand can do into a completely different space -- maybe a much more confined, disaster space."

articles.title: NFL to Face New Trial Over ‘Sunday Ticket’ $4.7 Billion Verdict
articles.author: Winston Cho

paras.en: The decision from the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Friday reverses a federal judge who had tossed a $4.7 billion award for consumers. A jury’s “verdict must stand unless it is clearly not supported by the evidence,” the court wrote.

The long running legal battle centers on allegations that the league and its 32 teams conspired in violation of antitrust laws to allow the NFL to reach exclusive deals with broadcast partners for the right to air out-of-market games.

After a jury sided with consumers in a 2024 trial, the court granted the NFL’s bid to throw out the verdict. U.S. District Judge Philip Gutierrez found that some of the testimony from experts who testified should’ve been excluded.
In Friday’s decision, the federal appeals court concluded that Gutierrez overstepped in her role as a gatekeeper of expert testimony.
