“Opinions are neither unfounded nor unreliable merely because they are impeachable,” the three-judge panel wrote. “Such opinions are for the jury to weigh at trial.”
Gutierrez’s reasoning to overturn the jury’s verdict was grounded in testimony from Daniel Rascher.

Rascher used college football as a comparison for what would happen in the absence of the broadcasting restraints at issue in the case. Without the NFL’s exclusive arrangements, he testified that individual teams and conferences could sell their out-of-market game rights separately, as colleges do.
Gutierrez ultimately found that Rascher’s work was too speculative.

The appeals court, however, said that the lower court abused its discretion by excluding Rascher’s findings. “Reasonable jurors may debate whether college and professional football telecasts are sufficiently similar or how out-of-market NFL games would have become available in the absence of the NFL’s anticompetitive conduct,” the court wrote. “But those questions are for the jury to decide. Dr. Rascher’s testimony was admissible.”
The case now goes back to district court. The $4.7 billion verdict can’t stand because the jury’s finding on damages wasn’t based on a proper consideration of the evidence, the appeals court ruled.

In a statement, the NFL said it’s considering its options on appeal. It added, “We continue to believe that our media distribution strategy – which features 100 percent of NFL games broadcast on free over-the-air television in the markets of the participating teams and national distribution of our most popular games, supplemented by many additional choices including RedZone, Sunday Ticket and NFL Plus – is by far the most fan-friendly distribution model in all of sports and entertainment.”

articles.title: Before ‘Star Trek,’ Patrick Stewart Proved His Sci-Fi Chops in ‘Dune’
articles.author: Julian Sancton

paras.en: Before there was Jean-Luc Picard, there was Gurney Halleck. Several years before Star Trek: The Next Generation sent his career into the cosmos, Sir Patrick Stewart played Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides in David Lynch’s Dune in 1984. Stewart, who died this week at age 86, was then a seasoned stage veteran in his native England, but Dune was merely his third film. It was also his introduction to science fiction, a precursor to his career-defining role as Picard. He imbued his character with the kind of presence and dignity that only classical stagecraft can summon — much as his English forebear Alec Guinness had in Star Wars.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In his new memoir, Fictional Selves (recently excerpted in The Hollywood Reporter) actor Kyle Maclachlan, recalled the surreal, formative experience of shooting Dune in the Mexican desert alongside Stewart.

“The first thing I noticed when I met Patrick was his voice,” writes MacLachlan, who was 24 at the time and, like Stewart, new to film. “I went to school for three years to learn how to speak onstage, but I’ll never sound like him. Coming from the prestigious Royal Shakespeare Company, Patrick has the most mellifluous tones, regal and elegant. No one can make the line ‘Behold, as a wild ass in the desert go I forth to my work’ sound correct except for him. He is Gurney Halleck, master swordsman and troubadour. And because he’s also Patrick Stewart, he’s suave and debonair about it. When he puts on the Atreides battle jacket or the Fremen stillsuit, it’s like he’s lived in it all his life. He also has the most marvelously shaped head of any human I’ve ever seen, and I tell him so. He gives me a ‘thank you, I think’ kind of look.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: A longtime fan of Frank Herbert’s Dune franchise, MacLachlan writes that he knew more about the works than most of the people involved in the film, including Lynch. As such, he became something of an authority on the subject matter. Stewart came to rely on MacLachlan’s expertise in order to get deeper into his character.

“Patrick is a mix of stately confidence and thoughtful inquiry. He regularly leans over and, sotto voce, asks me questions about what’s going on,” writes MacLachlan. “Though he presents a very cool and collected mien, he is just trying to figure shit out like me. We connect on our theater background — I did Shakespeare the previous summer — and laugh at the exponential difference between simple theater productions and … whatever this is. The size and scope of the film often leave us speechless, and I feel less alone with him beside me.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The following passage from Maclachlan’s memoir well illustrates Stewart’s refusal to treat popular entertainment with any less seriousness than Shakespeare, a trait that would serve him well throughout his career.

On his first day of shooting, he and I took our seats in a half-built “ornithopter,” which is like a giant, multifaceted bee that flies over the desert. We were seated in front of a gigantic blue screen, where the landscape would be matted in later. I could feel Patrick’s nervousness as we prepared to “fly” over the shield wall and the Great Desert of Arrakis. He leaned forward and quietly asked, ‘Kyle, what are we looking at here?’
I leaned back and spoke in an undertone: “There’s a sandworm down there bigger than a tractor trailer.”
“Aha. And there?” he asked, pointing lower down. “It’s swallowing one of the harvesters.”
“It’s like a large metal factory on wheels.”
“Seems like a risky mission,” he said, a trace of somber gravitas. “Tremendous risk,” I said quietly.
Patrick’s key line in the scene is “The worm is eight minutes away, sire.” After the first take, he had a question. “Pardon, David?”
“YES, PATRICK,” David said in his distinctive honk.
“How exactly would I know how far out the worm is?” I’m impressed that Patrick exists deeply enough within his character to ask such a thing.

David stopped, re-calculating in his mind. “EXCELLENT QUESTION, PATRICK,” he said, like a supportive teacher. “THANK YOU.” He then dispatched a propman to construct a gauge, with analog hands to be inserted later.

articles.title: Universal Studios Hollywood Workers Say They Are Still Facing Food and Housing Insecurity
articles.author: Katie Kilkenny

paras.en: Ensconced in a lush ballroom at the University of Southern California, underneath crystal chandeliers and vaulted ceilings, Diego Rodriguez was waiting for a chance to speak to Donna Langley.
paras.zh: 迭戈·罗德里格斯（ Diego Rodriguez ）坐在南加州大学（ University of Southern California ）郁郁葱葱的宴会厅里，在水晶吊灯和拱形天花板下，正在等待与唐娜·兰利（ Donna Langley ）交谈的机会。

paras.en: Langley, the NBCUniversal Entertainment chairman and arguably the most powerful woman in Hollywood, was the keynote speaker of the university law school’s annual entertainment law conference. Her captive audience was a mix of undergrads and “rich Beverly Hills lawyers,” describes Rodriguez, who is himself a cook at the Universal Studios Hollywood theme park, where he works in the kitchens behind unholy IP-park food combinations like “Marge Hair Cotton Candy” for the Simpsons-themed hot dog stand and “Boss Baby Beignets” for a DreamWorks-centered café.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Langley, fresh off of the successes of The Odyssey and Obsession for her division, had reason to be running a victory lap, but it wasn’t about to go as planned. Her conversation with industry lawyer Bruce Ramer appeared to be nearing its end when Rodriguez grabbed an extra mic he saw in the room. It wasn’t on, so he and his companion, a staffer for his union at the park, began raising their voices. Langley stepped down from the platform where she was talking and pulled the protestors aside.
paras.zh: 兰利刚刚从《奥德赛》和《痴迷》的成功中脱颖而出，她有理由跑一圈胜利，但它不会按计划进行。当罗德里格斯抓起他在房间里看到的额外麦克风时，她与行业律师布鲁斯·拉默（ Bruce Ramer ）的谈话似乎接近尾声。它没有打开，所以他和他的同伴，他在公园的工会的工作人员，开始提高他们的声音。兰利从讲话的平台上走下来，把抗议者拉到一边。

paras.en: Amid the fracas, “I told her, ‘Hey, my name is Diego Rodriguez. I’m currently one of your workers at Universal,’” Rodriguez says. At the time he lived with family in Fresno, as he says he couldn’t afford to live closer, and at times slept in his car or in the park between shifts — and he told her as much. “‘I think it’s unfair that I’m currently living in this situation and you’re over here talking about all these profits, all these margins, and you don’t even want to help your own employees.’”
paras.zh: 在争吵声中， “我告诉她， ‘嘿，我叫迭戈·罗德里格斯。我目前是环球影业的员工之一，” Rodriguez说。当时他和家人住在弗雷斯诺，因为他说他负担不起更近的生活，有时候轮班之间睡在他的车里或公园里—他告诉她这么多。“我认为，我目前生活在这种情况下，你在这里谈论所有这些利润，所有这些利润率，你甚至不想帮助自己的员工，这是不公平的。”

paras.en: Langley told them that theme parks didn’t fall under her corporate purview and she couldn’t help, per Rodriguez and the union staffer who attended the event. A Universal source who was there, meanwhile, says Langley “compassionately” told the two that she would make sure the right people were aware. Universal Destinations & Experiences chairman and CEO Mark Woodbury manages the parks.
paras.zh: 据罗德里格斯和一位出席活动的工会工作人员称，兰利告诉他们，主题公园不属于她的公司管辖范围，她无法提供帮助。与此同时，一位在场的环球影城内部人士表示，兰利“体贴地”告诉两人，她会确保相关人员知晓此事。环球目的地及体验公司董事长兼首席执行官马克·伍德伯里负责管理这些主题公园。

paras.en: But after watching her “expressing all these profits” in the keynote, Rodriguez wasn’t satisfied. “For a person that gave my blood and sweat to the company, I feel like even though she says she has nothing to do and say, she represents the company, what’s that all about?” he asks. (A version of this exchange was previously reported in Puck.)
paras.zh: 但在主题演讲中看到她“表达了所有这些利润”之后，罗德里格斯并不满意。他问道： “对于一个为我的公司付出鲜血和汗水的人来说，我觉得即使她说她无事可做，她代表公司，这是怎么回事？” （之前在Puck中报告过此交易所的版本。）

paras.en: As event staff tried to get them to leave, Rodriguez and the staffer protested being touched and eventually returned to union colleagues who were passing out leaflets outside stating Universal workers were going hungry.
paras.zh: 当活动工作人员试图让他们离开时，罗德里格斯和工作人员抗议被触摸，并最终回到工会同事那里，他们在外面分发传单，说环球员工正在挨饿。

paras.en: As this highly unusual interruption of a posh entertainment law function revealed, tensions between Universal Studios Hollywood food-service workers and management have been spilling over amid contract negotiations that have stretched on for about a year, as the two sides remain deep in talks. During a period of skyrocketing prices in the U.S., Unite Here Local 11, representing some 1,700 food cart, bakery, restaurant and warehouse workers at the park, is negotiating for higher wages and changes to scheduling practices. When talks were floundering in the past month, the union circulated the sobering results of an internal survey that offers a window into the experience of its workers over the last few years. According to that report, union members are facing food and housing insecurity while their working hours are being cut, exacerbating the problem.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The union conducted the survey itself, using a methodology that was not shared with THR. Naturally, the study — released amid a tense contract negotiation — was designed to build pressure on management to engage seriously with the union’s demands.
paras.zh: 工会使用未与THR共享的方法自行进行了调查。当然，这项研究是在紧张的合同谈判中发布的，旨在向管理层施加压力，要求他们认真对待工会的要求。

paras.en: But that workers making and selling the park’s Butterbeer Ice Cream and Toadstool Cheesy Garlic Knots are reporting skipping meals, unfortunately, isn’t a new finding. Two years ago, during contract negotiations involving two park unions, including Unite Here Local 11, The Hollywood Reporter reported on widespread poverty amongst these park workers. According to the union and some of its members who spoke again with THR, not much has changed — even as they hope that a new deal could help that situation. “Honestly, I don’t want to worry about what do I got to eat next? Where do I got to live next?” says Rodriguez.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In a statement in response to these claims, a Universal spokesperson says, “Universal Studios Hollywood has a long history of working collaboratively with our labor partners to reach comprehensive wage and benefits agreements, including most recently with IATSE Local B-192, which represents more than 4,000 employees in similar guest service positions as Unite HERE Local 11.”
paras.zh: 环球影城的一位发言人在回应这些说法时表示： “好莱坞环球影城长期以来一直与我们的劳工合作伙伴合作，以达成全面的工资和福利协议，包括最近与IATSE Local B-192达成的协议，后者代表了4,000多名与Unite HERE Local 11类似的客户服务职位的员工。”

paras.en: The spokesperson continues, “Our proposals to UNITE HERE Local 11 reflect this longstanding commitment, and build on the significant wage increases secured in their 2023 agreement. We remain fully engaged in the collective bargaining process and continue to make ourselves available to meet, negotiate, and work in good faith towards an agreement for our valued team members.”
paras.zh: 发言人继续说道： “我们将Local 11团结在这里的提议反映了这一长期承诺，并在其2023年协议中获得的大幅工资增长的基础上再接再厉。我们仍然充分参与集体谈判过程，并继续本着诚意与我们尊贵的团队成员会面、谈判和工作，以达成协议。”

paras.en: The union’s survey finds food insecurity is rampant among the park’s food-service workers. A little over 60 percent of the 828 union members who responded said they had to choose between paying for food, medications or housing over the last year. Nearly 53 percent reported choosing not to eat at times when they were hungry because they felt they couldn’t spend the money. And more than a quarter, nearly 26 percent, said they received food assistance of some kind, whether from SNAP, WIC, food banks or other services.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Chris Lillian, 40, a food stand attendant and seven-year veteran of the park, knows this struggle well. This year Lillian claims his quality of life has plummeted, which he attributes to inflation as well as a theme that arose among all the Universal workers THR spoke with — the park reducing his hours. Last year, he says he was working around 40 hours a week on average, whereas this year the average is roughly 32 hours a week on his $24 an hour salary. (Currently, he’s working more during the busy Halloween season. For comparison, the minimum wage in unincorporated areas of Los Angeles County, encompassing Universal City, is currently $18.47 an hour.)
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: As a result, Lillian says he’s stretching meals and eating less, saying he’s lost 20 pounds so far this year. And he feels an immense sense of precarity, being nearly unable to pay his rent. “It disgusts me that for all the time that I’ve put in, for the hard work that I do, for the effort that I put in for the guest experience as they call it, for all of that, for me to be struggling, just on the edge, just on the edge,” he says. “I would bet money that I’m one emergency away from just ruin.”
paras.zh: 因此， Lillian说他正在拉伸膳食并减少进食，说他今年到目前为止已经减掉了20磅。他感到一种巨大的不稳定感，几乎无力支付房租。他说：「我投入的所有时间、付出的辛勤工作、为参与者体验付出的努力，让我感到恶心，因为所有这些，让我感到挣扎，只是在边缘，只是在边缘。」“我敢打赌，我离毁灭只有一次紧急情况。”

paras.en: Heather Saxxon, a food stand attendant, makes $23 an hour: “Most of the meals in the park are more than that, and that doesn’t include a drink,” she deadpans. A single mother whose daughter is living at home through college, Saxxon says she drives for Lyft and HopSkipDrive (a student transportation company) to stay afloat given that her hours have also been seemingly reduced this year. That’s despite earning the title “Team Member of the Year” for 2025.
paras.zh: 餐厅服务员希瑟·萨克森（ Heather Saxxon ）每小时挣23 $ ： “公园里的大多数餐点都不止这些，而且不包括饮料。”她面无表情地说。Saxxon是一位单身母亲，她的女儿在大学期间一直住在家里，她说她开车去Lyft和HopSkipDrive （一家学生运输公司）维持生计，因为她今年的工作时间似乎也减少了。尽管获得了2025年“年度团队成员”的称号，但情况仍然如此。

paras.en: She says she doesn’t go to the grocery store much for herself. “I get to eat basically when I’m at work and it’s only usually at Take 5 [the employee cafeteria] because I can’t afford the food in the park,” she says. (Park employees receive a $9.50 voucher for food at work, per Saxxon.) “Sometimes I’ve had to forego my medications because I’m not making enough. I’ve used up all my credit cards, I’m in so much debt, and it’s just from basic living.”
paras.zh: 她说她自己不怎么去杂货店。她说： “我基本上在工作时可以吃饭，通常只在Take 5 （员工自助餐厅）吃饭，因为我买不起公园里的食物。” （每个Saxxon员工可获得$ 9.50的工作食品代金券。） “有时我不得不放弃我的药物，因为我做得不够。我已经用完了所有的信用卡，我欠了很多债，这只是基本的生活。”

paras.en: She adds, “Everything is just getting higher, you know, but not our pay.”
paras.zh: 她补充说： “你知道，一切都变得越来越高，但不是我们的薪水。”

paras.en: Housing insecurity is another theme of Unite Here Local 11’s survey. A little more than 11 percent of workers said they had been unhoused at some point while working at Universal Studios Hollywood. But many who spoke to THR simply emphasized the struggle to pay rent.

A cook in the upper lot named Cat lives in Section 8 housing. (Cat only agreed to talk if THR did not share her last name.) With a wage of $28 an hour, she currently works a bit under 30 hours a week, but when foot traffic falls at the start of the year, her hours are typically slashed. Earlier this year, she says she didn’t have enough to cover rent and almost got evicted. “It’s been hard lately, especially with everything that’s been going up in the country,” Cat says. “So it [the wage rate] doesn’t really keep up with everything that’s going up with all the inflation.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The latest study results aren’t all that different from one conducted by the UCLA Labor Center just two years previously, which was then reported on by THR. The UCLA study — which looked at park workers represented by both Unite Here Local 11 and a separate union, IATSE B-192, which represents tour guides, ride operators, carnival barkers and clerks — found that 67 percent of workers said they didn’t earn enough for monthly food, housing and utilities expenses. Ten percent of workers hired in 2021 or before said they had experienced homelessness in the previous few years. 53 percent said they reduced the size of meals or skipped meals, and a quarter of them received food benefits.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In the last contract Unite Here Local 11 negotiated with Universal Studios Hollywood, in 2024, employees with more than one year of work under their belts won a 23 percent raise over the course of the three-year contract unless the new base wage for their role was higher. Why didn’t that make a dent? “If you’re making close to the minimum wage of $20, a 23 percent increase in the life of a contract, stacked with how bad the economy has gone in the last few years, [means you’re] not feeling 23 percent,” argues Miguel Jauregui, Unite Here Local 11’s organizing director. In addition, he adds, hourly wage increase only goes so far when working hours are being cut. (Management has not provided an explanation for this practice, according to the union, but keeps hiring new workers who must log training hours.)
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In its latest contract negotiations, the labor group is seeking higher wages — a recent proposal was a 20 percent raise over the course of the deal — as well as revised scheduling practices. The union has also recently called for a 40-hour work week for workers with seniority and six-hour shifts to be expanded into eight-hour shifts for various workers. The contract that workers are currently operating under expired nearly nine months ago, and in September, more than 98 percent of voting bargaining unit members voted to authorize a strike, which their negotiators could call at any time, a move that would hobble the park. But negotiations remain ongoing to reach a deal.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In the meantime, Universal’s theme parks remain an important profit center for the company, even as they have been hit by some of the same inflationary pressures facing all companies and their workers. NBCUniversal’s theme parks division revenue dropped 4.4 percent to $2.6 billion in the third quarter of 2026, a decrease the company attributed to the macroeconomic and geopolitical environment as well as capacity issues at the Orlando resort’s new Epic Universe park and competitors being more nimble in their marketing. In 2025 the theme park division accounted for eight percent of NBCUniversal owner Comcast’s total revenue, per Barron’s, but it remains a potential growth area as other parts of the business are set to shrink.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: And executive pay, at least that which is disclosed to shareholders, sure isn’t going down. In 2025 Comcast co-CEO Mark Cavanagh received $71.8 million in compensation, more than 150 percent his take-home pay from 2024. Co-CEO Brian Roberts received $35.1 million, a raise of 4 percent from 2024. Information on the compensation of Woodbury, who manages the parks, is not provided to shareholders.

Like many of his colleagues, Rodriguez — the cook who confronted Donna Langley — is typically assigned a lot of hours during Halloween Horror Nights, the park’s annual scarefest featuring haunted houses and actors terrifying visitors. While in the past he has at times slept in his car or in the park, he’s recently moved into an apartment with a roommate in the Pico-Union neighborhood of L.A. He’s warned his roommate that he doesn’t know how long he can afford to stay there, however. Usually when hours are whittled down during the winter and early spring slow season, Rodriguez, a dual U.S.-Mexico citizen, lives with family in Mexico to enjoy the lower cost of living.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: This isn’t where he thought this job would take him. When he got started working at the park, he decided to try having a single job, rather than multiple. He says, “But man, I guess what [was] a futuristic idea for me turns out to be in between homeless and immigrating to another country.” Still, he loves his job. He says, “It’s really just seeing the smiles on people’s faces every day when I get to come into the park. I’m like, ‘Holy shit.’”

articles.title: Wall Street braces for Democratic gains as 2026 midterm election nears

paras.en: Investors expect a blue wave in next week's midterm election, as Democrats surge in polls and President Donald Trump's approval rating remains low.
paras.zh: 投资者预计下周的中期选举将出现蓝色浪潮，因为民主党的民意调查激增，唐纳德特朗普总统的支持率仍然很低。

paras.en: Public polling suggests Democrats are likely to take control of the House of Representatives, and analysts who parse what politics means for investors are in overdrive to tell their clients how to prepare for what Congress will look like after the Tuesday election.
paras.zh: 民意调查显示，民主党人可能会控制众议院，而分析政治对投资者意味着什么的分析师则过度热衷于告诉他们的客户，如何为周二大选后的国会做好准备。

paras.en: Concern about the spending plans and priorities of a Democratic-controlled Congress permeates analyst reports reviewed by CNBC. But because Trump has another two years of his presidency, a divided government would likely create gridlock that would prevent congressional leadership in opposition to the president from getting much done, analysts are advising their clients.
paras.zh: CNBC审查的分析师报告充斥着对民主党控制的国会的支出计划和优先事项的担忧。但由于特朗普还有两年的总统任期，一个分裂的政府可能会造成僵局，使反对总统的国会领导层无法做很多工作，分析师正在为他们的客户提供建议。

paras.en: Most analysts believe Democrats are also within striking distance of a Senate majority, though that outcome is significantly less likely than a House flip according to the polls. Next Tuesday's elections will determine which party controls both chambers of Congress for the remainder of Trump's presidency, after two years of full Republican control.
paras.zh: 大多数分析师认为，民主党人也在参议院多数席位的惊人距离之内，尽管根据民意调查，这一结果的可能性远远低于众议院的翻转。下周二的选举将决定哪个政党在共和党完全控制两年后，在特朗普总统任期的剩余时间内控制国会两院。

paras.en: Divided government typically makes must-pass legislation, like government funding and raising the debt ceiling, harder to enact. A debt ceiling standoff — or first-ever default on federal debt — could be particularly damaging.
paras.zh: 分裂的政府通常会使政府资助和提高债务上限等必须通过的立法更难颁布。债务上限对峙--或首次联邦债务违约--可能尤其具有破坏性。

paras.en: Wall Street watchers are also expecting Democrats to try to advance an ambitious and expensive agenda should they gain control of Congress. An Oct. 29 report from Piper Sandler analyzing Congressional Budget Office data projected that policy proposals from Democrats "would add $5 trillion to the deficit over the coming decade." The analysis assumes repeals of Trump's tariffs and reversing cuts to Medicaid, nutrition programs and Affordable Care Act subsidies.
paras.zh: 华尔街观察人士还预计，如果民主党获得对国会的控制权，他们将试图推进一项雄心勃勃且代价高昂的议程。派珀·桑德勒（ Piper Sandler ） 10月29日的一份报告分析了国会预算办公室的数据，预计民主党的政策提案“将在未来十年内增加5万$的赤字。“该分析假设特朗普的关税被废除，医疗补助、营养计划和《平价医疗法案》补贴的削减被撤销。

paras.en: Major policy swings — and big spending packages — become less likely as a divided government is unlikely to agree on issues. That's a dynamic the market typically enjoys. Trump's veto power would effectively block major Democratic policies from becoming law.
paras.zh: 由于分裂的政府不太可能就问题达成一致，重大政策波动以及大笔支出计划变得不太可能。这是市场通常喜欢的动态。特朗普的否决权将有效阻止民主党的主要政策成为法律。

paras.en: "A blue House is the obvious consensus base case," Wolfe Research said in an Oct. 27 report. The firm surveyed 138 investors and found 96% of those polled believed Democrats would prevail in House control.
paras.zh: “蓝宫是明显的共识基础案例，”沃尔夫研究公司在10月27日的一份报告中说。该公司对138名投资者进行了调查，发现96%的受访者认为民主党将在众议院占据主导地位。

paras.en: "The scale of polling error that would be required for Republicans to retain House control would be unprecedented in modern history, well above the polling error in the famously bad 2020 cycle," Wolfe wrote.
paras.zh: 沃尔夫写道： “共和党人保持众议院控制权所需的民意调查错误的规模在现代历史上是前所未有的，远远高于著名的2020年糟糕周期的民意调查错误。”

paras.en: Wolfe is less bullish on a Democratic Senate, though investors clearly see a possibility that Democrats regain control of both chambers of Congress.
paras.zh: 沃尔夫不太看好民主党参议院，尽管投资者清楚地看到民主党重新控制国会两院的可能性。

paras.en: Fifty-eight percent of investors the firm surveyed believed Democrats would gain control of the Senate, while 42% believed Republicans would retain control of the chamber. The investors surveyed were more bullish than Wolfe itself, which puts the chances of a Democratic Senate at 49%.
paras.zh: 该公司调查的投资者中有58%认为民主党人将获得参议院的控制权，而42%认为共和党人将保留对参议院的控制权。接受调查的投资者比沃尔夫本人更看好，后者认为民主党参议院的机会为49%。

paras.en: Other analysts are largely coalescing around the potential for a good night for Democrats.
paras.zh: 其他分析师在很大程度上围绕民主党人晚安的可能性进行了整合。

paras.en: "A blue wave scenario has become our base case," an Oct. 20 report from TD Securities reads. An Oct. 23 Raymond James report says "Democrats are in a solid position to win a majority in the House of Representatives and are increasingly likely to win enough seats to capture a Senate majority."
paras.zh: 道明证券10月20日的一份报告称： “蓝色浪潮已经成为我们的基本情况。” 10月23日，雷蒙德·詹姆斯（ Raymond James ）的一份报告说： “民主党在众议院赢得多数席位方面处于有利地位，并且越来越有可能赢得足够的席位来赢得参议院多数席位。”

paras.en: Even if Democrats sweep both chambers, protracted battles could still play out as Republicans maintain the White House and the Senate must still surpass the 60-vote filibuster threshold.
paras.zh: 即使民主党人横扫两院，随着共和党人维持白宫，参议院仍必须超过60票的议案阻挠门槛，旷日持久的战斗仍有可能爆发。

paras.en: Democrats winning control of the Senate could allay concerns about the Federal Reserve's independence from Trump, TD predicted.
paras.zh: 道明预测，赢得参议院控制权的民主党人可能会缓解人们对美联储独立于特朗普的担忧。

paras.en: That's because any new Fed members would need to be confirmed by the Senate, which would be unlikely to support a nominee who wouldn't support the central bank charting its own course.
paras.zh: 这是因为任何新的美联储成员都需要得到参议院的确认，参议院不太可能支持不支持美联储制定自己的路线的提名人。

paras.en: Democrats are also expected to investigate companies that have done business with the Trump administration should they win control of a chamber. The majority party in Congress holds subpoena power on committees. Some Democrats have already telegraphed their investigative priorities ahead of the election.
paras.zh: 预计民主党人还将调查那些与特朗普政府有业务往来的公司，如果他们赢得了商会的控制权。国会中的多数党拥有对委员会的传票权力。一些民主党人已经在选举前电报了他们的调查优先事项。

paras.en: The debt ceiling is likely the most critical sticking point for the economy that lawmakers will need to address during the next Congress, unless Republicans raise it during the lame-duck session between the election and the start of the next Congress in January. The Bipartisan Policy Center expects the U.S. will reach the debt limit between late-winter and mid-summer 2027.
paras.zh: 债务上限可能是立法者在下届国会期间需要解决的最关键的经济症结所在，除非共和党人在大选和1月份下届国会开始之间的跛脚鸭会议期间提高债务上限。两党政策中心预计，美国将在2027年冬末至夏中达到债务上限。

paras.en: "While negotiations around the debt ceiling may come down to the wire, a Democratic Congress would make it slightly more likely that a bill is passed than a divided Congress," TD said.
paras.zh: TD表示： “虽然围绕债务上限的谈判可能会陷入困境，但民主党国会将使法案通过的可能性略高于分裂的国会。”

paras.en: If Congress does not raise the debt ceiling, the U.S. could default on its debt, causing catastrophic economic consequences.
paras.zh: 如果国会不提高债务上限，美国可能会拖欠债务，造成灾难性的经济后果。

paras.en: Democrats, should they control one slice of government, are expected to demand concessions from Republicans in exchange for their votes to raise the debt ceiling. That sets up a potential standoff, which analysts note Republicans could avoid if they lose next week and raise the debt ceiling during the lame duck.
paras.zh: 如果民主党控制一小部分政府，预计他们将要求共和党人做出让步，以换取他们提高债务上限的选票。这引发了潜在的对峙，分析师指出，如果共和党人下周输球，并在跛脚鸭期间提高债务上限，他们可以避免这种对峙。

paras.en: "[R]aising the debt limit before January could substantially reduce leverage Democrats have over healthcare, Medicaid, SNAP, and broader domestic spending priorities in the next Congress," Raymond James told its clients.
paras.zh: 雷蒙德·詹姆斯（ Raymond James ）告诉其客户： “在1月之前提高债务上限可能会大大降低民主党在下届国会对医疗保健、医疗补助、SNAP和更广泛的国内支出优先事项的影响力。”

paras.en: This story has been corrected to reflect that the Bipartisan Policy Center projects the U.S. will reach its debt limit next year. An earlier version mischaracterized the center's projection.
paras.zh: 本文已更正，此前版本错误地描述了两党政策中心预测美国将于明年达到债务上限的情况。

articles.title: Fed officials are already saying they’ll need to get back to hiking rates

paras.en: Two Federal Reserve presidents on Friday said interest rates will need to move higher to rein in inflation.
paras.zh: 两位美联储主席周五表示，需要提高利率以抑制通胀。

paras.en: The St. Louis Fed's Alberto Musalem said another rate hike will need to happen soon. And Lorie Logan of the Dallas Fed predicted that the central bank will need to raise rates by quarter-point increments at least two more times.
paras.zh: 圣路易斯联储的阿尔贝托·穆萨勒姆表示，需要很快再次加息。达拉斯联储的洛里·洛根(Lorie Logan)预测，央行将需要至少两次加息四分之一个百分点。

paras.en: The comments from the two officials offer the first morsels of insight into what leaders at the Fed see next after the central bank on Wednesday elected to leave rates unchanged for now. The remarks are likely to bolster the view among investors that the Federal Open Market Committee will return to hiking rates at its next meeting in December.
paras.zh: 两位官员的言论为了解美联储周三选择暂时维持利率不变后美联储领导人下一步的看法提供了初步见解。这些言论可能会增强投资者的观点，即联邦公开市场委员会将在 12 月的下次会议上恢复加息。

paras.en: Fed funds futures traders are pricing in a roughly 76% likelihood of the Fed lifting rates by a quarter percentage point at that gathering, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
paras.zh: 根据 CME 的 FedWatch 工具，联邦基金期货交易员预计美联储在那次会议上加息 25 个百分点的可能性约为 76%。

paras.en: "I judge that additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon," Musalem said in prepared remarks for the Shadow Open Market Committee, a gathering of economists in New York focused on the central bank.
paras.zh: 穆萨利姆在为影子公开市场委员会准备的讲话中表示：“我认为有必要进一步收紧货币政策，而且很快就会出现这样的情况。”影子公开市场委员会是一个由纽约经济学家组成的会议，重点关注央行问题。

paras.en: "Incremental adjustments made earlier are usually less disruptive than larger and abrupt actions taken later," Musalem said. "Moving sooner in smaller steps while inflation expectations are anchored has a better chance of succeeding without adverse impact on the labor market or economic growth."
paras.zh: 穆萨利姆说：“较早采取的增量调整通常比后来采取的更大规模、突然的行动更具破坏性。” “在通胀预期得到锚定的情况下，以较小的步伐更快地采取行动，更有可能取得成功，而不会对劳动力市场或经济增长产生不利影响。”

paras.en: In remarks roughly an hour later, Logan said: "It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases."
paras.zh: 大约一个小时后，洛根在讲话中表示：“鉴于目前的前景，我仍然清楚，联邦公开市场委员会需要至少再两次加息 25 个基点。”

paras.en: Still, she said, that doesn't mean the Fed has to raise rates at every meeting.
paras.zh: 不过，她表示，这并不意味着美联储必须在每次会议上加息。

paras.en: "Skipping a meeting does not change the monetary policy destination," Logan told students at Davidson College in North Carolina, according to her prepared remarks. "Indeed, by making the destination clear, the FOMC can better help the economy adapt and obtain the promised benefits of a skip."
paras.zh: 根据洛根准备好的讲话，她对北卡罗来纳州戴维森学院的学生说：“跳过会议不会改变货币政策的目标。” “事实上，通过明确目标，联邦公开市场委员会可以更好地帮助经济适应并获得跳过承诺的好处。”

paras.en: After the predicted two rate hikes, Logan said, "it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate."
paras.zh: 洛根表示，在预测的两次加息之后， “在我看来，暂停并审查经济和金融发展以确定哪些进一步行动可能是合适的，这是有道理的。”

paras.en: Logan will be among the Fed officials voting on the rate decision in December; Musalem is slated to be a non-voting member of the committee until 2028.
paras.zh: 洛根将是 12 月份就利率决定进行投票的美联储官员之一； Musalem 预计将担任该委员会的无投票权成员直至 2028 年。

paras.en: In his remarks, Musalem broadly spoke positively about the state of the U.S. economy, which he described as "resilient." He pointed to Thursday's data on U.S. GDP, which showed a stronger-than-expected growth rate of 3.4%.
paras.zh: 在他的讲话中， Musalem广泛地积极谈到了美国经济的状况，他称之为“有弹性。“他指出，周四的美国国内生产总值数据显示，增长率高于预期，为3.4%。

paras.en: He said there are several factors boosting the economy, including the artificial-intelligence buildout and financial conditions that "remain accommodative."
paras.zh: 他说，有几个因素推动了经济发展，包括人工智能的建设和“保持宽松”的金融状况。

paras.en: Musalem said the labor market has been "remarkably stable and balanced." The unemployment rate of 4.2% sits at the median of long-run projections by participants in the Federal Open Market Committee, the group tasked with setting interest rates, he noted. Musalem is not a voting member of the FOMC this year, and isn't expected to have a vote until 2028.
paras.zh: Musalem表示，劳动力市场“非常稳定和平衡。他指出：“ 4.2%的失业率处于联邦公开市场委员会参与者长期预测的中位数，该委员会的任务是设定利率。Musalem今年不是联邦公开市场委员会的投票成员，预计要到2028年才能投票。

paras.en: But Musalem warned that inflation is "too high," citing the personal consumption expenditures price index released Thursday that showed annual inflation above 3%. In the question-and-answer portion of the event, Musalem said he's watching core inflation closely, and is on alert for any indications that current inflationary pressures are broadening out.
paras.zh: 但Musalem警告说，通货膨胀“过高” ，理由是周四公布的个人消费支出价格指数显示年通货膨胀率超过3%。在活动的问答部分， Musalem表示他正在密切关注核心通胀，并对当前通胀压力正在扩大的任何迹象保持警惕。

paras.en: Fed officials have been closely monitoring inflation expectations among consumers and investors to ensure they don't get too far above the central bank's long-term target of 2%.
paras.zh: 美联储官员一直在密切关注消费者和投资者的通胀预期，以确保他们不会超出美联储2%的长期目标。

paras.en: Musalem said there's a likely scenario where inflation remains above 2% into the future unless the Fed adjusts monetary policy.
paras.zh: Musalem表示，除非美联储调整货币政策，否则未来可能会出现通货膨胀率保持在2%以上的情况。

paras.en: "The best that monetary policy can do now for employment and economic growth is to restore price stability in a timely manner," Musalem said. "The short-run economic costs of reducing inflation are less when the central bank acts before inflation has become entrenched and is expected to persist."
paras.zh: Musalem表示： “货币政策现在对就业和经济增长能做的最好的事情就是及时恢复价格稳定。” “当央行在通货膨胀根深蒂固并有望持续下去之前采取行动时，降低通货膨胀的短期经济成本较低。”

paras.en: Two of the 12 FOMC voters dissented from Wednesday's decision to keep rates unchanged – Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack – both of whom wanted the committee to raise rates by a quarter percentage point.
paras.zh: 12名联邦公开市场委员会(FOMC)选民中有两人反对周三维持利率不变的决定，即州长丽莎·库克(Lisa Cook)和克利夫兰联储主席贝丝·哈马克(Beth Hammack) ，他们都希望委员会将利率提高四分之一个百分点。

paras.en: Speaking on CNBC Friday, former Richmond Fed President Jeffrey Lacker said he too would have been in favor of a rate hike this week.
paras.zh: 前里士满联储主席杰弗里·拉克（ Jeffrey Lacker ）周五在CNBC发表讲话时表示，他本周也会支持加息。

paras.en: "I've been surprised by the lack of urgency. Inflation's been high around three, three-and-a-half percent for so long," Lacker told Kelly Evans on CNBC's "The Exchange." "Maybe they'll come around in the next couple of meetings, but I've been surprised at the lack of urgency."
paras.zh: “我对缺乏紧迫感感到惊讶。长期以来，通货膨胀率一直高达3.5%左右，” Lacker在CNBC的“The Exchange”节目中告诉Kelly Evans。“也许他们会在接下来的几次会议中出现，但我对缺乏紧迫感感到惊讶。”

paras.en: A December increase would be the second of 2026, after the FOMC elected for a quarter-point hike in September. That marked the central bank's first increase to borrowing costs since 2023.
paras.zh: 12月将是2026年的第二次加息，此前联邦公开市场委员会(FOMC)选择在9月份加息25个百分点。这标志着央行自2023年以来首次提高借贷成本。

paras.en: James Bullard, a former St. Louis Fed president, told CNBC that he was not in favor of Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's plan to make certain Fed meetings focused on broader strategy rather than on live interest rate decisions.
paras.zh: 前圣路易斯联储主席詹姆斯•布拉德(James Bullard)告诉CNBC ，他不赞成美联储主席凯文•沃什(Kevin Warsh)的计划，即让美联储的某些会议专注于更广泛的战略，而不是实时利率决策。

paras.en: Warsh on Wednesday announced a plan for one Fed meeting in 2027 and two meetings in 2028 to center on bigger policy discussions. Warsh said he did not expect to announce rate decisions or make Fed statements at these adjusted meetings.
paras.zh: Warsh周三宣布了一项计划，即在2027年召开一次美联储会议，在2028年召开两次会议，以更大的政策讨论为中心。沃什表示，他预计不会在这些调整后的会议上宣布利率决定或发表美联储声明。

paras.en: "I don't think skipping a meeting is a good idea," Bullard said. "If you don't have a meeting, and then it's a pretty volatile world and you have to act, you're going to have to call a special meeting in that circumstance."
paras.zh: “我不认为跳过会议是个好主意，”布拉德说。“如果你没有开会，那么这是一个相当不稳定的世界，你必须采取行动，在这种情况下，你将不得不召集一次特别会议。”

paras.en: Lacker recommended Warsh take the opposite approach.
paras.zh: Lacker建议Warsh采取相反的方法。

paras.en: "If you want to take the pressure off individual meetings, have more of them," he said.
paras.zh: “如果你想减轻个人会议的压力，那就多参加一些，”他说。

articles.title: Alaska Senate: Judge fast tracks new bids to dismiss DOJ lawsuit over 2nd Sullivan candidacy

paras.en: A federal judge in Alaska on Friday kept on a fast track efforts to dismiss a Department of Justice lawsuit that seeks to delay certification of the state's U.S. Senate election because of possible voter confusion from having two Dan Sullivans — one of whom is the incumbent Republican — on the ballot.
paras.zh: 阿拉斯加的一名联邦法官周五继续快速驳回司法部的一项诉讼，该诉讼旨在推迟对该州美国参议院选举的认证，因为两名丹·沙利文（其中一名是现任共和党人）参加选票可能会让选民感到困惑。

paras.en: Judge Sharon Gleason ordered the DOJ to respond by 1 p.m. Alaska Time on Friday to the new dismissal motions, which were filed hours after the department amended its suit in U.S. District Court in Anchorage on Thursday to add a new legal claim.
paras.zh: 莎伦·格里森法官命令司法部在下午 1 点前做出回应。阿拉斯加州时间周五公布了新的驳回动议，该动议是在该部门周四向安克雷奇美国地方法院修改诉讼以增加新的法律主张几个小时后提出的。

paras.en: The DOJ's updating of the civil complaint forced Gleason to rule the prior dismissal motions were moot.
paras.zh: 司法部对民事申诉的更新迫使格里森裁定先前的驳回动议没有实际意义。

paras.en: Gleason gave state election officials, the campaign of Democratic nominee Mary Peltola, and other groups until noon Saturday to reply to the DOJ's response.
paras.zh: 格里森要求州选举官员、民主党候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉的竞选团队和其他团体在周六中午之前回复司法部的回应。

paras.en: The judge's order leaves open the possibility that she will rule on the dismissal motions before Tuesday, which is Election Day, as both the state and Peltola's campaign have requested.
paras.zh: 法官的命令使得她有可能按照州政府和佩尔托拉竞选团队的要求，在周二即选举日之前对解雇动议做出裁决。

paras.en: The state, the campaign, and other intervenors in the suit argue the DOJ has no legal authority to block certification of an election because two candidates on a four-candidate ballot happen to share the same name.
paras.zh: 州政府、竞选团队和诉讼中的其他干预者认为，司法部没有法律权力阻止选举认证，因为四名候选人选票上的两名候选人碰巧姓名相同。

paras.en: The winner of Alaska's race could determine which party holds a majority in the Senate starting in January. Republicans currently have 53 seats in the 100-member chamber.
paras.zh: 阿拉斯加竞选的获胜者可能会从一月份开始决定哪个政党在参议院占据多数席位。共和党目前在 100 名议员的众议院中拥有 53 个席位。

paras.en: Alaska's election uses ranked choice voting. If no candidate obtains more than 50% of the vote in the first count, then the fourth-place finisher will be eliminated, and the second choice on that candidate's ballots will be allocated to the remaining candidates.
paras.zh: 阿拉斯加的选举采用排名选择投票。如果没有候选人在第一次计票中获得超过 50% 的选票，那么第四名的候选人将被淘汰，该候选人选票上的第二个选择将分配给剩余的候选人。

paras.en: Only Peltola and Sen. Sullivan are considered likely to draw large shares of the votes.
paras.zh: 只有佩尔托拉和参议员沙利文被认为可能获得大量选票。

paras.en: The DOJ's suit seeks to delay certification of the Senate election if Sen. Sullivan loses by a margin that could be attributable to voter confusion over the presence of the other candidate, who is listed as Daniel J. Sullivan, on the ballot.
paras.zh: 如果参议员沙利文以微弱优势落败，司法部的诉讼旨在推迟对参议院选举的认证，而这种差距可能是由于选民对另一位候选人（被列为丹尼尔·J·沙利文）出现在选票上感到困惑。

paras.en: The amended complaint, which updates the suit filed Oct. 23, added a claim under the Supremacy Clause of the U.S. Constitution to the first claim, under the National Voter Registration Act.
paras.zh: 修改后的起诉书更新了 10 月 23 日提起的诉讼，在根据《国家选民登记法》提出的第一项索赔中增加了根据美国宪法至高无上条款提出的索赔。

paras.en: The DOJ also included details of a New York Times article published Wednesday that reported that Peltola campaign aides and senior aides at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee helped recruit the retired school teacher Daniel J. Sullivan to enter the Senate race with the hope of drawing votes from the incumbent Sullivan.
paras.zh: 司法部还提供了《纽约时报》周三发表的一篇文章的详细信息，该文章报道佩尔托拉竞选助手和民主党参议员竞选委员会的高级助手帮助招募退休学校教师丹尼尔·J·沙利文参加参议院竞选，希望从现任沙利文那里吸引选票。

paras.en: Peltola's campaign and the DSCC deny being involved in the retiree's Senate campaign.
paras.zh: 佩尔托拉的竞选团队和 DSCC 否认参与了这位退休人员的参议院竞选活动。

paras.en: Peltola's campaign, in its dismissal motion filed Thursday, said, "Rather than defend its indefensible legal claims as it was ordered to do, the Department of Justice ... has filed an Amended Complaint that does nothing to address the fatal problems that preclude it from bringing this case or obtaining the relief that it seeks."
paras.zh: 佩尔托拉的竞选团队在周四提交的驳回动议中表示，“司法部没有按照命令捍卫其站不住脚的法律主张，而是……提交了一份修订后的起诉书，该起诉书无助于解决阻止其提起此案或获得其寻求的救济的致命问题。”

paras.en: "The U.S. Constitution leaves the regulation of federal elections exclusively to the States and to Congress, and DOJ has no statutory authority to bring this case," the motion said.
paras.zh: 该动议说： “美国宪法将联邦选举的监管权仅留给各州和国会，司法部没有法定权力提起诉讼。”

paras.en: In their own dismissal motion, state election officials said the amended lawsuit "rests on the same meritless theory that the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA)—a voter registration law—governs this case, which has nothing to do with voter registration."
paras.zh: 州选举官员在自己的驳回动议中表示，修改后的诉讼“基于与《国家选民登记法》（NVRA）（一部选民登记法）管辖此案的同样毫无根据的理论，与选民登记无关。”

paras.en: "Because this reading of the NVRA fails, the amended complaint fails," the motion said.
paras.zh: 动议称：“由于对 NVRA 的解读失败，修改后的投诉也失败。”

articles.title: An exclusive conversation with the developer of REA, the viral AI reverse engineering tool

paras.en: Buy a new car, and you’re free to repaint the exterior or add new wheels. But you aren’t supposed to edit the code controlling the dash display and other electronics. Once software is packaged up and shipped, it’s meant to stay the way the manufacturer intended it.
paras.zh: 购买新车，您可以自由地重新粉刷外部或添加新车轮。但您不应该编辑控制仪表板显示屏和其他电子设备的代码。一旦软件打包并发货，它就应该保持制造商预期的样子。

paras.en: Morluto, a software engineer who spoke with Scientific American on the condition that he remain pseudonymous, took that as a challenge. His tool, Reverse Engineer Anything, or REA, lets artificial intelligence agents pull apart programs and reconstitute them to their users’ liking.
paras.zh: 软件工程师莫鲁托（Morluto）在接受《科学美国人》采访时表示，他要求保持化名，他认为这是一个挑战。他的工具“逆向工程任何东西”（Reverse Engineer Anything，简称 REA）可以让人工智能代理分解程序并根据用户的喜好重新构建它们。

paras.en: His interest began with game decompilation, a corner of reverse engineering in which fans painstakingly rebuild the code of video games. Such work has taken years without AI assistance. Now Morluto—whose name comes from an old video gaming alias—sees much broader uses. REA’s Discord community includes examples of people modifying everything from printers to televisions. The project has more than 400,000 stars on GitHub, a rough gauge of its popularity.
paras.zh: 他的兴趣始于游戏反编译，这是逆向工程的一个角落，粉丝们在其中煞费苦心地重建视频游戏代码。在没有人工智能协助的情况下，此类工作需要花费数年时间。现在，Morluto（其名字来自一个古老的视频游戏别名）有了更广泛的用途。 REA 的 Discord 社区包含人们修改从打印机到电视等所有东西的示例。该项目在 GitHub 上拥有超过 400,000 颗星，粗略衡量了其受欢迎程度。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “We’ve gotten used to the fact that software is all around us, but none of it is anything that we can influence,” he says. He hopes AI-enabled reverse engineering could fix this: “If code is magic, then we are all capable of it,” Morluto says.
paras.zh: “我们已经习惯了软件就在我们身边这一事实，但我们无法影响它们，”他说。他希望人工智能逆向工程能够解决这个问题：“如果代码有魔力，那么我们都有能力实现它，”莫鲁托说。

paras.en: For decades, software makers have enjoyed a sense of security through tedium: taking apart a compiled program was such a grind that few people bothered. But the packaging also kept us out of the guts of our own gadgets. If anyone with a ChatGPT subscription or an open-weight model can hand off that work, control over a device tilts toward whoever’s curious to look inside—no matter their intentions. “This is going to pose a crisis for trade secret and copyright law,” says James Grimmelmann, a law professor at Cornell Tech.
paras.zh: 几十年来，软件制造商在单调乏味中享受着安全感：拆开编译好的程序是一件苦差事，很少有人会费心。但包装也让我们远离了自己的小玩意。如果拥有 ChatGPT 订阅或开放权重模型的任何人都可以移交这项工作，那么对设备的控制权就会倾向于那些好奇地想了解内部情况的人，无论他们的意图如何。康奈尔理工大学法学教授詹姆斯·格里梅尔曼表示：“这将对商业秘密和版权法造成危机。”

paras.en: Morluto sees this as a natural progression in the relationship between people and the technology they use. Throughout our conversation, he kept invoking tech founders who shaped his work—Apple’s Steve Jobs, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Y Combinator’s Paul Graham. “A lot of the creators in the past,” he says, “were all hackers and tinkerers, experimenters growing up.” He believes REA can turn its users into that kind of creator. “You are capable not just of magic but of creating beautiful things,” Morluto says.
paras.zh: 莫鲁托认为这是人与他们使用的技术之间关系的自然发展。在我们的整个谈话中，他不断引用那些塑造了他的作品的科技创始人——苹果公司的史蒂夫·乔布斯、英伟达公司的黄仁勋、Y Combinator 的保罗·格雷厄姆。 “过去的很多创作者，”他说，“都是黑客、修补匠、实验者。”他相信 REA 可以将其用户变​​成这样的创作者。 “你不仅有能力施展魔法，还能创造美丽的事物，”莫鲁托说。

paras.en: In his view, tech has become an industry full of walled gardens, and thanks to AI, “their walls were not as robust as they had thought.”
paras.zh: 在他看来，科技已经成为一个充满围墙花园的行业，而由于人工智能，“他们的围墙并不像他们想象的那么坚固。”

paras.en: Those walls come from the way software is bundled into executable programs. Before a program can run, the code people write in a programming language such as Python has to be translated, or compiled, into binary, a sequence of 1’s and 0’s that actually tells the computer what to do. Reverse engineering software involves running that translation backward, turning binary back into code a person can read in the process of decompilation.
paras.zh: 这些墙来自于软件捆绑成可执行程序的方式。在程序运行之前，人们用 Python 等编程语言编写的代码必须被翻译或编译为二进制，即由 1 和 0 组成的序列，实际上告诉计算机要做什么。逆向工程软件涉及向后运行该翻译，将二进制文件转回人们在反编译过程中可以阅读的代码。

paras.en: Reverse engineers have long done this with tools such as Ghidra, a program the U.S. National Security Agency developed as part of its cybersecurity efforts. REA provides the pipelines that let an AI agent orchestrate Ghidra and other programs on its own.
paras.zh: 逆向工程师长期以来一直使用 Ghidra 等工具来完成此任务，Ghidra 是美国国家安全局作为其网络安全工作的一部分而开发的程序。 REA 提供了让 AI 代理自行编排 Ghidra 和其他程序的管道。

paras.en: "Reverse engineering is a little bit like pattern matching," says Morluto. "AI has extremely strong reasoning and pattern matching skills."
paras.zh: “逆向工程有点像模式匹配，”莫鲁托说。 “人工智能具有极强的推理和模式匹配能力。”

paras.en: Before 2026 decompilation was the domain of a select few experts, according to Zion Basque, an assistant professor at the University of Georgia, who studies reverse engineering. Now, he says, nearly anyone can play. His research group developed Kuna, one of the decompilers REA can equip AI agents with. The kinds of reverse engineering he sees people doing with REA could have been done before, just never at this scale. “I haven’t seen what the limits of this are yet,” he says.
paras.zh: 佐治亚大学研究逆向工程的助理教授 Zion Basque 表示，在 2026 年之前，反编译是少数专家的领域。他说，现在几乎任何人都可以玩。他的研究小组开发了 Kuna，这是 REA 可以装备人工智能代理的反编译器之一。他看到人们用 REA 进行的逆向工程以前就可以完成，只是从未达到如此规模。 “我还没有看到这有什么限制，”他说。

paras.en: Done by hand, that kind of work would take experts months, if they managed it at all, according to Grimmelmann. Now the limit, he says, is what you can afford. “If you have the tokens, you can set it loose on almost any piece of software,” he says.
paras.zh: 格里梅尔曼表示，如果专家们能够完成的话，这种工作如果是手工完成的话，需要花费数月的时间。他说，现在的限制是你能承受的范围。 “如果你有代币，你就可以在几乎任何软件上使用它，”他说。

paras.en: For some corners of the software industry, that’s an existential problem that the law cannot easily patch. Copyright protects a program’s code, Grimmelmann says, but not the algorithms and ideas the code implements. “This opens up a whole world of mods and remixes and interoperable new clients that really reduce the lead time people get from deploying software,” he says.
paras.zh: 对于软件行业的某些领域来说，这是一个法律无法轻易解决的生存问题。格里梅尔曼说，版权保护程序的代码，但不保护代码实现的算法和想法。 “这开启了一个模组、混音和可互操作的新客户端的世界，真正减少了人们部署软件的准备时间，”他说。

paras.en: REA isn’t the only thing eating into that head start. In early October Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 helped a developer build open-source clones of Adobe’s Creative Cloud programs, which are known for their tight controls and steep prices.
paras.zh: REA 并不是唯一影响这一领先优势的因素。 10 月初，Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5.5 帮助开发人员构建了 Adob​​e Creative Cloud 程序的开源克隆，该程序以其严格的控制和高昂的价格而闻名。

paras.en: Joey Castillo, an open-source developer and technologist in residence at Cornell Tech, went after something smaller. He has reverse engineered various tools in the past, but his first brush with using AI to do it came when he tried to modify a smart ring he had bought in Shenzhen, China. He was impressed that the AI model could reverse engineer the ring and teach him at the same time. “I learned a lot just by watching Claude work,” he says.
paras.zh: Joey Castillo 是康奈尔科技大学的一名开源开发人员和技术专家，他追求的是更小的东西。他过去曾对各种工具进行逆向工程，但当他试图修改他在中国深圳购买的智能戒指时，他第一次接触到使用人工智能来实现这一点。令他印象深刻的是，人工智能模型可以对戒指进行逆向工程，同时教他。 “通过观看克劳德工作，我学到了很多东西，”他说。

paras.en: The desire to tinker comes from wanting to take control of the things you buy, according to Castillo. “I bought this object, and it’s being gatekept from me,” he says. “Now I’m going to have the power to make it do what I want.”
paras.zh: 卡斯蒂略表示，修补的欲望来自于想要掌控你所购买的东西。 “我买了这个东西，但它却被我看守着，”他说。 “现在我将有能力让它做我想做的事。”

paras.en: Some of those gates serve an important purpose, though. Much as AI is proving adept at breaking into security systems, it is also very good at breaking things like digital rights management and the protected firmware baked into devices.
paras.zh: 不过，其中一些大门有重要的用途。正如人工智能被证明擅长闯入安全系统一样，它也非常擅长破坏数字版权管理和设备中受保护的固件等内容。

paras.en: Projects like REA may also make it too easy for amateurs to gain a sort of synthetic expertise. Castillo and his open-source friends worry about people digging around in devices they don’t fully understand. “This is all going to be very fun and games until someone vibe codes firmware and it causes the battery to catch fire midflight,” Castillo says. He doubts AI models have the foresight that reverse engineering experts bring to deciding which modifications to make because AI “can only ‘yes, and.’ It can’t ‘no, but.’”
paras.zh: 像 REA 这样的项目也可能让业余爱好者很容易获得某种综合专业知识。卡斯蒂略和他的开源朋友担心人们在他们不完全理解的设备上进行挖掘。卡斯蒂略说：“这一切都将非常有趣和游戏，直到有人对固件进行编码并导致电池在飞行中着火。”他怀疑人工智能模型是否具有逆向工程专家那样的远见来决定进行哪些修改，因为人工智能“只能说‘是，并且’。而不能说‘不，但是’。”

paras.en: Since our first conversation with Morluto, some social media users have reported OpenAI and Anthropic banning or blocking their use of REA. In a reply on X, an OpenAI researcher called the block on reverse engineering “mostly accidental.”
paras.zh: 自从我们第一次与 Morluto 交谈以来，一些社交媒体用户报告了 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 禁止或阻止他们使用 REA。在 X 上的回复中，一位 OpenAI 研究人员称逆向工程受阻“主要是偶然的”。

paras.en: Morluto isn’t worried. If anything, he says, the “fiasco” just brings more attention to the project and to the kind of discovery he was aiming for. “That’s the core of Reverse Engineer Anything,” he says. “It’s a road that leads you to question what it is that you want.”
paras.zh: 莫鲁托并不担心。他说，如果说有什么不同的话，那就是“惨败”只会让更多人关注这个项目以及他所追求的发现。 “这就是逆向工程的核心，”他说。 “这是一条让你质疑自己想要什么的道路。”

paras.en: Accidental or not, such obstacles are unlikely to stop people who really want to reverse engineer their devices. Castillo already has a fallback in GLM-5.3, an open-weight model from the Chinese company Z.ai. Once it’s downloaded, no one can take it away. “If Anthropic and OpenAI decide they’re going to ban my account for reverse engineering, I’m going to fire up GLM-5.3 and reverse engineer the smart ring,” he says, “because I think it’s really cool to make this thing do what I wanted.”
paras.zh: 不管是否偶然，这些障碍不太可能阻止那些真正想要对其设备进行逆向工程的人。 Castillo 已经有了 GLM-5.3 的后备方案，这是中国公司 Z.ai 的开放权重模型。一旦下载，任何人都无法将其带走。 “如果 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 决定禁止我的逆向工程账户，我就会启动 GLM-5.3 并对智能环进行逆向工程，”他说，“因为我认为让这个东西做我想做的事情真的很酷。”

articles.title: This October is on track to be the hottest ever recorded

paras.en: This October is almost certainly going to be the hottest October ever recorded. Global temperatures this month are set to be around 1.76 degrees Celsius (about 3.17 degrees Fahrenheit) above preindustrial levels, surpassing the previous record set in 2023, researchers predict.
paras.zh: 几乎可以肯定，今年十月将是有记录以来最热的十月。研究人员预测，本月全球气温将比工业化前水平高出约 1.76 摄氏度（约 3.17 华氏度），超过 2023 年创下的纪录。

paras.en: An especially hot October also puts 2026 on track to be among the hottest years ever recorded—if not the hottest—according to projections from climate scientists Andrew Dessler and Zeke Hausfather. Their projection is based on data collected by the Europe-based Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S).
paras.zh: 根据气候科学家安德鲁·德斯勒 (Andrew Dessler) 和泽克·豪斯法瑟 (Zeke Hausfather) 的预测，特别炎热的 10 月也将使 2026 年成为有记录以来最热的年份之一（即使不是最热的）。他们的预测基于欧洲哥白尼气候变化服务（C3S）收集的数据。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Next year could be even more blistering. “This year’s record-setting October is a sign that the ‘Super El Niño’ is kicking into gear and will likely be the first in a series of record-setting months, culminating in a record-setting 2027,” Hausfather says.
paras.zh: 明年可能会更加激烈。 Hausfather 表示：“今年创纪录的 10 月是‘超级厄尔尼诺现象’即将启动的一个迹象，并且很可能是一系列创纪录月份中的第一个，并在 2027 年达到创纪录的顶峰。”

paras.en: El Niño is a cyclic climate pattern that occurs when part of the Pacific Ocean is unusually warm, affecting weather across the world. El Niño can exacerbate climate change—which is driven by the burning of fossil fuels—to boost global temperatures.
paras.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象是一种周期性气候模式，当太平洋部分地区异常温暖时就会发生，影响世界各地的天气。厄尔尼诺现象会加剧由化石燃料燃烧引起的气候变化，从而提高全球气温。

paras.en: In 2023, also an El Niño year, October temperatures reached 1.7 degrees C (3.06 degrees F) above preindustrial levels, according to Dessler and Hausfather’s analysis. The year was the hottest ever recorded at the time, after which it was surpassed by 2024. The following year, 2025, was the third-hottest year ever recorded.
paras.zh: 根据德斯勒和豪斯法瑟的分析，2023 年也是厄尔尼诺现象年，10 月气温比工业化前水平高出 1.7 摄氏度（3.06 华氏度）。这一年是当时有记录以来最热的一年，之后到 2024 年就超过了这一年。次年，即 2025 年，是有记录以来第三热的一年。

paras.en: October’s likely record follows several other superlative moments so far in 2026, including the U.S.’s hottest September, hottest first eight months and hottest 12-month period ever recorded, as well as the hottest global ocean temperatures ever recorded.
paras.zh: 10 月可能创下的纪录是在 2026 年迄今为止的几个最热时刻之后发生的，包括美国有记录以来最热的 9 月、最热的前 8 个月和最热的 12 个月，以及有记录以来最热的全球海洋温度。

articles.title: ‘Paleo lighting’ can fix your brain’s clock after daylight savings

paras.en: At 2 A.M. on November 1, the clocks will fall back, and for one weekend out of the year, the whole country will think about light and time. Most people will spend the extra hour asleep and the following week complaining that it’s nearly dark at 5 P.M. Regardless of how you feel about the time change, for the next four months the sun will rise in the sky closer to the time you do. That alignment is the best thing that could happen to your body clock—and your sleep—all year.
paras.zh: 凌晨 2 点11 月 1 日，时钟将倒退，一年中的一个周末，整个国家都会思考光和时间。大多数人会多睡一个小时，然后在接下来的一周里抱怨下午 5 点天就快黑了。无论您对时间变化有何感受，在接下来的四个月里，太阳在天空中升起的时间将会更接近您的升起时间。这种调整是全年对您的生物钟和睡眠可能发生的最好的事情。

paras.en: Of course, you can try to buy your way into a better night’s sleep right now: mouth tape, tablets of magnesium glycinate, blackout curtains, a wearable sensor that grades your sleep, a mattress that maintains a chill 62-degree-Fahrenheit temperature. The stack of such approaches can run into the thousands of dollars and has a name on social media—“sleep maxxing.” It’s the wellness market’s latest way of turning a basic human function into a product line.
paras.zh: 当然，您现在就可以尝试通过购买方式获得更好的睡眠：口腔胶带、甘氨酸镁片剂、遮光窗帘、可对您的睡眠进行分级的可穿戴传感器、保持 62 华氏度低温的床垫。这些方法的成本可能高达数千美元，并且在社交媒体上有一个名字——“睡眠最大化”。这是健康市场将人类基本功能转变为产品线的最新方式。

paras.en: But the two things that will do the most for your sleep cost nothing. That is because nobody has figured out how to package them.
paras.zh: 但对你的睡眠最有帮助的两件事是免费的。那是因为没有人知道如何包装它们。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: I’m talking about light: bright days, dark nights. Think of it as a return to nature. Call it Paleo lighting.
paras.zh: 我说的是光：明亮的白天，黑暗的夜晚。将其视为回归自然。称之为古照明。

paras.en: I shamelessly borrowed the term from the “Paleo diet,” which sold the premise that human physiology took shape under conditions that no longer exist and that the mismatch costs us something. We built an industry around what goes into our mouths. We left the eyes alone. Our ancestors could not dim the day, postpone the night, or order light at midnight. That is not an argument for candlelight or for unplugging the grid. It is the same dietary logic aimed at the organ that sets our internal clock.
paras.zh: 我无耻地从“古饮食”中借用了这个术语，它的前提是人类生理学是在不再存在的条件下形成的，而这种不匹配会让我们付出一些代价。我们围绕进入我们嘴里的东西建立了一个产业。我们留下了眼睛。我们的祖先无法调暗白天，推迟夜晚，或在午夜点灯。这并不是支持烛光或拔掉电网的理由。这与针对设定我们体内时钟的器官的饮食逻辑相同。

paras.en: This clock sits at the base of the brain, about 40,000 nerve cells in a structure called the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) in the hypothalamus, and it generally runs slightly long. Shut a person in a laboratory with no windows and no clocks, and typically the body settles into a day of roughly 24 hours and 12 minutes.
paras.zh: 这个时钟位于大脑底部，下丘脑中称为视交叉上核 (SCN) 的结构中约有 40,000 个神经细胞，并且它的运行时间通常稍长。将一个人关在没有窗户、没有时钟的实验室里，身体通常会适应大约 24 小时 12 分钟的一天。

paras.en: Light early in the morning is what pulls the clock back in line with the sun. Bright light at night does the opposite, telling it the day isn’t finished. And the clock in your head is not the only clock you own. Your liver, pancreas and immune cells all run on their own daily schedules, taking their cues from that cluster of cells in the hypothalamus linked to the sun. When the SCN loses alignment with the sun, these rhythms drift apart and optimal functioning may be lost.
paras.zh: 清晨的光线使时钟与太阳保持一致。夜晚的明亮光线则起到相反的作用，告诉它这一天还没有结束。而且你脑子里的时钟并不是你拥有的唯一时钟。你的肝脏、胰腺和免疫细胞都按照自己的日常时间表运行，从下丘脑中与太阳相关的细胞群中获取线索。当视交叉上核与太阳失去对准时，这些节律就会偏离，并且可能会失去最佳功能。

paras.en: The disruption to our circadian rhythms comes at a physiological price. Light at the wrong hour can suppress melatonin, the hormone that tells your body it is night. And from there, the effects may spread to digestion, heart rate and the timing of metabolic and immune programs evolved to run on a 24-hour schedule. How far that reach extends is still being mapped. The clearest view comes from animals, for which you can hold everything else steady and change only the light.
paras.zh: 我们的昼夜节律被破坏是要付出生理代价的。错误时间的光照会抑制褪黑激素的分泌，褪黑激素是一种告诉身体现在是晚上的激素。从那时起，影响可能会蔓延到消化、心率以及代谢和免疫程序的时间安排，进化为按 24 小时计划运行。该范围的延伸范围仍在绘制中。最清晰的视野来自动物，为此你可以保持其他一切稳定，只改变光线。

paras.en: In my laboratory, we have kept mice at night with lights set to five lux, roughly the brightness of a night-light in a kid’s bedroom. They gained more weight than mice sleeping in genuine darkness. They were not sleep-deprived; the night-light just disrupted their clock-gene rhythms, subsequently shifting their food intake to the wrong part of the day. In the case of nocturnal mice, they shifted their food intake from night to daytime. Because they generally sleep during the day, light at night can scramble their circadian timing without touching their sleep or rest time. Related work found the same dim night worsened weight gain, glucose control and inflammation in animals on a high-fat diet. Sleep, metabolism and immunity seem to act as gears in a clock: if there’s one misalignment, the whole system is disrupted.
paras.zh: 在我的实验室里，我们在晚上饲养老鼠，灯光设置为 5 勒克斯，大约相当于孩子卧室夜灯的亮度。它们比在真正的黑暗中睡觉的老鼠增加了更多的体重。他们并没有睡眠不足；夜光只是打乱了他们的生物钟基因节律，随后将他们的食物摄入转移到了一天中错误的时间。对于夜行性小鼠来说，它们将食物摄入量从夜间转移到白天。因为他们通常在白天睡觉，所以夜间的光线会扰乱他们的昼夜节律，而不会影响他们的睡眠或休息时间。相关研究发现，同样昏暗的夜晚会导致高脂肪饮食动物的体重增加、血糖控制和炎症恶化。睡眠、新陈代谢和免疫力似乎就像时钟中的齿轮：如果有一个失调，整个系统就会受到干扰。

paras.en: The obvious objection is fair: these are mice, they are nocturnal, they live in cages, and nobody has ever asked one how it slept. What happens when you run the experiment on people?
paras.zh: 明显的反对意见是公平的：这些是​​老鼠，它们是夜间活动的，它们住在笼子里，没有人问过它是如何睡觉的。当你对人进行实验时会发生什么？

paras.en: Researchers at Northwestern University put healthy young adults to bed for a single night in a room lit to 100 lux—dimmer than a well-lit kitchen, brighter than a night-light—and measured them in the morning. Their heart rates ran higher through the night. And by breakfast, they were measurably worse at handling sugar, assessed by increasing insulin resistance, than another group that slept in the dark.
paras.zh: 西北大学的研究人员让健康的年轻人在一个亮度为 100 勒克斯的房间里睡一晚——比光线充足的厨房更暗，比夜灯更亮——并在早上进行测量。他们的心率整夜都升高。通过胰岛素抵抗的增加来评估，到早餐时，他们处理糖分的能力明显比另一组在黑暗中睡觉的人差。

paras.en: That was one night in a laboratory, with 20 participants. “What happens over years in ordinary bedrooms?” is the harder question, and the best answer we have comes from 43,722 women, none of them shift workers, who were tracked for about five years. Those who slept with a television or a light on in the room were 17 percent more likely to gain 11 pounds or more and 33 percent more likely to develop obesity over that time, after researchers accounted for diet, exercise and sleep duration. Night-shift workers, who experience the extreme case of circadian rhythm disruption, carry higher rates of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, mood disorders and several cancers—though people who live that far out of phase with the sun differ from non-shift workers in many ways besides light.
paras.zh: 那是在实验室的一个晚上，有 20 名参与者。 “多年来，普通卧室里会发生什么？”这是一个更难的问题，我们的最佳答案来自 43,722 名女性，其中没有轮班工人，她们被跟踪了大约五年。研究人员考虑了饮食、锻炼和睡眠时间后，那些在房间里开着电视或灯睡觉的人在此期间体重增加 11 磅或以上的可能性增加了 17%，患肥胖症的可能性增加了 33%。夜班工人的昼夜节律受到严重破坏，他们患 2 型糖尿病、心血管疾病、情绪障碍和多种癌症的几率较高，尽管生活在与太阳的相位相差如此远的人与不值班工人在许多方面都存在差异，除了光线之外。

paras.en: The prescription costs almost nothing. Within an hour of waking, get outside for 10 to 30 minutes in whatever the sky is offering—an overcast morning outdoors still runs to thousands of lux; a well-lit kitchen only manages a few hundred. Sit near a window if you have one. In one small study, office workers with windows got far more daytime light than colleagues without them and slept the better part of an hour longer at night. When indoors in the evening, dim the lights and use warm light bulbs rather than overhead and blue lighting.
paras.zh: 处方几乎不需要花费任何费用。醒来一小时内，无论天气如何，到户外活动 10 到 30 分钟——阴天的早晨，户外的光照强度仍可达数千勒克斯；一个光线充足的厨房只能容纳几百人。如果有窗户的话，请坐在靠近窗户的地方。在一项小型研究中，有窗户的上班族比没有窗户的同事白天获得的光线要多得多，晚上的睡眠时间也多了一个小时。晚上在室内时，调暗灯光并使用暖色灯泡，而不是头顶和蓝色灯光。

paras.en: Then deal with the bedroom, which is the part everyone skips. Stand in yours tonight with the lights off and count what still glows: the router, the smoke detector, the charger, the standby light on the television, the sliver where the curtains refuse to meet.
paras.zh: 然后处理卧室，这是大家都跳过的部分。今晚关掉灯，站在你家里，数数还有哪些东西还在发光：路由器、烟雾探测器、充电器、电视上的待机灯、窗帘无法接合的条子。

paras.en: Nobody is ever going to sell you a dark night. You will have to make it on your own.
paras.zh: 没有人会卖给你一个漆黑的夜晚。你必须自己做。

articles.title: NASA’s Swift telescope will face a fiery demise after a failed rescue
articles.author: Meghan Bartels

paras.en: For two decades, when the high-energy universe called, NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory has answered. But now, the spacecraft’s science tenure is ending, just when its skills might be more valuable than ever. The Swift spacecraft is falling uncontrollably, destined to burn up in Earth’s atmosphere in just a few days.
paras.zh: 二十年来，当高能宇宙发出召唤时，美国宇航局尼尔·格尔尔斯·斯威夫特天文台就会做出回应。但现在，航天器的科学任期即将结束，而此时它的技能可能比以往任何时候都更有价值。雨燕号宇宙飞船正在失控地坠落，几天之内注定会在地球大气层中燃烧殆尽。

paras.en: The telescope launched in 2004, tailored to reveal the secrets of gamma-ray bursts. These outbursts are the most powerful kind scientists have ever seen, but they often faded before earlier telescopes could respond. Swift took its name from its ability to jump to work when a flash went off. That talent both illuminated these elusive bursts and made the observatory a cornerstone of modern astronomy for far longer than scientists ever dreamed.
paras.zh: 该望远镜于 2004 年发射，专为揭示伽马射线暴的秘密而定制。这些爆发是科学家所见过的最强大的爆发，但它们常常在早期望远镜做出反应之前就消失了。 Swift 因其能够在闪光灯一亮时立即开始工作而得名。这种天赋不仅照亮了这些难以捉摸的爆发，也使该天文台成为现代天文学的基石，时间比科学家们想象的要长得多。

paras.en: “This was designed to be a two-year mission,” says astrophysicist Brad Cenko of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Md. “We’re coming up on year 22. We are so fortunate to have had the opportunity to do all the things that we have.”
paras.zh: 马里兰州格林贝尔特美国宇航局戈达德太空飞行中心的天体物理学家 Brad Cenko 表示：“这是一项为期两年的任务。我们即将迎来第 22 年。我们很幸运有机会做我们拥有的所有事情。”

paras.en: Over the decades, the spacecraft has lost about half its original altitude as it constantly slammed into molecules in the atmosphere. Those minuscule impacts infinitesimally slowed the observatory, pushing it closer to Earth. The sun’s relatively high activity in recent years has accelerated the process, leaving the spacecraft unable to continue into the 2030s as engineers hoped. A spacecraft commissioned by NASA to loft Swift out of danger launched in early July, but by late August, technical issues made a boost attempt impossible.
paras.zh: 几十年来，由于不断撞击大气中的分子，航天器已经失去了大约一半的原始高度。这些微小的影响极大地减慢了天文台的速度，使其更接近地球。近年来太阳相对较高的活动加速了这一过程，导致航天器无法像工程师希望的那样持续到 2030 年代。美国国家航空航天局 (NASA) 委托一艘航天器将雨燕号送出危险，该航天器于 7 月初发射升空，但到了 8 月底，技术问题使得助推尝试变得不可能。

paras.en: Swift is doomed — with nothing lined up to replace its unique capabilities.
paras.zh: Swift 注定要失败——没有任何东西可以取代它独特的功能。

paras.en: When scientists dreamed up the Swift mission, the massive energy and elusive nature of gamma-ray bursts made them one of the most tantalizing phenomena out there. Astronomers desperately wanted to understand how they worked.
paras.zh: 当科学家们梦想着雨燕号任务时，伽马射线暴的巨大能量和难以捉摸的性质使它们成为最诱人的现象之一。天文学家迫切想了解它们是如何工作的。

paras.en: Swift was equipped with three instruments. Its Burst Alert Telescope gave scientists eyes on gamma-ray emissions from up to half the visible sky, with the resolution to pinpoint where light is coming from. The agile spacecraft could then swing itself and its other instruments — one tuned to X-rays and the other to visible and ultraviolet light — to quickly give scientists a view of a patch of sky across a swath of types of light. It was a combination unlike any observatory before or since.
paras.zh: 斯威夫特配备了三种乐器。它的爆发警报望远镜让科学家们能够观察到半个可见天空的伽马射线发射，并能够精确定位光线的来源。然后，这艘敏捷的航天器可以摆动自身和其他仪器——一个调整到X射线，另一个调整到可见光和紫外光——以快速让科学家们看到一片天空中穿过一系列光的情况。这是一个不同于之前或之后任何天文台的组合。

paras.en: “It’s such a unique telescope,” says astrophysicist Wen-fai Fong of Northwestern University in Evanston, Ill., who is not part of the mission team. “It has all these views of the universe, all in one observatory, which by itself is rare, but it can also rapidly point any of these instruments.”
paras.zh: “这是一台非常独特的望远镜，”伊利诺伊州埃文斯顿西北大学的天体物理学家方文辉说道，他不是任务团队的成员。 “它拥有所有这些宇宙视图，全部集中在一个天文台中，这本身就很罕见，但它也可以快速指向任何这些仪器。”

paras.en: Swift’s roster of accomplishments speaks to the power of that recipe. “Almost immediately after launch, Swift started discovering things,” says astrophysicist Lynn Cominsky of Sonoma State University in Rohnert Park, Calif. That’s not an exaggeration: One record-breaking observation, taken just the month after launch, revealed that stellar corpses with powerful magnetic fields undergo outbursts that create a distinct kind of gamma-ray signature.
paras.zh: 斯威夫特的成就证明了这个秘诀的力量。加利福尼亚州罗内特公园索诺玛州立大学的天体物理学家林恩·科明斯基说：“几乎在发射后不久，斯威夫特就开始发现一些东西。”这并不夸张：发射后一个月进行的一项破纪录的观测表明，具有强大磁场的恒星尸体会发生爆发，从而产生一种独特的伽马射线特征。

paras.en: That observation pushed back against scientists’ existing categorization of gamma-ray bursts. Before Swift, the bursts fell into two buckets. Long gamma-ray bursts lasted as long as minutes, and scientists believed they stemmed from exploding stars triggering supernovae. Short gamma-ray bursts, in contrast, lasted less than two seconds and were believed to originate in merging neutron stars, the superdense remains of a star large enough to explode but too small to create a black hole.
paras.zh: 这一观察结果推翻了科学家现有的伽马射线暴分类。在斯威夫特之前，爆发分为两桶。长时间的伽马射线暴持续了长达几分钟，科学家认为它们源于恒星爆炸引发的超新星。相比之下，短伽马射线暴持续时间不到两秒，被认为起源于中子星合并，中子星是一颗大到足以爆炸但又太小而无法形成黑洞的恒星的超致密残骸。

paras.en: Swift confirmed this basic sketch, but also complicated it by finding bursts that didn’t cleanly fit into this binary. “The more data you get, the more confused you get,” Cominsky says. Other notable bursts the telescope observed included the brightest (gamma-ray burst) of all time, nicknamed BOAT, the highest-energy photons from such a burst, and multiple claimants to the title of most distant burst.
paras.zh: 斯威夫特证实了这个基本的草图，但也通过发现不完全适合这个二进制文件的爆发来使其复杂化。 “你获得的数据越多，你就越困惑，”科明斯基说。该望远镜观察到的其他值得注意的爆发包括有史以来最亮的爆发（伽马射线暴），绰号为“船”，这种爆发中能量最高的光子，以及多个最遥远爆发称号的获得者。

paras.en: Notably, all of Swift’s data was public right away, even as team scientists were still working to understand what the telescope had seen. “That was very new,” Fong says, crediting the mission with inspiring other observatory teams to follow suit.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，斯威夫特的所有数据都立即公开，尽管团队科学家仍在努力了解望远镜所看到的内容。 “这是非常新的，”方说，并称赞这次任务激励了其他天文台团队效仿。

paras.en: As other astronomers heard about Swift’s work, they realized how powerful the observatory might be for their own interests as well. As Swift’s tenure unfolded, astronomers started asking to borrow the nimble observatory to study a whole range of objects changing on the sky.
paras.zh: 当其他天文学家听说斯威夫特的工作时，他们意识到天文台对于他们自己的利益也可能有多么强大。随着斯威夫特任期的展开，天文学家开始要求借用灵活的天文台来研究天空中变化的各种物体。

paras.en: “With scientists, if you give them a tool to do something, they will other find other things that you can do with that tool,” says astrophysicist Phil Evans of the University of Leicester in England. In its later years, Swift observed between five and 10 “targets of opportunity” most days, tallying hundreds or even thousands in a year.
paras.zh: 英国莱斯特大学的天体物理学家菲尔·埃文斯说：“对于科学家来说，如果你给他们一个工具来做某事，他们就会找到你可以用该工具做的其他事情。”在其晚年，斯威夫特大多数时候都会观察到 5 到 10 个“机会目标”，一年内会观察到数百甚至数千个。

paras.en: Perhaps its most ground-breaking collaborations were partnerships with observatories hunting for ghostly neutrinos that travel nearly as quickly as light but don’t interact often, and for gravitational waves, the ripples in spacetime triggered by massive objects. In 2017, Swift participated in back-to-back discoveries: the unique explosion caused by two neutron stars merging, then the first neutrino traced back to its origin.
paras.zh: 也许它最具突破性的合作是与天文台的合作，寻找幽灵般的中微子，它们的传播速度几乎与光一样快，但不经常相互作用，以及引力波，即由大质量物体引发的时空涟漪。 2017年，斯威夫特参与了背靠背的发现：两颗中子星合并引起的独特爆炸，然后第一个中微子追溯到它的起源。

paras.en: Since then, all efforts to observe light affiliated with a neutrino or gravitational-wave signal have come up empty. “We had these two really close together and then nothing since,” Evans says. “Which is frustrating, but also kind of fun.”
paras.zh: 从那时起，所有观测与中微子或引力波信号有关的光的努力都徒劳无功。埃文斯说：“我们两个人的关系非常密切，但从那以后就再也没有发生过。” “这令人沮丧，但也很有趣。”

paras.en: A range of current and future observatories will be able to take over some of Swift’s work, but not all of it. Even during the six months this year when Swift paused operations to prepare for the boost attempt, scientists felt its loss, says astrophysicist Judith Racusin of NASA Goddard. Racusin worked with Swift during its early years before turning her focus to NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, which launched in 2008 but boasts different strengths than its colleague. “We’re going to miss out,” she says of Swift’s loss. “Not just on the common events we have thousands of, but the really rare, unusual ones, which are often the ones we learn the most from.”
paras.zh: 当前和未来的一系列天文台将能够接管斯威夫特的部分工作，但不是全部。美国宇航局戈达德中心的天体物理学家朱迪思·拉库辛表示，即使在今年斯威夫特号暂停运行以准备助推尝试的六个月里，科学家们也感受到了损失。拉库辛早年曾与 Swift 合作，后来将重点转向美国宇航局的费米伽马射线太空望远镜，该望远镜于 2008 年发射，但拥有与其同事不同的优势。 “我们会错过的，”她谈到斯威夫特的损失时说道。 “不仅是我们有数以千计的常见事件，而且还有真正罕见、不寻常的事件，这些事件往往是我们学到最多的事件。”

paras.en: Mission personnel had Swift cram in as much science as possible as its demise approached. After the boost attempt was called off, the team turned Swift’s instruments back on for a scientific swan song. That included technical observations to ensure the utility of all its recent data, as well as indirect observations of Earth’s atmosphere at lower altitudes than many spacecraft are able to withstand. Swift even caught glimpses of a comet in its final weeks.
paras.zh: 在斯威夫特快要灭亡的时候，任务人员让斯威夫特灌输了尽可能多的科学知识。升压尝试被取消后，团队重新打开斯威夫特的仪器，谱写了一首科学的绝唱。其中包括确保其所有最新数据的实用性的技术观测，以及在比许多航天器能够承受的海拔更低的高度对地球大气层进行间接观测。斯威夫特甚至在最后几周瞥见了一颗彗星。

paras.en: And, of course, there were gamma-ray bursts. One particularly intriguing burst came in late September and was rather far away but remarkably energetic.
paras.zh: 当然，还有伽马射线暴。九月下旬发生了一次特别有趣的爆发，虽然距离相当远，但能量却非常大。

paras.en: “It feels a little bit like a last hurrah of Swift,” Racusin says of the event. “It’s a burst that we’ll be studying for some time, so I’m really glad we got Swift data on it while we could.”
paras.zh: “这感觉有点像斯威夫特的最后一次欢呼，”拉库辛谈到这次活动时说道。 “这是一个我们将研究一段时间的爆发，所以我真的很高兴我们能够尽可能地获得有关它的 Swift 数据。”

articles.title: ‘Exhumed’ recounts the true story of America’s first vampire
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: October is my favorite month. I love when the leaves change colors and the air gets brisk. My hunger for media that sends a shiver down my spine is at an all-time high. This spooky season, I found satiation in Exhumed, a new book by historian Aaron Mahnke.
paras.zh: 十月是我最喜欢的月份。我喜欢树叶变色、空气清新的感觉。我对媒体的渴望达到了历史最高点，这让我脊背发凉。在这个令人毛骨悚然的季节，我在历史学家亚伦·马恩克（Aaron Mahnke）的新书《挖掘》（Exhumed）中找到了满足。

paras.en: Mahnke draws on rich science-based history and folklore to show how fear of the unknown has shaped culture throughout history, even into the present day. He cites Taylor Swift, Twilight and other pop culture phenomena in his analysis — a choice that injects fresh air into the otherwise miasmic atmosphere. And thanks to Mahnke’s gripping prose, I felt like I was in the middle of the action. It was hard to lay the book down.
paras.zh: 马恩克利用丰富的基于科学的历史和民间传说来展示对未知的恐惧如何在整个历史中塑造文化，甚至到了今天。他在分析中引用了泰勒·斯威夫特、《暮光之城》和其他流行文化现象——这一选择为原本瘴气的气氛注入了新鲜空气。感谢马恩克扣人心弦的散文，我感觉自己仿佛置身于故事之中。很难放下书。

paras.en: Exhumed kicks off with the true story of America’s first “vampire.”
paras.zh: 《挖掘》以美国第一个“吸血鬼”的真实故事开始。

paras.en: Walk with me for a moment back in time to Exeter, Rhode Island in 1892. Rampant tuberculosis is killing scores of people, including three members of the Brown family: matriarch Mary and her daughters, Mary O. and Mercy L. Then a son, Edwin, falls ill with the same symptoms — sparking concern that one of the women is an undead vampire who is sucking his life away. The town exhumes the bodies.
paras.zh: 和我一起回到 1892 年罗德岛州埃克塞特。猖獗的结核病正在夺去数十人的生命，其中包括布朗家族的三名成员：女族长玛丽和她的女儿玛丽·O. 和梅西·L。然后，一个儿子埃德温也出现了同样的症状，引发了人们的担忧，其中一名妇女是一个正在吸走他生命的不死吸血鬼。镇上挖出了尸体。

paras.en: Mercy is surprisingly well-preserved. Her hair and nails appear longer and blood dribbles from her skin when it is pierced, “evidence” that confirms everyone’s worst fear: Mercy is indeed a vampire. (Nevermind that she perished in the dead of winter, when temperatures were probably cold enough to substantially slow decomposition.) The town burns Mercy’s heart, though it doesn’t save poor Edwin. These events helped inspire Bram Stoker’s Dracula, which was published five years later.
paras.zh: 令人惊奇的是，慈悲保存完好。她的头发和指甲显得更长，当皮肤被刺穿时，血液会从她的皮肤上滴下来，“证据”证实了每个人最担心的事情：梅西确实是一个吸血鬼。 （别介意她是在隆冬时节死去的，当时的气温可能足够冷，可以大大减缓分解速度。）这座小镇灼伤了梅西的心，尽管它并没有拯救可怜的埃德温。这些事件激发了布拉姆·斯托克的《德古拉》的灵感，该书于五年后出版。

paras.en: Interestingly, the cause of tuberculosis — a bacterium — was discovered a full decade before Mercy’s story unfolded. But news doesn’t always travel fast and entrenched beliefs can be difficult to change, even in the face of hard evidence. Exhumed explores this idea far beyond Mercy’s tragic tale.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，结核病的病因——一种细菌——在梅西的故事展开之前整整十年就被发现了。但消息并不总是传播得很快，即使面对确凿的证据，根深蒂固的信念也很难改变。 《挖掘》对这个想法的探索远远超出了梅西的悲剧故事。

paras.en: Fear has led people to do some extremely odd things by today’s standards: burning hearts to kill “vampires,” setting boobie-traps in graves to prevent the dead from rising or drinking the blood of freshly hanged men to “cure” epilepsy. Without modern science to explain the unexplained, people often filled in the blanks with stories, Mahnke explains.
paras.zh: 恐惧导致人们做出一些以今天的标准来看极其奇怪的事情：焚烧心脏来杀死“吸血鬼”，在坟墓中设置陷阱以防止死者复活，或者喝刚上吊的人的血来“治愈”癫痫。马恩克解释说，由于没有现代科学来解释无法解释的事情，人们常常用故事来填补空白。

paras.en: He implores readers to withhold judgement. After all, storytelling is one of the main ways that humans make sense of the world. “All of us, both then and now, are simply making the best of what we have, trying to find a way to improve our lives,” Mahnke writes.
paras.zh: 他恳请读者不要做出判断。毕竟，讲故事是人类理解世界的主要方式之一。 “我们所有人，无论是过去还是现在，都只是在充分利用我们所拥有的一切，试图找到一种方法来改善我们的生活，”马恩克写道。

paras.en: Perhaps this practice continues today in different shades.
paras.zh: 也许这种做法今天仍在以不同的方式延续着。

paras.en: At one point, eating mummies, or “mumia,” was considered cure-all for most ailments —headaches, stomach troubles and general sickness. Is it too far from the expectations some people have of buying a “health shot” from Whole Foods? Not really!
paras.zh: 曾几何时，吃木乃伊或“mumia”被认为能治愈大多数疾病——头痛、胃病和一般疾病。这与一些人从全食超市购买“健康疫苗”的期望相去甚远吗？并不真地！

paras.en: More than a century after Mercy Brown’s heart was incinerated, we’re still clinging to stories and rituals that offer us a sense of control over the thing we fear most: death. Exhumed makes it clear that we haven’t outrun this instinct, we’ve just given it different packaging.
paras.zh: 梅西·布朗的心脏被焚毁一个多世纪后，我们仍然坚持相信故事和仪式，这些故事和仪式让我们有一种控制我们最害怕的事情的感觉：死亡。 《挖掘》清楚地表明，我们并没有超越这种本能，我们只是给了它不同的包装。

paras.en: If you are the type of person who has 50 tabs open at any given moment, then you will appreciate Exhumed’s myriad quirky facts. Here are three of my favorites:
