paras.zh: 13 名受访者表示，他们预计最终利率，即日本央行预计停止紧缩周期的水平，将在 2027 年中期左右达到 1.75% 至 2%。

paras.en: Japan has been grappling with a weak yen and high energy prices that have pushed up inflation.
paras.zh: 日本一直在努力应对日元疲软和能源价格上涨推高通胀的问题。

paras.en: However, experts have told CNBC that CPI numbers are being held down by energy subsidies from the Takaichi administration.
paras.zh: 然而，专家告诉 CNBC，高市政府的能源补贴抑制了消费者物价指数 (CPI) 数据。

paras.en: The most recent inflation numbers for September revealed core inflation hit their highest level in 2026, coming in at 2.1% and overshooting expectations.
paras.zh: 9 月份最新通胀数据显示，核心通胀达到 2026 年最高水平，为 2.1%，超出预期。

paras.en: Earlier this month, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reportedly told parliament that Japan was "on the cusp of shifting to a period of sustained inflation driven by rising wages."
paras.zh: 据报道，本月早些时候，日本财务大臣片山五月向议会表示，日本“即将进入由工资上涨推动的持续通胀时期”。

paras.en: Japan's inflation-adjusted wages rose for the eighth month in a row in August, climbing 1.5% from a year earlier, according to the most recent government data, signaling potential wage-growth-driven inflation as well.
paras.zh: 根据最新的政府数据，日本8月份经通胀调整后的工资连续第八个月上涨，同比上涨1.5%，这也表明潜在的工资增长驱动的通胀。

paras.en: — CNBC's Lisa Kim contributed to this report.
paras.zh: — CNBC 的丽莎·金 (Lisa Kim) 对本报告作出了贡献。

articles.title: Biggest-ever crypto hack impacts $6.3 billion as Binance works to contain fallout

paras.en: Binance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses.
paras.zh: 币安周五表示，一次安全事件估计造成了 63 亿美元的影响，迄今为止已冻结了约 30 亿美元的加密货币资产，并承诺弥补所有损失。

paras.en: The world's largest crypto exchange said an initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions."
paras.zh: 全球最大的加密货币交易所表示，初步调查表明“安全事件可能涉及 DevOps 工程师的笔记本电脑，这使得攻击者能够访问服务容器并提交未经授权的提款交易。”

paras.en: Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls. It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours.
paras.zh: 币安联合创始人何一表示，存款未受影响并继续正常运行，同时该交易所正在努力增强提款服务和相关地址控制。预计将在未来 48 小时内开始恢复提款服务。

paras.en: The exchange said it would cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company funds, adding that customer funds remained safe.
paras.zh: 该交易所表示，将使用用户安全资产基金和公司资金来弥补所有损失，并补充说客户资金仍然安全。

paras.en: Binance also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, revoked the affected address authorization and enlisted law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover funds.
paras.zh: 币安还暂时暂停存款和取款，撤销受影响地址的授权，并聘请执法机构和区块链情报公司追踪和追回资金。

paras.en: The company said it would publish a technical report, and an updated Proof of Reserves after remediation efforts.
paras.zh: 该公司表示，将在修复工作后发布一份技术报告和更新的储备证明。

paras.en: "We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified," Binance said.
paras.zh: 币安表示：“我们没有发现任何钱包私钥泄露的证据。一旦调查完成且事实得到充分验证，我们将分享详细的技术事后分析。”

paras.en: The announcement followed moves by several crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group, Tether and Ripple, to freeze funds tied to the hack.
paras.zh: 在此之前，包括 Circle Internet Group、Tether 和 Ripple 在内的多家加密货币公司采取了冻结与黑客攻击相关的资金的行动。

paras.en: Bitcoin fell more than 4% to $77,994.96 on Friday as the hack weighed on crypto markets. Shares of Circle tumbled about 5% in after-hours trading on Thursday.
paras.zh: 由于黑客攻击给加密货币市场带来压力，周五比特币下跌超过 4% 至 77,994.96 美元。周四盘后交易中，Circle 股价下跌约 5%。

paras.en: "Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," a Binance spokesperson said. "Rest assured that user funds are completely safe." Binance also said on X that Binance Alpha trading had been temporarily suspended, and that "the current verified total frozen is $2.54 billion."
paras.zh: 币安发言人表示：“我们的团队已了解有关潜在安全问题的报告，并正在积极调查。” “请放心，用户资金是完全安全的。”币安还在 X 上表示，币安 Alpha 交易已暂时停止，“目前经核实的冻结总额为 25.4 亿美元”。

paras.en: Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Thursday evening in a social media post that the company had frozen more than 800 million in USD Coin associated with the incident. USDT stablecoin issuer Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino also said in on X that his firm had frozen more than 1.5 billion of its stablecoin that may have been related to a potential breach.
paras.zh: Circle 首席执行官杰里米·阿莱尔 (Jeremy Allaire) 周四晚上在社交媒体帖子中表示，该公司已冻结与该事件相关的超过 8 亿美元代币。 USDT 稳定币发行商 Tether 首席执行官 Paolo Ardoino 也在 X 上表示，他的公司已冻结了超过 15 亿美元的稳定币，这些稳定币可能与潜在的违规行为有关。

paras.en: Jack McDonald, Ripple's senior vice president of stablecoins, said it was actively freezing affected funds held in RLUSD, its U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin.
paras.zh: Ripple 稳定币高级副总裁 Jack McDonald 表示，该公司正在积极冻结以美元支持的稳定币 RLUSD 中持有的受影响资金。

paras.en: Later, Yi He said in a statement that the XRP and RLUSD-tied firm Ripple helped halt the movement of $200 million of funds linked to the possible attack.
paras.zh: 随后，Yi He 在一份声明中表示，与 XRP 和 RLUSD 相关的公司 Ripple 帮助阻止了与可能的攻击相关的 2 亿美元资金的流动。

paras.en: But those frozen funds could represent only part of those impacted. Crypto data provider Arkham Intelligence linked nearly $6 billion in digital assets — including bitcoin, ether, solana and various stablecoins — to 55 wallet addresses it has linked to the potential exploit.
paras.zh: 但这些被冻结的资金可能仅代表受影响资金的一部分。加密数据提供商 Arkham Intelligence 将近 60 亿美元的数字资产（包括比特币、以太币、solana 和各种稳定币）与其潜在漏洞相关的 55 个钱包地址关联起来。

paras.en: Arkham identifies, tracks and flags crypto wallets by analyzing publicly available blockchain data. It also solicits tips from its community members.
paras.zh: Arkham 通过分析公开的区块链数据来识别、跟踪和标记加密钱包。它还向社区成员征求建议。

paras.en: Exploits are not uncommon in the crypto space. In 2025, Bybit suffered roughly $1.5 billion in losses due to a hack. More recently, Bitget lost more than $350 million worth of digital assets in a cyber theft incident. Over the past several years, bad actors have also drained billions of dollars in crypto from decentralized exchanges.
paras.zh: 漏洞利用在加密货币领域并不罕见。 2025 年，Bybit 由于黑客攻击遭受了约 15 亿美元的损失。最近，Bitget 在一次网络盗窃事件中损失了价值超过 3.5 亿美元的数字资产。在过去的几年里，不良行为者还从去中心化交易所窃取了数十亿美元的加密货币。

articles.title: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory may have just discovered our solar system’s sixth dwarf planet

paras.en: Congratulations to Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake—there may be a new sibling to welcome into the dwarf planet family.
paras.zh: 恭喜冥王星、谷神星、阋神星、豪美亚和鸟神星——矮行星家族可能会迎来一个新的兄弟姐妹。

paras.en: On Tuesday astronomers at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory announced the discovery of a new dwarf planet candidate in a distant part of the solar system beyond Neptune’s orbit. The new object doesn’t have an official name yet and is instead going by its provisional designation—2026 ED138.
paras.zh: 周二，维拉·C·鲁宾天文台的天文学家宣布，在太阳系海王星轨道之外的遥远区域发现了一颗新的候选矮行星。新物体还没有正式名称，而是使用其临时名称 - 2026 ED138。

paras.en: The discovery was made by running billions of pieces of data collected by the Rubin Observatory through a search code developed by Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian astronomers Matthew Holman and Kevin Napier.
paras.zh: 这一发现是通过天体物理中心开发的搜索代码运行鲁宾天文台收集的数十亿条数据而得出的。哈佛和史密森尼天文学家马修·霍尔曼和凯文·纳皮尔。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “My first reaction was one of excited disbelief,” Holman said in a statement. “Objects like this are very rare, so I immediately started checking whether I or the code had done something wrong.”
paras.zh: “我的第一反应是兴奋和难以置信，”霍尔曼在一份声明中说。 “这样的对象非常罕见，所以我立即开始检查我或代码是否做错了。”

paras.en: When Holman and his colleague Mario Jurić of the University of Washington went to double-check, they found 30 more observations of the object by Rubin that dated to between March and July 2026. Looking at other observation tools, the pair found even more sightings going back to 2016. Together, these data allowed the astronomers to begin mapping out 2026 ED138’s orbit.
paras.zh: 当霍尔曼和他华盛顿大学的同事马里奥·尤里奇去仔细检查时，他们发现鲁宾在 2026 年 3 月至 7 月期间对该物体进行了另外 30 次观测。通过查看其他观测工具，两人发现了更多可以追溯到 2016 年的目击事件。总而言之，这些数据使天文学家能够开始绘制 2026 年 ED138 的轨道。

paras.en: The suspected dwarf planet is about 46 times as far from the sun as Earth, making it even more remote than Pluto, which is just 40 times as far. The object is also tilted off the solar system’s plane by around 25 degrees, an arrangement that could be linked to disruptions caused by Neptune’s gravitational pull.
paras.zh: 这颗疑似矮行星距太阳的距离约为地球距太阳的46倍，甚至比冥王星还要遥远，而冥王星的距离仅为地球的40倍。该物体还与太阳系平面倾斜约 25 度，这种排列可能与海王星引力造成的破坏有关。

paras.en: Initial measurements indicate that 2026 ED138 has a diameter between 600 and 1,500 kilometers (373 and 932 miles), which makes it one of the largest dwarf planet candidates yet detected. But size isn’t all that matters: further observations are required to determine if the object has enough mass to be pulled into a round shape, which is a key requirement for a dwarf planet.
paras.zh: 初步测量表明，2026 ED138 的直径在 600 至 1,500 公里（373 至 932 英里）之间，这使其成为迄今为止发现的最大候选矮行星之一。但大小并不是最重要的：需要进一步观察来确定该物体是否有足够的质量来被拉成圆形，这是矮行星的关键要求。

paras.en: Despite its size, 2026 ED138 was able to avoid detection for all these years because it’s located in a part of the night sky that’s crowded with stars whose light drowned it out. The Vera C. Rubin observatory, which is loaded with state-of-the-art, powerful instruments and only recently came online, made the discovery possible. Now that the object has been identified, astronomers can get to work on learning more about it to see if it can join Pluto and the others in the dwarf planet family.
paras.zh: 尽管体积巨大，2026 ED138 多年来仍能避免被发现，因为它位于夜空的一部分，那里挤满了星星，星星的光芒淹没了它。维拉·C·鲁宾天文台配备了最先进、功能强大的仪器，最近才投入使用，使这一发现成为可能。现在这个天体已经被识别出来，天文学家可以开始更多地了解它，看看它是否可以加入冥王星和其他矮行星家族。

paras.en: “If confirmed as a dwarf planet, ED138 would join a very small family of worlds,” Holman said. “Rubin will image the whole southern sky again and again for ten years, so any others hiding in the places earlier surveys skipped are now within reach.”
paras.zh: “如果被确认为矮行星，ED138 将加入一个非常小的世界家族，”霍尔曼说。 “鲁宾将在十年内一次又一次地拍摄整个南方天空，因此任何其他躲藏在先前调查跳过的地方的人现在都触手可及。”

articles.title: Can the world’s religions survive the existence of aliens?

paras.en: One of the greatest mysteries of life is whether we are alone in the cosmos. The laws of probability suggest we aren’t, but despite centuries of searching, we have never seen any clear evidence of life beyond our planet. Still, the world’s religious leaders are already formulating how they would respond to extraterrestrial life—and some have more interesting approaches than others.
paras.zh: 生命中最大的谜团之一是我们在宇宙中是否孤独。概率定律表明我们并非如此，但尽管经过几个世纪的探索，我们从未发现任何明显的地球以外存在生命的证据。尽管如此，世界宗教领袖已经在制定如何应对外星生命——其中一些人的方法比其他人更有趣。

paras.en: These discussions took center stage at a Capitol Hill gathering called the Disclosure Forum that took place earlier this year on a sunny day in June. A gaggle of lawmakers, retired military personnel, academics and businesspeople crowded into the Russell Senate Office Building’s Kennedy Caucus Room with me. As I listened, they spitballed ideas on how to handle what they believe are the increasingly likely chances of first contact with alien life.
paras.zh: 这些讨论成为今年早些时候六月阳光明媚的一天举行的国会山聚会的中心舞台，该聚会名为“信息披露论坛”。一群议员、退役军人、学者和商人和我一起挤进拉塞尔参议院办公楼的肯尼迪核心小组会议室。在我听着的时候，他们就如何处理他们认为首次接触外星生命的可能性越来越大的问题提出了一些想法。

paras.en: Several speakers at the event stressed that a revelation that Earth has been visited by intelligent extraterrestrials would raise immediate questions about planetary defense. Others theorized hopefully that there could be enormous economic opportunities.
paras.zh: 活动中的几位发言者强调，智慧外星人访问地球的消息将立即引发有关行星防御的问题。其他人则认为，这可能会带来巨大的经济机会。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: There would also be enormous societal impacts: Carlos Eire, a historian and religious studies professor at Yale University, told event attendees that finding out humanity isn’t alone in the universe could shake us to our very souls—religious leaders would need to contain the fallout, he said.
paras.zh: 这也会产生巨大的社会影响：耶鲁大学历史学家和宗教研究教授卡洛斯·艾尔(Carlos Eire)告诉活动与会者，发现人类在宇宙中并不孤单可能会震撼我们的灵魂——他说，宗教领袖需要控制其影响。

paras.en: Eire serves on the advisory board for the Disclosure Foundation, a nonprofit that organized the event and is dedicated to transparency around unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) and aliens.
paras.zh: Eire 是披露基金会 (Disclosure Foundation) 的顾问委员会成员，该基金会是一家非营利组织，组织了此次活动，致力于提高不明异常现象 (UAP) 和外星人的透明度。

paras.en: “If disclosure reveals that there are nonhuman intelligences,” Eire told me later in an interview, “it remains to be seen who these intelligences really are and what they do, or what they’re hoping to accomplish, with human beings.”
paras.zh: “如果披露的内容表明存在非人类智慧生物，”艾尔后来在一次采访中告诉我，“这些智慧生物到底是谁，他们做了什么，或者他们希望与人类一起完成什么，还有待观察。”

paras.en: “There won’t be a single reaction,” he adds. “For some people, it will confirm all sorts of things. For some people, it will demolish certain beliefs.”
paras.zh: “不会有任何反应，”他补充道。 “对于某些人来说，它将证实各种各样的事情。对于某些人来说，它将摧毁某些信念。”

paras.en: Reactions could be split along religious lines—and some belief systems may be better equipped to deal with aliens than others, experts say.
paras.zh: 专家表示，人们的反应可能会因宗教信仰而异，而某些信仰体系可能比其他信仰体系更适合应对外星人。

paras.en: For example, Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and other religions that originate in the Global East “have always conceived of the universe as vast, as going through many cycles of existence,” says Jeffery Long, a religious studies professor at Elizabethtown College.
paras.zh: 例如，印度教、佛教、耆那教和其他起源于全球东方的宗教“一直认为宇宙是广阔的，经历了许多存在的循环，”伊丽莎白敦学院宗教研究教授杰弗里·朗说。

paras.en: Hinduism, Long tells me, has many deities, some of whom are described in religious texts as traveling through the cosmos on “vimanas”—flying chariots that could, to some, be read as akin to spaceships.
paras.zh: 朗告诉我，印度教有许多神，其中一些神在宗教文本中被描述为乘坐“维曼纳斯”（vimanas）——一种飞行战车，对某些人来说可以理解为类似于宇宙飞船——穿越宇宙。

paras.en: “If you start reading ancient Hindu literature and about different deities and then other species of intelligent beings, it’s very sci-fi,” Long says.
paras.zh: “如果你开始阅读古代印度教文学，以及有关不同神灵和其他智慧生物的文献，那就非常科幻了，”朗说。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the Abrahamic religions—the largest of which are Christianity, Judaism and Islam—are largely accepting of the idea that conscious life might exist that isn’t human, but none of these religions are monoliths.
paras.zh: 与此同时，亚伯拉罕宗教——其中最大的是基督教、犹太教和伊斯兰教——在很大程度上接受这样的观点，即可能存在非人类的有意识生命，但这些宗教都不是铁板一块。

paras.en: The sheer scope of Christian belief systems makes attitudes to aliens among believers difficult to pin down, Eire says. Some theologians are optimistic: in his 2023 book Astrobiology and Christian Doctrine: Exploring the Implications of Life in the Universe, which received some NASA grant funding, Andrew Davison, now a divinity professor at the University of Oxford, wrote that he believes Christianity would be more “robust” in accepting alien life than some might think.
paras.zh: 艾尔说，基督教信仰体系的庞大范围使得信徒对外星人的态度很难确定。一些神学家持乐观态度：现为牛津大学神学教授的安德鲁·戴维森 (Andrew Davison) 在其 2023 年出版的《天体生物学和基督教教义：探索宇宙生命的影响》一书中写道，他相信基督教在接受外星生命方面比一些人想象的更加“稳健”。该书获得了美国宇航局的部分拨款资助。

paras.en: Certainly, leaders in the Roman Catholic Church have hinted at being open to extraterrestrials—the late Pope Francis once said he’d happily baptize an alien if they asked—Eire points out that within certain forms of Christianity, such as Protestantism, there can be incredible diversity in beliefs.
paras.zh: 当然，罗马天主教会的领导人已经暗示对外星人持开放态度——已故教皇方济各曾经说过，如果他们提出要求，他很乐意为外星人施洗——艾尔指出，在某些形式的基督教中，比如新教，信仰可能存在令人难以置信的多样性。

paras.en: “There are Bible-thumping antievolutionists in parts of the U.S. that call themselves Evangelicals, and there are Evangelicals that are damn close to Catholics,” Eire says. “Predicting what Protestants will do is just impossible. The spectrum is so wide and contains so many different kinds of Christianity.”
paras.zh: “在美国部分地区，有一些重读《圣经》的反进化论者自称福音派，也有一些福音派与天主教徒非常接近，”艾尔说。 “预测新教徒会做什么是不可能的。范围如此之广，包含如此多不同种类的基督教。”

paras.en: The Abrahamic religion that may be the most open-minded about aliens, Long says, is also the oldest. Jewish scripture, while making no mention of spaceships, does include repeated mention of angels with a higher consciousness than that of humans. Even the most devout followers would perhaps be accepting of aliens because the religion’s dogma is “more about ethics and living your life here and now than it’s about ‘if you do this, you’ll go to heaven,’” Long says.
paras.zh: 朗说，亚伯拉罕宗教可能是对外星人最开放的宗教，也是最古老的宗教。犹太圣经虽然没有提到宇宙飞船，但确实多次提到比人类具有更高意识的天使。即使是最虔诚的追随者也可能会接受外星人，因为该宗教的教条“更多的是关于道德和此时此地的生活，而不是‘如果你这样做，你就会去天堂’，”朗说。

paras.en: Academic explorations of how religious belief might influence attitudes to potential alien life are spotty at best, but that dearth of research could change. Aliens have become less taboo for scientists beyond astrobiology; the possibility of extraterrestrial life is no longer a punch line.
paras.zh: 关于宗教信仰如何影响对潜在外星生命的态度的学术探索充其量是参差不齐的，但研究的缺乏可能会改变。对于天体生物学以外的科学家来说，外星人已经不再是禁忌。外星生命的可能性不再是一句俏皮话。

paras.en: At the June Disclosure Forum, I heard more about how the White House is approaching the issue by setting up an advisory group on UAP, led by Harvard professor Avi Loeb. Loeb said at the event that he hopes the UAP Science Advisory Council will go on to publish scientific findings in reputable journals. That may include research in the field of exotheology—the study of religion and theological ideas related to alien life, Eire says.
paras.zh: 在 6 月的信息披露论坛上，我更多地了解到白宫如何通过设立由哈佛大学教授阿维·勒布 (Avi Loeb) 领导的 UAP 咨询小组来解决这一问题。勒布在活动中表示，他希望 UAP 科学咨询委员会继续在知名期刊上发表科学发现。艾尔说，这可能包括外星神学领域的研究——研究与外星生命有关的宗教和神学思想。

paras.en: “The academic community is readier now than it was 10 years ago for various reasons,” he says. Eire points to the Pentagon’s recent publishing of several tranches of previously classified UAP-related documents and media as a reason for this increased openness.
paras.zh: “由于各种原因，学术界现在比 10 年前做好了准备，”他说。 Eire 指出，五角大楼最近公布了几批先前机密的 UAP 相关文件和媒体，这是这种开放性增加的原因。

paras.en: As to whether a kind of spiritual malaise or panic might result from aliens revealing themselves, that’s unclear. According to one recent poll, a third of Americans believe at least some UAP sightings were actual spacecraft; another poll found about half the country believes aliens probably exist. But drilling down more formally into specific religions is more murky: A 2021 poll revealed that among U.S. Christians, people who said religion was very important to them were less likely to believe that intelligent life might exist on other planets, as were those who attended religious services at least weekly. Belief in alien life also varied by denomination.
paras.zh: 至于外星人的暴露是否会导致某种精神上的不适或恐慌，目前还不清楚。根据最近的一项民意调查，三分之一的美国人相信至少有一些 UAP 目击事件是真正的航天器；另一项民意调查发现，大约一半的人相信外星人可能存在。但更正式地深入研究特定宗教则更加模糊：2021 年的一项民意调查显示，在美国基督徒中，那些认为宗教对他们非常重要的人不太可能相信其他星球上可能存在智慧生命，那些至少每周参加宗教仪式的人也是如此。对外星生命的信仰也因教派而异。

paras.en: Much could also hinge on what kind of alien life is out there. While most people imagine intelligent beings that are in the best case friendly and curious like E.T., or, in the worst case, here to annihilate humanity, like in Independence Day, that’s not what most exobiologists are searching for. Instead they are on the lookout for distant exoplanets that exhibit signs of life closer to Earth’s microbes than humans.
paras.zh: 很大程度上还取决于那里存在什么样的外星生命。虽然大多数人想象的智能生物在最好的情况下是友好和好奇的，就像外星人一样，或者在最坏的情况下，在这里消灭人类，就像《独立日》一样，但这并不是大多数外星生物学家所寻找的。相反，他们正在寻找遥远的系外行星，这些行星表现出比人类更接近地球微生物的生命迹象。

paras.en: “If there was amoebalike life on other planets, that would be a significant thing,” says Shoaib Malik, a science and religion lecturer at the University of Edinburgh and co-editor of the book Islamic Theology and Extraterrestrial Life: New Frontiers in Science and Religion. But while microscopic life would “definitely show proof of concept,” Malik adds, it wouldn’t fundamentally shake people’s faith.
paras.zh: 爱丁堡大学科学与宗教讲师、《伊斯兰神学与外星生命：科学与宗教新前沿》一书的联合编辑肖伊布·马利克（Shoaib Malik）说：“如果其他行星上存在类似变形虫的生命，那将是一件意义重大的事情。”马利克补充道，虽然微观生命“肯定会证明概念”，但它不会从根本上动摇人们的信仰。

paras.en: “I think the real challenge really is if there’s something equivalent or something more advanced than the human being, particularly if you associate human uniqueness with rationality and spirituality,” Malik says.
paras.zh: 马利克说：“我认为真正的挑战是是否存在与人类相当或更先进的东西，特别是如果你将人类的独特性与理性和灵性联系起来。”

paras.en: Other scholars aren’t so sure. David Weintraub, a retired astronomer and author of Religions and Extraterrestrial Life: How Will We Deal With It?, says the difference between a microbe and, say, a primate is only a matter of degree.
paras.zh: 其他学者则不太确定。退休天文学家、《宗教与外星生命：我们将如何应对它？》一书的作者戴维·温特劳布 (David Weintraub) 表示，微生物和灵长类动物之间的区别只是程度问题。

paras.en: “I think it would only make a difference to someone who does not believe in evolution, and that’s where we start drilling into the religious aspect of this,” he says. “If you accept evolution as a natural part of the way the universe works, then if you find microbial life of any sort, a possibility exists that that microbial life could evolve into intelligent life someday.”
paras.zh: “我认为这只会对那些不相信进化论的人产生影响，这就是我们开始深入研究宗教方面的地方，”他说。 “如果你接受进化作为宇宙运作方式的自然组成部分，那么如果你发现任何类型的微生物生命，那么微生物生命有一天可能进化成智慧生命。”

paras.en: Although there are no direct comparisons of similar evolutionary situations arising in modern history, says Paul Gutjahr, a professor at Indiana University Bloomington and author of the book Faith in Space: American Religious Belief in Extraterrestrial Life, there are many examples in human history in which religion and new knowledge of the cosmos has collided. When evolution was an emerging theory, for example, it presented a major challenge to Christianity.
paras.zh: 印第安纳大学布卢明顿分校教授、《太空信仰：美国对外星生命宗教信仰》一书的作者保罗·古特亚尔表示，尽管现代历史中出现的类似进化情况没有直接比较，但人类历史上有很多宗教和宇宙新知识发生冲突的例子。例如，当进化论成为一种新兴理论时，它对基督教提出了重大挑战。

paras.en: “What you find is that people within that tradition find ways to adapt,” Gutjahr says. “It’s not like everybody becomes a friend of evolution, but there are there are very smart, capable and vocal people that start to think about if evolution is just the way that God worked his magic.”
paras.zh: “你会发现，处于这一传统的人们找到了适应的方法，”古特亚尔说。 “并不是每个人都成为进化论的朋友，但有些非常聪明、有能力、敢于发声的人开始思考进化论是否只是上帝施展魔法的方式。”

articles.title: Oldest known Mars rock is a ‘Rosetta stone’ for the Red Planet’s watery past

paras.en: In 2022 a group of nomadic meteorite hunters discovered a strange stone in the Sahara Desert. Called Teghaza 001, initial analysis by experts showed it was a meteorite from Mars. Now new research reveals it’s the oldest ever found, and it’s revealing more about the Red Planet’s complex history.
paras.zh: 2022 年，一群游牧陨石猎人在撒哈拉沙漠发现了一块奇怪的石头。专家初步分析显示，它是一颗来自火星的陨石，名为 Teghaza 001。现在，新的研究表明它是迄今为止发现的最古老的行星，并且揭示了更多关于这颗红色星球复杂历史的信息。

paras.en: Scientists fortunate enough to get their hands on samples of the space rock have been analyzing tiny pieces of Teghaza for years to better understand exactly what it is and when it formed. The new paper, published today in Science, identifies it as a piece of Mars’s crust that’s at least 4.1 billion years old, from a time when that world was warmer, wetter and more Earth-like.
paras.zh: 有幸获得太空岩石样本的科学家多年来一直在分析特加扎的微小碎片，以便更好地了解它是什么以及它何时形成。这篇今天发表在《科学》杂志上的新论文指出，它是火星地壳的一部分，至少有 41 亿年的历史，当时的世界更温暖、更湿润，也更像地球。

paras.en: “We’re holding a piece of a rock that’s dated even before the oldest Earth rock—a piece of Mars that’s so ancient, it existed when life had just started on Earth,” says Yang Liu, lead author of the study and a planetary scientist at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory at the California Institute of Technology.
paras.zh: 该研究的主要作者、加州理工学院喷气推进实验室的行星科学家杨刘说：“我们手上拿着的一块岩石的年代甚至早于最古老的地球岩石——一块非常古老的火星，当生命在地球上刚刚开始时它就已经存在了。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Several hundred Martian meteorites are known. All of them got here by giant impacts that have pelted Mars for eons, occasionally blasting bits of the planet into space, some of which by chance fall to Earth. Most are relatively young, each revealing little more than a snapshot from the most recent 600 million years or so of Mars’s 4.5-billion-year history. The only other known intact ancient sample, a meteorite discovered in Antarctica in the 1980s, is just 10 million years younger than Teghaza.
paras.zh: 已知有数百块火星陨石。它们都是通过巨大的撞击到达这里的，这些撞击已经撞击了火星数千年，偶尔会将地球的一些碎片炸入太空，其中一些偶然落到地球上。大多数都相对年轻，每一个都揭示了火星 45 亿年历史中最近 6 亿年左右的快照。唯一已知的完整古代样本是 20 世纪 80 年代在南极洲发现的陨石，它的年龄仅比 Teghaza 年轻 1000 万年。

paras.en: When Liu received a piece of the rock from the team at the University of New Mexico that initially analyzed it, she was tasked with studying its manganese, an element that can help scientists discern whether an ancient rock was ever exposed to water and oxidation. But soon she noticed the presence of zircons in the meteorite—tough crystalline minerals that can endure in rock for billions of years and contain radioactive isotopes that can be used for ultraprecise dating. The zircons, Liu realized, made Teghaza very special. In the exhaustive work that followed, she and her team isolated zircons and other minerals from small scraps of their precious samples, pinning down the meteorite’s chemical composition and dating its elements to the early days of Mars’s history.
paras.zh: 当刘从新墨西哥大学的团队收到一块岩石并对其进行初步分析时，她的任务是研究其中的锰，这种元素可以帮助科学家辨别古代岩石是否曾经暴露于水和氧化中。但很快她注意到陨石中存在锆石，这是一种坚韧的结晶矿物，可以在岩石中保存数十亿年，并且含有可用于超精确年代测定的放射性同位素。刘意识到，锆石让特加扎变得非常特别。在随后的详尽工作中，她和她的团队从珍贵样品的小碎片中分离出了锆石和其他矿物，确定了陨石的化学成分，并将其元素追溯到火星历史的早期。

paras.en: Teghaza, they found, is an igneous rock that formed from slowly-cooled magma and was once a piece of the planet’s crust. Comparing ratios of certain elements in the meteorite to those measured by orbiters for larger swaths of the planet’s surface, Liu and her team found the closest matches within the rugged, crater-pocked terrain in Mars’s southern highlands, a region thought to be among the world’s most ancient.
paras.zh: 他们发现，特加扎是一种由缓慢冷却的岩浆形成的火成岩，曾经是地球地壳的一部分。刘和她的团队将陨石中某些元素的比率与轨道飞行器在火星表面较大区域测量到的比率进行比较，在火星南部高地崎岖不平、布满陨石坑的地形中发现了最接近的匹配，该地区被认为是世界上最古老的地区之一。

paras.en: Pinpointing the possible sites where Teghaza was launched by a giant impact on its fateful journey to Earth is a feat all its own, but the meteorite’s chemical composition shows something even more enlightening.
paras.zh: 确定特加扎在其致命的地球之旅中因巨大撞击而发射的可能地点本身就是一项壮举，但陨石的化学成分显示出更具启发性的东西。

paras.en: As detailed in work from Liu’s team published earlier this year, some of the minerals in the meteorite have been aqueously altered—a sign that liquid water once percolated through Mars’s ancient mantle and crust. And careful analysis of remnant hydrogen trapped inside Teghaza shows that even when the rock formed, more than 4.1 billion years ago, the planet was already well on its way to losing most of its atmosphere, growing cold and transitioning to its current freeze-dried state. Taken together with the results in today’s paper, Liu says, all this reinforces how Mars’s mantle is likely more heterogeneous and complex than many planetary scientists have long assumed.
paras.zh: 正如刘团队今年早些时候发表的研究报告所详细描述的那样，陨石中的一些矿物质已经发生了水性改变——这表明液态水曾经渗透过火星古老的地幔和地壳。对特加扎内部残留氢的仔细分析表明，即使在 41 亿年前岩石形成时，这颗行星就已经开始失去大部分大气层，变得越来越冷，并转变为目前的冻干状态。刘说，与今天论文中的结果结合起来，所有这些都证明了火星地幔可能比许多行星科学家长期以来的假设更加异质和复杂。

paras.en: Liu’s research on Teghaza is ongoing; her team “has only scratched the surface,” she says, of the insights the meteorite might hold.
paras.zh: 刘对 Teghaza 的研究正在进行中；她说，她的团队对于陨石可能蕴含的见解“只触及了表面”。

paras.en: A clearer understanding of Mars’s deep past can also inform our own. Mars and Earth formed in similar ways, with giant magma oceans that cooled into cores, mantles and crusts. Because of its tectonic activity that continuously buries, melts and recycles the planet’s crust across geological time, Earth’s surface does not preserve many (if any) samples from its primordial youth—but Mars is different, as its geophysical tumults ebbed long ago.
paras.zh: 更清楚地了解火星的深层过去也可以为我们自己的过去提供信息。火星和地球的形成方式相似，都有巨大的岩浆海洋冷却成核心、地幔和地壳。由于其构造活动在整个地质时期不断地掩埋、融化和回收地壳，地球表面并没有保存许多（如果有的话）原始时期的样本——但火星不同，因为它的地球物理骚动很久以前就已经消退了。

paras.en: One reviewer of the paper called this meteorite “the Rosetta stone of Mars,” Liu says, because it may be able to tell the stories of planets across the solar system.
paras.zh: 刘说，该论文的一位审稿人称这块陨石为“火星的罗塞塔石碑”，因为它可能能够讲述整个太阳系行星的故事。

paras.en: “We’re hoping to start using Mars to compare and contrast and to understand what makes a planet habitable for life,” she adds.
paras.zh: “我们希望开始利用火星进行比较和对比，并了解是什么让一颗行星适合生命居住，”她补充道。

paras.en: There’s much still to learn about this meteorite’s mysteries, says Anya Udry, a planetary scientist at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, who was not involved with the Science study. But truly understanding the full story of Mars requires more than gathering additional impact-imported fragments of the Red Planet here on Earth; what’s necessary is more visits to the world itself.
paras.zh: 内华达大学拉斯维加斯分校的行星科学家安雅·乌德里（Anya Udry）并未参与这项科学研究，他表示，关于这颗陨石的奥秘还有很多有待了解。但真正了解火星的完整故事需要的不仅仅是在地球上收集这颗红色星球的额外撞击碎片；还需要更多的信息。必要的是更多地参观世界本身。

paras.en: “Mars is a complex planet, and this meteorite is really cool, but we don’t know exactly where it came from, so this is really another example of why we need to bring back samples,” she says.
paras.zh: “火星是一颗复杂的行星，这块陨石真的很酷，但我们不知道它到底来自哪里，所以这确实是我们需要带回样本的另一个例子，”她说。

articles.title: After the dinosaurs died, the massive ‘D. rex’ fungus ruled the woods
articles.author: Jake Buehler

paras.en: A pineapple-sized fungus has quietly grown undetected in the forests of southwestern China – until now. The massive mushroom may set a size record for a major branch of the fungal family tree.
paras.zh: 直到现在，一种菠萝大小的真菌在中国西南部的森林中悄然生长，未被发现。这种巨大的蘑菇可能会创下真菌家族树主要分支的大小记录。

paras.en: The fungus — named Dianjunus rex — may also represent a previously unknown family, researchers report September 28 in Frontiers in Fungal Biology. Fittingly, D. rex is part of a lineage that split off from other fungi right after the dinosaurs — like T. rex — went extinct.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 9 月 28 日在《真菌生物学前沿》上报道，这种名为 Dianjunus rex 的真菌也可能代表一个以前未知的家族。恰如其分的是，霸王龙是恐龙（如霸王龙）灭绝后立即从其他真菌中分离出来的谱系的一部分。

paras.en: In 2024, researchers in China were conducting a survey of fungal diversity in a tropical rainforest in Yunnan Province when local farmers tipped them off to an unusual fungus in the area. The farmers included photos, says Indunil Chinthani Senanayake, a mycologist at the Kunming Institute of Botany in China. Some of the farmers who’d made the discovery took a bite of the mystery fungus, Senanayake says, and the tipster “wanted to confirm whether it was edible or not.”
paras.zh: 2024 年，中国的研究人员正在对云南省热带雨林中的真菌多样性进行调查，当地农民向他们透露该地区有一种不寻常的真菌。中国昆明植物研究所的真菌学家 Indunil Chinthani Senanayake 说，农民们附上了照片。塞纳纳亚克说，发现这一神秘真菌的一些农民咬了一口，而消息提供者“想确认它是否可以食用”。

paras.en: When Senanayake and her colleagues went to the location, they found strange, yellowish, tentacle-like and spatula-like mushrooms growing out of decaying tree roots. These were some kind of ascomycete, or “sac fungi”. Sac fungi like morels, truffles and molds make their spores in microscopic bladderlike receptacles, unlike the bowling pin-shaped reproductive structures in club fungi, the group that includes most culinary mushrooms.
paras.zh: 当塞纳纳亚克和她的同事前往该地点时，他们发现腐烂的树根中长出了奇怪的、淡黄色的、触手状和铲状的蘑菇。这些是某种子囊菌，或“囊真菌”。羊肚菌、松露和霉菌等囊真菌在微观的囊状容器中产生孢子，这与俱乐部真菌（包括大多数烹饪蘑菇）的保龄球瓶形状的生殖结构不同。

paras.en: The mushrooms we see growing out of the ground are called fruiting bodies and make the spore-producing cells for the often hidden or subterranean fungus. Most sac fungi have relatively small fruiting bodies. But the mushrooms growing off these mysterious Yunnan fungi were enormous, with some reaching 50 centimeters tall. The team took samples of the fungi back to the lab for further study and found that they weighed up to 2.2 kilograms. By their estimates, these are the largest spore-making fruiting bodies among all sac fungi.
paras.zh: 我们看到的从地里长出来的蘑菇被称为子实体，它们为通常隐藏的或地下的真菌提供产孢细胞。大多数囊真菌的子实体相对较小。但这些神秘的云南真菌长出的蘑菇非常巨大，有些高达 50 厘米。研究小组将真菌样本带回实验室进行进一步研究，发现它们重达2.2公斤。据他们估计，这些是所有囊真菌中最大的产孢子实体。

paras.en: Torda Varga — a mycologist at the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew in Richmond, England who was not involved with the research — notes that some truffle species are known to get close to the bulk. D. rex appears to be the largest sac fungal fruiting body he’s aware of. “What I find particularly remarkable is that a fungus with such an enormous fruiting body appears to have remained scientifically undocumented until now,” says Varga, though he adds his experience has mostly been within Europe.
paras.zh: 英国里士满邱园皇家植物园的真菌学家托尔达·瓦尔加（Torda Varga）并未参与这项研究，他指出，已知某些松露品种的体积接近于块菌的体积。霸王龙似乎是他所知道的最大的囊真菌子实体。瓦尔加说：“我发现特别引人注目的是，迄今为止，具有如此巨大子实体的真菌似乎尚未在科学上得到记录。”不过他补充说，他的经历主要发生在欧洲。

paras.en: The researchers compared samples of the fungus’s DNA with those from other fungi to determine its evolutionary relationships. They found that it was a relative of species like candlesnuff fungus and dead-man’s-fingers, which make fruiting bodies only a few centimeters tall, but that it was probably in its own, unique family. The team gave the new species the name Dianjunus rex, referencing both the Latin “rex” for “king” and the ancient Dian kingdom of the region.
paras.zh: 研究人员将这种真菌的 DNA 样本与其他真菌的 DNA 样本进行了比较，以确定其进化关系。他们发现，它是烛鼻真菌和死人指等物种的近亲，这些物种的子实体只有几厘米高，但它可能属于自己独特的家族。研究小组将这个新物种命名为“Dianjunus rex”，既指拉丁语“rex”，意为“国王”，也指该地区的古滇王国。

paras.en: The team’s genetic analysis suggests D. rex’s family first evolved in the aftermath of the mass extinction at the end of the Cretaceous Period that wiped out the dinosaurs, some 65 million years ago. “During the dark, cold, postimpact years after the mass extinction, fungi that decompose dead organic matter could keep functioning better than light-dependent photosynthesizers,” Senanayake says.
paras.zh: 该团队的基因分析表明，霸王龙家族首次进化是在大约 6500 万年前的白垩纪末期恐龙大灭绝之后。 Senanayake 说：“在大灭绝发生后的黑暗、寒冷和撞击后的几年里，分解死亡有机物的真菌可以比依赖光的光合作用器继续更好地发挥作用。”

paras.en: Varga wonders if searching databases for bits of DNA shed into the environment could help uncover other members of D. rex’s royal family in the absence of physical specimens.
paras.zh: 瓦尔加想知道，在数据库中搜索流失到环境中的 DNA 片段是否有助于在缺乏实物标本的情况下发现霸王龙王室的其他成员。

paras.en: “Some of these [genetic] sequences might belong to previously undocumented relatives of Dianjunus rex,” he says. Finding these hidden species could tell researchers more about the biology and evolutionary history of this king of the sac fungi.
paras.zh: “其中一些[遗传]序列可能属于以前未记录的Dianjunus rex亲戚，”他说。发现这些隐藏的物种可以让研究人员更多地了解这种囊真菌之王的生物学和进化历史。

articles.title: Roller coaster safety is a matter of science
articles.author: Lindsay Lee Wallace

paras.en: The first roller coaster in the United States to loop upside down tucked riders by twos into bench seats, secured them with a single seat belt and subjected them to an estimated 7.5 times the force of gravity (some say it was closer to 12 g). The Flip Flap Railway opened in New York City’s Sea Lion Park in 1895, where the roller coaster reportedly strained backs, wrenched necks and dazzled spectators until the park closed in 1902.
paras.zh: 美国第一座倒转的过山车将乘客两人一组塞进长椅上，用一条安全带将他们固定，并让他们承受估计 7.5 倍的重力（有人说接近 12 克）。 Flip Flap 铁路于 1895 年在纽约市的海狮公园投入运营，据报道，这座过山车曾让游客扭伤背部、扭断脖子，让观众眼花缭乱，直到公园于 1902 年关闭。

paras.en: Now, roller coaster safety is in the news again. In September, three lawsuits were filed against Six Flags and ride manufacturer S&S Global, alleging that riders sustained “catastrophic” brain injuries on the roller coaster X2 at California’s Magic Mountain theme park. These are just the most recent cases related to the ride, filed after a CNN investigation found dozens of injuries on X2 leading to hospitalization, disability and death. On September 29, Six Flags announced X2 would shut down permanently even though it said the ride “consistently passed a multitude of safety tests.”
paras.zh: 现在，过山车安全再次成为新闻焦点。 9 月份，针对六旗游乐设施和游乐设施制造商 S&S Global 提起了三起诉讼，指控乘客在加州魔术山主题公园的 X2 过山车上遭受“灾难性”脑损伤。这些只是与该游乐设施相关的最新案件，CNN 调查发现 X2 上有数十人受伤，导致住院、残疾和死亡。 9 月 29 日，六旗宣布 X2 将永久关闭，尽管该游乐设施“始终通过了多项安全测试”。

paras.en: Weeks later, the company said it would temporarily close another nine coasters across the United States and Canada after a man fell from his seat on the roller coaster Goliath and died at Six Flags Over Georgia. Six Flags announced Oct. 24 that it would add seat belts to Goliath and other coasters, and a spokesperson told Science News that the company is “committed to rigorous ride inspection, maintenance and safety procedures.” But the incidents and closures are prompting new questions about coaster design and safety — particularly when they are operating correctly — and whether guidelines overlook crucial factors.
paras.zh: 几周后，该公司表示，在佐治亚六旗游乐园的“歌利亚”过山车上一名男子从座位上坠落身亡后，该公司将暂时关闭美国和加拿大的另外九个过山车。六旗乐园于 10 月 24 日宣布，将为歌利亚和其他过山车添加安全带，发言人告诉《科学新闻》，该公司“致力于严格的游乐设施检查、维护和安全程序”。但这些事件和关闭引发了有关过山车设计和安全的新问题——特别是当它们正确运行时——以及指导方针是否忽视了关键因素。

paras.en: Roller coasters are not regulated at the federal level in the United States; each state has its own approach to their management. But an international technical group comprising over 1,000 industry professionals, the ASTM Committee F24 on Amusement Rides and Devices, publishes recommendations that are considered industry standards.
paras.zh: 过山车在美国不受联邦层面的监管；每个州都有自己的管理方法。但由 1,000 多名行业专业人士组成的国际技术团体——ASTM 游乐设施和设备委员会 F24，发布了被视为行业标准的建议。

paras.en: The first ASTM standards for roller coaster design were released in 1982. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission had been stripped of authority to regulate fixed-site amusement rides the year before. In the wake of this newfound freedom, it was a “roller coaster arms race,” says Brian Avery, an event and tourism management researcher at the University of Florida in Gainesville who studies risk and amusement ride safety protocols. The period was characterized by attempts to “build it taller, faster, longer.”
paras.zh: 第一个过山车设计 ASTM 标准于 1982 年发布。前一年，美国消费品安全委员会被剥夺了监管固定场所游乐设施的权力。佛罗里达大学盖恩斯维尔分校的活动和旅游管理研究员布莱恩·艾弗里（Brian Avery）研究风险和游乐设施安全协议，他说，在这种新获得的自由之后，这是一场“过山车军备竞赛”。这一时期的特点是试图“把它建得更高、更快、更长”。

paras.en: When X2, originally called X, opened in 2002, it was the world’s first fourth-dimension coaster. It catapulted people 60 meters high, traveling 122 kilometers per hour while its seats rotated independently on their own tracks. In the 24 years since, only 20 or so other fourth-dimension coasters have been built, and several have closed.
paras.zh: X2（最初称为 X）于 2002 年开放时，是世界上第一个第四维度过山车。它将人弹射到 60 米高的地方，以每小时 122 公里的速度行驶，而其座椅则在自己的轨道上独立旋转。此后的 24 年里，只建造了大约 20 个四维过山车，其中有几个已经关闭。

paras.en: As roller coasters grew more extreme, injuries increased and were more publicized, sparking calls for further research and regulation.
paras.zh: 随着过山车变得越来越极端，伤害增加并且更加公开，引发了进一步研究和监管的呼声。

paras.en: Generally, roller coasters are quite safe. Out of 1.7 billion annual amusement park rides across North America, just 652 roller coaster injuries were reported in 2024 by parks choosing to share data. Studies suggest that riding a roller coaster is very unlikely to cause a brain injury, although most research on roller coaster brain impacts is about a decade or more old.
paras.zh: 一般来说，过山车是相当安全的。 2024 年，在北美每年 17 亿次的游乐园游乐设施中，选择共享数据的公园仅报告了 652 起过山车受伤事件。研究表明，乘坐过山车不太可能导致脑损伤，尽管大多数关于过山车大脑影响的研究已有十年或更久的历史。

paras.en: In 2002, a study used reported g forces from three roller coasters in a mathematical model to determine that their acceleration levels were below those predicted to cause head injuries. A 2017 study found brain effects on three roller coasters that were low on average, but “comparable with mild sports impacts,” like those sustained by heading a soccer ball, at their peak.
paras.zh: 2002 年，一项研究在数学模型中使用报告的三个过山车的重力来确定它们的加速度水平低于预计会导致头部受伤的水平。 2017 年的一项研究发现，三座过山车对大脑的影响平均较低，但“与轻度运动影响相当”，比如在巅峰时期头球足球所带来的影响。

paras.en: “The limiting of g forces alone might be an insufficient design criterion for roller coaster rides,” wrote the authors of the 2017 study.
paras.zh: 2017 年研究的作者写道：“仅对重力进行限制可能不足以构成过山车游乐设施的设计标准。”

paras.en: In 2020, David Eager, a biomechanical engineer at the University of Technology Sydney, coauthored a paper on under-acknowledged forces affecting roller coaster safety, including jerk (the rate at which acceleration changes), snap (the rate at which jerk changes) and vibration.
paras.zh: 2020 年，悉尼科技大学生物力学工程师 David Eager 与人合着了一篇论文，内容涉及影响过山车安全的未被充分认识的力，包括加加速度（加速度变化的速率）、折断（加加速度变化的速率）和振动。

paras.en: “Roller coaster passengers need time to sense acceleration changes and adjust their muscle tension or suffer conditions such as whiplash,” Eager wrote.
paras.zh: “过山车乘客需要时间来感知加速度的变化并调整他们的肌肉张力，否则就会遭受颈部扭伤等情况，”伊格写道。

paras.en: The ASTM standards are exacting in some ways. Research conducted during the space race led to a 6g recommended limit on roller coaster acceleration exposure. However, ASTM doesn’t make recommendations about other types of motion on a roller coaster that might impact the neck, head and brain. It disregards forces lasting less than 200 milliseconds, no matter how intense.
paras.zh: ASTM 标准在某些方面非常严格。太空竞赛期间进行的研究建议将过山车加速暴露限制为 6 克。然而，ASTM 并未对过山车上可能影响颈部、头部和大脑的其他类型的运动提出建议。它忽略持续时间少于 200 毫秒的力，无论强度如何。

paras.en: But each tiny imperfection and variation in the circumference of the track — especially plentiful in coasters built before modern manufacturing techniques — causes a jolt, says Jurnan Schilder, a mechanical engineer and researcher who teaches roller coaster design at the University of Twente in Enschede, the Netherlands. He studies ways to create smoother roller coaster rides.
paras.zh: 但在荷兰恩斯赫德特文特大学教授过山车设计的机械工程师兼研究员朱尔南·希尔德 (Jurnan Schilder) 表示，轨道周长的每一个微小缺陷和变化（尤其是在现代制造技术之前制造的过山车中大量存在）都会引起震动。他研究如何创造更平稳的过山车游乐设施。

paras.en: Schilder’s research suggests that at each track imperfection, “theoretically, you experience infinite jerk.” On a fourth-dimension coaster, he says, two sets of tracks mean double the variations. “Not only is the train sometimes shaking, but also the tilting mechanism is shaking.”
paras.zh: 希尔德的研究表明，在每条赛道不完美的情况下，“理论上，你都会经历无限的颠簸。”他说，在第四维过山车上，两组轨道意味着双倍的变化。 “不仅火车有时会晃动，而且倾斜机构也在晃动。”

paras.en: Research beyond rides also suggests intense and repeated rattling, jostling and vibration could meaningfully impact the brain. The U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration recommends limiting the duration and intensity of whole-body vibration. In April, the Virginia Tech Helmet Lab, which studies the science of brain injuries, published an article suggesting some concussions experienced by baseball players may result from just milliseconds of vibration.
paras.zh: 游乐设施之外的研究还表明，强烈且重复的嘎嘎声、推挤和振动可能会对大脑产生有意义的影响。美国职业安全与健康管理局建议限制全身振动的持续时间和强度。今年四月，研究脑损伤科学的弗吉尼亚理工大学头盔实验室发表了一篇文章，指出棒球运动员经历的一些脑震荡可能是由几毫秒的振动引起的。

paras.en: North Carolina high school student Kayleigh Bonner’s quest to understand her father’s death exposed similar risks. After her father, a retired U.S. Coast Guard surfman who captained boats through rough waves for 21 years, experienced symptoms of a brain injury and died by suicide, Kayleigh surveyed 77 other elite surfmen for a senior capstone project. She found that 89 percent of those she spoke to had some symptoms of brain injury likely caused by the intense, rapidly changing forces traveling through their bodies as their boats were tossed by waves. Her quest to understand her father’s death was written about in July in the New York Times, and soon after acknowledged by the Coast Guard.
paras.zh: 北卡罗来纳州高中生凯莉·邦纳（Kayleigh Bonner）试图了解父亲的死因，也面临着类似的风险。凯莉的父亲是一位退休的美国海岸警卫队冲浪运动员，曾在汹涌的海浪中驾驶船只长达 21 年，出现脑损伤症状并自杀身亡。凯莉为一项高级顶点项目对其他 77 名精英冲浪运动员进行了调查。她发现，在与她交谈的人中，89% 的人都有一些脑损伤症状，这可能是由于船只被海浪颠簸时，强烈、快速变化的力量穿过他们的身体而引起的。七月，《纽约时报》报道了她对父亲之死的了解，不久之后就得到了海岸警卫队的承认。

paras.en: Of course, professional baseball players and Coast Guard surfmen have more significant and prolonged exposure to these forces than occasional roller coasters riders. But as researchers discover more about how different kinds of motion impact the brain, safety standards seem to lag behind. Minimizing jerk and snap is “an important consideration,” Eager says.
paras.zh: 当然，职业棒球运动员和海岸警卫队冲浪者比偶尔乘坐过山车的人更长时间地接触这些力量。但随着研究人员更多地了解不同类型的运动如何影响大脑，安全标准似乎落后了。伊格说，最大限度地减少冲击和折断是“一个重要的考虑因素”。

paras.en: The mounting roller coaster-related headlines have renewed scrutiny of both the existing coaster safety standards and the lack of federal regulation. U.S. Rep. André Carson, a Democrat from Indiana, has called to pass a bill he first introduced in 2025 that would create federal oversight of amusement rides. Since 1999, Democratic U.S. Sen. Ed Markey of Massachusetts has repeatedly introduced legislation to regulate fixed rides, but the bills have consistently stalled.
paras.zh: 越来越多的与过山车相关的头条新闻重新引发了对现有过山车安全标准和缺乏联邦监管的审查。来自印第安纳州的民主党众议员安德烈·卡森 (André Carson) 呼吁通过他于 2025 年首次提出的一项法案，该法案将对游乐设施实行联邦监管。自1999年以来，马萨诸塞州民主党参议员埃德·马基多次提出监管固定游乐设施的立法，但这些法案一直停滞不前。

paras.en: The amusement industry has long opposed federal oversight. In 2010, Avery coauthored a paper asserting that “the industry needs to find a collective voice and establish consistent self‐regulating policies in order to curb the incidents rates and avoid federal regulation.”
paras.zh: 娱乐业长期以来一直反对联邦监管。 2010 年，艾弗里与人合着了一篇论文，声称“该行业需要找到集体声音并建立一致的自我监管政策，以控制事故发生率并避免联邦监管。”

paras.en: But Schilder says: “It makes you wonder: Are the current safety standards sufficient?”
paras.zh: 但席尔德说：“这让你想知道：当前的安全标准是否足够？”

paras.en: For modern rides, Schilder says he believes they are. Modern manufacturing techniques mean roller coasters designed and built today are much smoother than predecessors. ASTM standards that filter out brief but intense forces, like vibration and jerk, are likely fine for rides that don’t vibrate and jerk very much. But at many parks, the ambitious and intense rides born of the roller coaster arms race are still in place.
paras.zh: 对于现代游乐设施，席尔德说他相信它们是这样的。现代制造技术意味着今天设计和制造的过山车比以前的过山车要平稳得多。 ASTM 标准可以过滤掉短暂但强烈的力，例如振动和冲击力，对于振动和冲击力不大的游乐设施来说可能很好。但在许多公园里，过山车军备竞赛所带来的雄心勃勃和激烈的游乐设施仍然存在。

paras.en: Riders are “flirting, if you would, with danger when they experience rides and devices. They know that they’re more likely than not going to be safe,” Avery says. The point is to be “right on the cusp.”
paras.zh: 乘客“在体验游乐设施和设备时，如果你愿意的话，就是在与危险调情。他们知道自己更有可能是安全的，”艾弗里说。关键是要“处于风口浪尖”。

articles.title: How brain implants turn thoughts into speech
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: Casey Harrell lost his voice to ALS or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. As a volunteer in a clinical trial, he’s helping scientists test a brain-computer interface. Electrode arrays that are implanted in Casey’s brain send signals to nearby computers, where those signals are translated into words he intended to say.
paras.zh: 凯西·哈雷尔 (Casey Harrell) 因肌萎缩侧索硬化症 (ALS) 或肌萎缩侧索硬化症而失声。作为临床试验的志愿者，他正在帮助科学家测试脑机接口。植入凯西大脑中的电极阵列向附近的计算机发送信号，这些信号被翻译成他想说的话。

paras.en: Casey uses this system every day to talk with his wife, daughter, friends and work colleagues. The moment he realized that it worked was “pure joy,” Casey says. Even though the researchers scripted his words for that first test, “it was a profound moment,” he says. “The possibilities for the near future for me and the rest of humanity were overwhelming to realize.”
paras.zh: 凯西每天都使用这个系统与他的妻子、女儿、朋友和同事交谈。凯西说，当他意识到它起作用的那一刻，他感到“纯粹的喜悦”。尽管研究人员为第一次测试编写了他的话，但“这是一个意义深远的时刻，”他说。 “对我和其他人来说，不久的将来的可能性是难以想象的。”

paras.en: This episode of The Deep End: Talk to Me follows Casey and the fast-moving neuroscience that enables him to speak.
paras.zh: 这一集《深渊：跟我说话》讲述了凯西和快速发展的神经科学，使他能够说话。

paras.en: Patients paralyzed from the neck down can manipulate robotic arms with their thoughts. The woman in this video is controlling a robot with her mind. The so-called BrainGate system relies on a sensor of electrodes implanted in the motor cortex of the brain. Researchers hope by implanting electrodes in the brain it can read the brain signals meant to move the muscles involved in speaking, and translate the person’s intention to speak into comprehensive speech produced by a computer.
paras.zh: 颈部以下瘫痪的患者可以用意念操纵机械臂。视频中的女人正在用意念控制机器人。所谓的 BrainGate 系统依赖于植入大脑运动皮层的电极传感器。研究人员希望通过在大脑中植入电极，它可以读取大脑信号，从而移动参与说话的肌肉，并将人的说话意图转化为计算机产生的综合语音。

paras.en: Laura Sanders: Controlling things with your mind. It sounds like science fiction, but it’s definitely real. Today, we’re going to explore what it’s like to communicate with a brain implant that decodes your thoughts and turns them into words.
paras.zh: 劳拉·桑德斯：用意念控制事物。这听起来像是科幻小说，但它绝对是真实的。今天，我们将探索与大脑植入物进行交流的感觉，该植入物可以解码你的想法并将其转化为语言。

paras.en: [voices] Hey mom, can I tell you something? The voice is absolutely an integral part of your identity. Hello? That added layer of it being you. Do you want to talk? Your voice. Hi. Your voice is you.
paras.zh: [声音] 嘿妈妈，我可以告诉你一件事吗？声音绝对是您身份的一个组成部分。你好？那增加的一层就是你。你想说话吗？你的声音。你好。你的声音就是你。

paras.en: Sanders: From Science News, I’m Laura Sanders, and this is The Deep End, Talk to Me. Okay, so what is BrainGate? It’s an experimental system that connects electrodes that are implanted in a person’s brain to a nearby computer. It’s called a brain-computer interface, or BCI. The goal here is big: to help people with paralysis or brain injuries or missing limbs regain control over their world.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：来自《科学新闻》，我是劳拉·桑德斯，这里是《深渊》，跟我谈谈。好的，那么 BrainGate 是什么？这是一个实验系统，将植入人大脑的电极连接到附近的计算机。它被称为脑机接口（BCI）。这里的目标很远大：帮助瘫痪、脑损伤或肢体缺失的人重新掌控自己的世界。

paras.en: Leigh Hochberg: BrainGate clinical trials have now been going on for nearly 22 years. It’s 21 point something at the moment.
paras.zh: Leigh Hochberg：BrainGate 临床试验现已进行了近 22 年。现在是 21 点。

paras.en: Sanders: Leigh Hochberg is the director of the BrainGate Consortium and Clinical Trials. He also has a job at Massachusetts General Hospital, Brown University and the VA.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：Leigh Hochberg 是 BrainGate 联盟和临床试验的主管。他还在马萨诸塞州总医院、布朗大学和退伍军人管理局工作。

paras.en: Hochberg: People who may have had a brainstem stroke and suddenly lost the ability both to move and to speak, or for somebody with ALS who is progressively losing the ability to move or to speak, there’s long been a hope that particularly implantable brain-computer interfaces could restore communication and could restore mobility.
paras.zh: Hochberg：对于可能患有脑干中风并突然失去移动和说话能力的人，或者对于逐渐失去移动或说话能力的 ALS 患者，长期以来人们一直希望特别植入的脑机接口可以恢复沟通并恢复活动能力。

paras.en: Sanders: In 2004, a BrainGate device was implanted into a person’s brain for the very first time. That person was a man named Matthew Nagle, and he had been paralyzed in an accident. With BrainGate, he could control a computer cursor with his thoughts. Here’s a 2008 report from IT World.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：2004 年，BrainGate 设备首次被植入人的大脑中。那个人名叫马修·内格尔，他在一次事故中瘫痪了。有了 BrainGate，他可以用意念控制电脑光标。这是 IT World 2008 年的报告。

paras.en: Technology gave him hope. He was one of four testing BrainGate, a new technology where a chip is implanted in the brain that picks up electrical impulses. A computer then interprets those impulses as actions.
paras.zh: 科技给了他希望。他是测试 BrainGate 的四人之一，这是一项新技术，将芯片植入大脑中以接收电脉冲。然后计算机将这些冲动解释为动作。

paras.en: Hochberg: Those early studies have been really encouraging, and I think speaks to the potential for the field.
paras.zh: Hochberg：这些早期研究确实令人鼓舞，我认为这说明了该领域的潜力。

paras.en: Sanders: Over the years, there’s been amazing examples of people using BrainGate. People have used it to click around on the internet, play video games, one woman who was paralyzed was even able to drink a cinnamon latte with a robotic arm.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：多年来，人们使用 BrainGate 的例子层出不穷。人们用它来上网、玩电子游戏，一位瘫痪的妇女甚至可以用机械臂喝一杯肉桂拿铁。

paras.en: Hochberg: And she was able to think about using her own arm and reach out with a robotic arm and pick up that thermos and bring it to her mouth, and tip it towards her mouth, and then put the straw in her mouth and then to take that sip. And while it wasn’t the first time in nearly 15 years that she had had something to drink, it was the first time that she was really able to do so solely of her own volition. I remember the smile on her face when she did that.
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格：她能够考虑使用自己的手臂，用机械臂伸出来，拿起保温瓶，将其送到她的嘴边，然后将其朝她的嘴倾斜，然后将吸管放入她的嘴里，然后喝一口。虽然这不是近 15 年来她第一次喝东西，但这是她第一次真正能够完全按照自己的意愿喝东西。我记得她这样做时脸上的笑容。

paras.en: Sanders: Over the decades, BrainGate has had a lot of research success in a lot of ways. But what about talking? Hochberg says that when it comes to decoding speech, the science here is still very, very young.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：几十年来，BrainGate 在很多方面取得了很多研究成功。但是说话呢？霍赫伯格说，在解码语音方面，这门科学还非常非常年轻。

paras.en: Hochberg: We are at early days, just to be super clear. This is the very beginning of this field. There are only a small handful of people in the world who have had any type of implantable BCI that has been decoding speech.
paras.zh: Hochberg：我们还处于早期阶段，需要非常明确。这是这个领域的开始。世界上只有极少数人拥有任何类型的可解码语音的植入式脑机接口。

paras.en: Sanders: Where does the science stand when it comes to decoding the intention to talk? In the past few episodes, we’ve heard the stories of people who have lost their ability to speak. One of those people was Casey Harrell, and Casey also happens to have a BrainGate device implanted in his brain.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在解读谈话意图方面，科学处于什么位置？在过去的几集中，我们听到了失去说话能力的人的故事。其中之一就是凯西·哈雷尔（Casey Harrell），而凯西的大脑中也恰好植入了 BrainGate 设备。

paras.en: Casey Harrell: My name is Casey Harrell and I am 47 years old.
paras.zh: 凯西·哈雷尔：我叫凯西·哈雷尔，今年 47 岁。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey wakes up in the morning, and plugs in.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西早上醒来，然后接通电源。

paras.en: Casey: The first thing I will usually do after getting out of bed is to plug into the Matrix, so to speak.
paras.zh: Casey：可以这么说，我起床后通常要做的第一件事就是插入 Matrix。

paras.en: Sanders: By that, he means attaching two wires to two pedestals that come out of the top of his head. These two black wires then snake down to nearby computers. Collectively, these electrodes in Casey’s brain, wires from his head, and computers are called the BrainGate 2 neural interface system. So Casey gets it all fired up and then he’s off.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他的意思是，将两根电线连接到从他头顶伸出的两个基座上。然后这两根黑线蜿蜒连接到附近的计算机。凯西大脑中的这些电极、来自他头部的电线和计算机统称为 BrainGate 2 神经接口系统。所以凯西把一切都点燃了，然后他就出发了。

paras.en: Casey: Unless I have a medical appointment or something that will move me out of the house, I will sit in this position for most of the day, with specifically small breaks in between.
paras.zh: 凯西：除非我有医疗预约或需要离开家的事情，否则我会在一天的大部分时间里保持这个姿势，中间会有特别小的休息时间。

paras.en: Sanders: All the while, Casey is generating brain signals as he thinks about saying words. These are small, precise electrical pulses made by Casey’s neurons, specifically the cells in his speech motor cortex. Remember how we learned there are over 100 muscles that are involved in speech? These are the parts of the brain that control those muscles.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西在思考说话时一直在产生大脑信号。这些是由凯西的神经元（特别是他的言语运动皮层中的细胞）发出的小而精确的电脉冲。还记得我们是如何了解到有超过 100 块肌肉参与言语的吗？这些是控制这些肌肉的大脑部分。

paras.en: Casey: I am using a decoder for about ten to 14 hours a day, seven days a week, for the past almost two years, making me the world’s biggest power user of the brain-to-computer interface known to man.
paras.zh: 凯西：在过去的近两年里，我每周 7 天、每天使用解码器大约 10 到 14 个小时，这使我成为世界上人类已知的脑机接口的最大用户。

paras.en: Sanders: Like Jules, Casey has ALS. The disease has slowly taken away his ability to move and to talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：像朱尔斯一样，凯西也患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症。这种疾病慢慢地剥夺了他行动和说话的能力。

paras.en: Casey: I began to lose my ability to talk shortly after my diagnosis in 2020. Then it became a slow motion car crash of multiple years before almost no one would be able to understand me.
paras.zh: 凯西：2020年确诊后不久，我就开始失去说话的能力。然后，这变成了一场长达数年的慢动作车祸，直到几乎没有人能够理解我。

paras.en: By the time of my surgery, only my assistant and my wife, Levana, could really understand me fully. A few other friends who were around often would be able to understand some of what I was saying. I relied upon my assistant and my wife to basically serve as my translators to other people. I did not go anywhere, even a video call without them, either one or both.
paras.zh: 在我接受手术时，只有我的助手和我的妻子莱瓦娜（Levana）能够真正完全理解我。其他一些经常在附近的朋友应该能够理解我在说什么。我基本上依靠我的助手​​和我的妻子充当我向其他人提供翻译的工作。我没有去任何地方，甚至在没有他们的情况下进行视频通话，无论是其中一个还是两个。

paras.en: Sanders: In July of 2023, Casey volunteered for a clinical trial called BrainGate 2. A UC Davis neurosurgeon put four small electrical arrays onto the left side of Casey’s brain. I wanted to know more about how these arrays worked, so I talked to the neurosurgeon who put Casey’s devices into his brain.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：2023 年 7 月，凯西自愿参加了一项名为 BrainGate 2 的临床试验。加州大学戴维斯分校的神经外科医生在凯西的左侧大脑上放置了四个小型电子阵列。我想更多地了解这些阵列是如何工作的，所以我与将凯西的设备放入他大脑中的神经外科医生进行了交谈。

paras.en: David Brandman: My name is David Brandman, and I am the co-director of the UC Davis neuroprosthetics lab, developing next-generation neurotechnology to help people with paralysis. A brain-computer interface is a device that records brain signals from people that are paralyzed and then translates those brain signals to allow people to control objects in their environment using their minds.
paras.zh: 大卫·布兰德曼：我叫大卫·布兰德曼，是加州大学戴维斯分校神经修复实验室的联合主任，致力于开发下一代神经技术来帮助瘫痪患者。脑机接口是一种记录瘫痪者大脑信号的设备，然后翻译这些大脑信号，使人们能够用意念控制环境中的物体。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey’s implant is made of four arrays. Each of them are square and they’re about as wide as a peppercorn. Each array has a bunch of pointy ends that go down into his brain. They look a little like those metal cat brushes. Altogether, the four arrays contain 256 electrodes. These electrodes are all listening to Casey’s brain activity when he thinks about saying a word.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西的植入物由四个阵列组成。它们都是方形的，大约有花椒那么宽。每个阵列都有一堆尖头，深入他的大脑。它们看起来有点像那些金属猫刷。四个阵列总共包含 256 个电极。当凯西想要说一句话时，这些电极都会监听他的大脑活动。

paras.en: Brandman: The way this device works is by recording the electrical activity of the brain as he tries to speak.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：这个设备的工作原理是记录他试图说话时大脑的电活动。

paras.en: Sanders: The wires from Casey’s head carry those neural signals to nearby computers. That’s where machine learning algorithms attempt to do a very complex sort of matching. The algorithms match Casey’s brain activity patterns to the patterns that predictably occur with certain sounds called phonemes.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西头部的电线将这些神经信号传送到附近的计算机。这就是机器学习算法尝试进行非常复杂的匹配的地方。这些算法将凯西的大脑活动模式与某些称为音素的声音可预测出现的模式进行匹配。

paras.en: Brandman: We translate his brain signals into one of 39 different English phonemes. Now, a phoneme is a building block of language. So if I say the word hello, the word hello can be broken down into ha, uh, uhl, and oh. Hello.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：我们将他的大脑信号翻译成 39 种不同的英语音素之一。现在，音素是语言的组成部分。因此，如果我说“hello”这个词，那么“hello”这个词可以分解为“ha”、“uh”、“uhl”和“oh”。你好。

paras.en: Sanders: Next up, those algorithms assembles these phonemes into words by making its best guess about what Casey wants to say.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：接下来，这些算法通过对凯西想说的话进行最佳猜测，将这些音素组装成单词。

paras.en: Brandman: So I translate this brain activity into a phoneme and then, using artificial intelligence, turn phonemes into words, words into sentences, and sentences into paragraphs.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：所以我将这种大脑活动转化为音素，然后使用人工智能将音素转化为单词，单词转化为句子，句子转化为段落。

paras.en: Sanders: So that’s the process, and it allows Casey to type messages on Slack, text his friends, and send emails. Sometimes in his emails to me, he includes a tagline at the bottom: “Sent from my brain,” with that cute little pink brain emoji. His setup also lets him convert these typed messages into spoken words. These words show up on a screen for him where Casey proofreads them. If everything looks good, Casey gives the go-ahead and the system speaks the words out loud. Brandman tells me that when Casey tries to speak naturally, he can say about six understandable words per minute. That’s pretty slow.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这就是这个过程，它允许凯西在 Slack 上输入消息、给他的朋友发短信以及发送电子邮件。有时，在他给我的电子邮件中，他会在底部添加一个标语：“从我的大脑发送”，并带有可爱的粉红色大脑表情符号。他的设置还可以让他将这些键入的消息转换为口头语言。这些文字出现在他的屏幕上，凯西对其进行校对。如果一切看起来都不错，凯西就会批准，系统会大声说出这些话。布兰德曼告诉我，当凯西试图自然地说话时，他每分钟可以说大约六个可以理解的单词。那是相当慢的。

paras.en: Brandman: Using this prosthesis, he’s in the ballpark of 50 words per minute. Now, as I’m speaking to you right now, I’m speaking on the order of 120 to 150 words per minute, depending on how excited I am, right? So we’ve got him back to about a third of how quickly he spoke as an able-bodied person.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：使用这个假肢，他大约每分钟可以说 50 个单词。现在，正如我现在对你们讲话一样，我每分钟讲 120 到 150 个单词，具体取决于我的兴奋程度，对吧？因此，我们已经让他恢复了正常人说话速度的三分之一左右。

paras.en: Sanders: I had emailed Casey some questions a few days before our talk. But he didn’t answer them by email. He used his brain-computer interface to answer my questions in real time just by thinking about the words he wanted to say to me. As we introduced ourselves, I saw how the timescale had stretched.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在我们谈话前几天，我通过电子邮件向凯西发送了一些问题。但他没有通过电子邮件回复他们。他通过脑机接口实时回答我的问题，只需思考他想对我说的话。当我们自我介绍时，我发现时间已经被拉长了。

paras.en: Casey: It’s a challenge because we can have this conversation, but I am slower than the average Joe, even where we grew up.
paras.zh: 凯西：这是一个挑战，因为我们可以进行这样的对话，但我比普通人慢，即使在我们长大的地方也是如此。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey and I both grew up in the south, Casey in the Atlanta area and me in middle Tennessee. But he’s lived in the Bay Area for over 20 years now. And like me, his accent had faded.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西和我都在南部长大，凯西在亚特兰大地区，我在田纳西州中部长大。但他已经在湾区生活了 20 多年。和我一样，他的口音也消失了。

paras.en: Casey: And yes, I do not have much of a Southern accent anymore. But I love my roots, and I would love to show my daughter where and how I grew up. But it is exceedingly difficult to travel when you cannot move.
paras.zh: 凯西：是的，我不再有太多南方口音了。但我爱我的根，我很乐意向我的女儿展示我在哪里以及如何长大。但当你无法移动时，旅行就变得非常困难。

paras.en: Sanders: Before his mobility was limited, Casey did a lot of cool things.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在行动受限之前，凯西做了很多很酷的事情。

paras.en: Casey: I spent most of my professional career as a climate campaigner and have went all over the globe, fighting companies who are destroying the Earth and trying to bring some justice to our planet and the people who inhabit it. I am very fortunate because I have been able to do something that I love and also develop some deep friendships and relations with other phenomenal people.
paras.zh: 凯西：我职业生涯的大部分时间都是作为气候活动家，并走遍了全球，与破坏地球的公司作斗争，并试图为我们的星球和居住在地球上的人们伸张正义。我很幸运，因为我能够做我喜欢的事情，并与其他杰出的人建立了深厚的友谊和关系。

paras.en: Sanders: My interview with Casey was unlike any I’ve ever had. I’m used to being flexible for interviews. There’s time zone problems, language barriers, mathematicians who sometimes answer my questions in symbols and formulas. But when I logged on to Zoom to talk with Casey, I quickly realized this conversation would be different. I was self-conscious at the beginning of our talk. I fumbled around too much. I’d ask Casey a question and then another one before he had a chance to answer. I accidentally interrupted him a few times. Sometimes I wasn’t sure if he was composing an answer or just waiting for me to say something else. This poor performance on my part wasn’t unusual for Casey at all.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我对凯西的采访与我以往接受过的采访都不一样。我习惯于在面试中保持灵活性。有时区问题、语言障碍、数学家有时用符号和公式回答我的问题。但当我登录 Zoom 与凯西交谈时，我很快意识到这次谈话会有所不同。在我们谈话开始时我很不自在。我摸索太多了。在凯西有机会回答之前，我会问他一个问题，然后再问另一个问题。有几次我不小心打断了他的话。有时我不确定他是在写答案还是只是在等我说别的话。我的糟糕表现对凯西来说并不罕见。

paras.en: Casey: It is hard for people in your position to stay focused because you were not used to the cadence of a conversation this slowly.
paras.zh: 凯西：对于你这个职位的人来说，很难保持专注，因为你不习惯如此缓慢的谈话节奏。

paras.en: Sanders: He’s right. I was not used to it. And timing, in conversations and in life, is everything. Here’s Greg Bryant of UCLA.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他是对的。我不习惯。在谈话和生活中，时机就是一切。这是加州大学洛杉矶分校的格雷格·布莱恩特的报道。

paras.en: Bryant: Turns, conversational turns, happen at the level of hundreds of milliseconds at the longest. Two hundred milliseconds is a long turn. That’s a fifth of a second. I mean, that’s really fast. So if you are slow at all, it’s noticeable. We have to coordinate our talk so our terms make sense. I can’t take too long or be too quick to respond to your questions. I have to know when to stop and start. We get into this flow, kind of a dynamic, and that is hugely consequential for how we feel about the conversation, the other person, ourselves. You know, it’s all timing.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：对话，对话的轮转，最长发生在数百毫秒的水平。两百毫秒是一个漫长的转弯。那是五分之一秒。我的意思是，这真的很快。因此，如果你的速度很慢，就会很明显。我们必须协调我们的谈话，以便我们的条款有意义。我不能花太长时间或太快来回答你的问题。我必须知道何时停止和开始。我们进入这种流动状态，一种动态，这对于我们对谈话、对方和我们自己的感受非常重要。你知道，这一切都是时机。

paras.en: Sanders: Let’s turn to Jules. His words start in his brain too, but then they take a different route. He types them by looking at letters on a screen, then his voice clone says them. It’s also a slow process and one that takes a lot of mental power, too. At one point in our conversation, MA describes the effort this requires of Jules.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我们来谈谈朱尔斯。他的话语也从他的大脑中开始，但随后却走了不同的路线。他通过查看屏幕上的字母来输入它们，然后他的声音克隆说出它们。这也是一个缓慢的过程，也需要大量的精神力量。在我们的谈话中，MA 描述了 Jules 需要付出的努力。

paras.en: MA: And in his brain, you know, you can imagine he’s doing all these mental gymnastics, to, right now, he’s listening to us. He’s writing something with his eyes, like letter by letter to contribute to the conversation. Plus, he has the answers that he pre-wrote, of the questions that you asked. So it really is like, there’s a whole lot happening behind the scenes that of course anybody who doesn’t have to think about their voice takes for granted. So I’ll pause to let him complete what he’s saying.
paras.zh: MA：在他的大脑中，你知道，你可以想象他正在做所有这些心理体操，现在他正在听我们说话。他正在用眼睛写一些东西，比如一个字母一个字母地写，以促进对话。另外，他还预先写好了您提出的问题的答案。所以，实际上，幕后发生了很多事情，当然，任何不需要考虑自己声音的人都会认为这是理所当然的。所以我会停下来让他完成他所说的。

paras.en: Sanders: MA and I wait here for Jules to weigh in. So far you’ve heard ten seconds of the pause. The full length of the pause was a minute and 18 seconds.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：妈妈和我在这里等朱尔斯发表意见。到目前为止，你已经听到了十秒钟的停顿。整个暂停时间为一分十八秒。

paras.en: Jules: It is a challenge to communicate with people who don’t interact with me on a daily basis. I have a major bottleneck from my thoughts to actually speaking.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：与那些不每天与我互动的人沟通是一个挑战。从我的想法到实际说话，我遇到了一个很大的瓶颈。

paras.en: Sandes: And as with Casey, these pauses can introduce difficulties. Here’s speech pathologist Jessica Pietrowski with more on that.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：和凯西一样，这些停顿可能会带来困难。言语病理学家杰西卡·皮特罗斯基 (Jessica Pietrowski) 对此有更多了解。

paras.en: Pietrowski: Humans are not very comfortable with silence, especially communication. And when we’re talking to one another, we fill in the silences, it’s less awkward. And so, someone who’s communicating with a device is probably very used to those latency periods and some more silence and they’re comfortable with it. Whereas the person they’re communicating with is like, let’s keep it going, like this is, I want to help, I want to fill in the blanks, I don’t want this to feel awkward, but in turn, might make it a little more awkward than they think.
paras.zh: Pietrowski：人类不太适应沉默，尤其是交流。当我们互相交谈时，我们会填补沉默，这样就不那么尴尬了。因此，与设备通信的人可能非常习惯这些等待时间和更多的沉默，他们对此感到很舒服。而与他们交流的人却说，让我们继续下去，就像这样，我想提供帮助，我想填补空白，我不想让这感觉尴尬，但反过来，可能会让事情比他们想象的更尴尬。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules hates when people read his screen before he’s ready to say what he wants. This particular hate inspired a joke in his stand-up routine.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯讨厌人们在他准备好说出他想说的话之前阅读他的屏幕。这种特殊的仇恨在他的脱口秀节目中引发了一个笑话。

paras.en: [Jules audio]: People read off my screen while I’m typing and try to finish what I am saying. It’s like having to constantly deal with an over-competitive charades partner.
paras.zh: [Jules 音频]：当我打字时，人们会从我的屏幕上读出内容，并尝试完成我所说的内容。这就像必须不断地与竞争过度的猜字游戏伙伴打交道。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules and Casey encounter other people’s impatience constantly. Not that it isn’t well-intentioned but still, it does not help. Even worse, they face other people’s misconceptions about what they’re capable of. Casey is an interesting, funny and compelling conversationalist. That might not be apparent to everyone who doesn’t slow down to hear him. And that’s an assumption that really bothers him.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯和凯西经常遇到其他人的不耐烦。并不是说它不是出于好意，但它仍然没有帮助。更糟糕的是，他们面临着其他人对他们能力的误解。凯西是一位有趣、风趣且引人注目的健谈者。对于那些不放慢速度听他讲话的人来说，这一点可能并不明显。这个假设确实让他困扰。

paras.en: Casey: It is incredibly undignified and a terrible consequence of the health care system to treat me like this very quickly.
paras.zh: 凯西：医疗保健系统如此迅速地对待我，这是非常不尊严的，也是一个可怕的后果。

paras.en: Sanders: Brandman has seen this dismissal, this mistreatment too. It happens with some of the volunteers he works with on the BrainGate 2 project I mentioned earlier. That’s the same trial Casey’s in.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：布兰德曼也看到过这种解雇和虐待。我之前提到的与他一起参与 BrainGate 2 项目的一些志愿者身上就发生过这种情况。这与凯西所参加的审判相同。

paras.en: Brandman: I think as healthcare professionals, we conflate the inability to communicate with the lack of understanding. And I’ve witnessed this firsthand as I’ve watched doctors and nurses interact with my BrainGate participants and then treat them as if they are invalid. Or they’re not there because they’re unable to express themselves. And in fact, I go out of my way in the intensive care unit on the wards and dealing with anyone who’s dealing with my participants to say, look, you know, they’re inside. They’re there. They can understand everything that’s happening. They just happen to not be able to speak. And so please treat them with the respect and dignity that they deserve. And it’s a constant challenge for the participants that I work with. And it’s the reality of which we face and it’s the bias that we have against people that can’t speak for themselves.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：我认为作为医疗保健专业人员，我们将无法沟通与缺乏理解混为一谈。我亲眼目睹了这一点，因为我看到医生和护士与我的 BrainGate 参与者互动，然后像对待病人一样对待他们。或者他们不在那里是因为他们无法表达自己。事实上，我在病房的重症监护室里不遗余力地对待任何与我的参与者打交道的人，说，看，你知道，他们在里面。他们就在那里。他们可以理解正在发生的一切。他们只是碰巧无法说话。因此，请给予他们应有的尊重和尊严。对于与我一起工作的参与者来说，这是一个持续的挑战。这就是我们面临的现实，这就是我们对那些不能为自己说话的人的偏见。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey and the other people with ALS are not alone. Many people who have trouble talking or who just need more time can be judged this way. Here’s Karina Nagin from Bridging Voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西和其他患有 ALS 的人并不孤单。许多说话有困难或者只是需要更多时间的人都可以这样判断。这是来自 Bridging Voice 的卡琳娜·纳金 (Karina Nagin) 的报道。

paras.en: Nagin: It’s how people see you. And so when you have ALS and you cannot move and you don’t even have facial expressions and you’re hooked up to machines, people assume you’re not there. And we see this every day where people either don’t talk to the person with ALS, assuming that they can’t respond. They speak really loudly and slow. Their mind is completely working.
paras.zh: 纳金：这就是人们如何看待你。因此，当你患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）时，你无法移动，甚至没有面部表情，而且你还连接着机器，人们会认为你不在那里。我们每天都会看到这样的情况：人们要么不与 ALS 患者交谈，认为他们无法做出回应。他们说话声音很大而且很慢。他们的头脑完全运转。

paras.en: Sanders: For now, Casey’s words may be slow. But despite all the drawbacks, they are still an absolute marvel. Remember Hochberg from the start of this episode? He’s one of the neuroscientists who works with Casey, and he told me a story from the first few days of testing after Casey’s BCI was implanted.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：目前来看，凯西的话可能会很慢。但尽管有这些缺点，它们仍然是一个绝对的奇迹。还记得本集一开始的霍赫伯格吗？他是与凯西一起工作的神经科学家之一，他给我讲了凯西脑机接口植入后最初几天测试的故事。

paras.en: Hochberg: We gave him a 50-word vocabulary on day one. And even on day one, he was able to say some key sentences from those 50 high-value words.
paras.zh: Hochberg：第一天我们就给了他 50 个单词的词汇。即使在第一天，他就能说出这 50 个高价值单词中的一些关键句子。

paras.en: Sanders: At this point in the testing, Casey was asked to say some pre-specified sentences so researchers could test their system out.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在测试的这个阶段，凯西被要求说出一些预先指定的句子，以便研究人员可以测试他们的系统。

paras.en: Casey: Most of the sentences were what we called closed loops.
paras.zh: 凯西：大多数句子都是我们所说的闭环。

paras.en: Sanders: That means that the researchers already knew what brain activity patterns should go with the words Casey thought about saying. It was a test to see if the system was working.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这意味着研究人员已经知道什么大脑活动模式应该与凯西想要说的话相匹配。这是一个测试，看看系统是否正常工作。

paras.en: Casey: The decoder would be able to verify whether I was right or wrong, giving me short preloaded sentences to say. I was asked to say, “What good is that?”
paras.zh: 凯西：解码器将能够验证我是对还是错，给我预先加载的简短句子。我被要求说：“那有什么好处？”

paras.en: Sanders: “What good is that?” is not the most poignant sentence ever uttered, but it had a big effect both in the room and for researchers joining remotely by video.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：“那有什么好处？”这并不是有史以来最令人心酸的一句话，但它在房间里和通过视频远程加入的研究人员中产生了很大的影响。

paras.en: Casey: “What good is that?” Everyone is crying after I am successful.
paras.zh: 凯西：“那有什么好处？”当我成功后，每个人都在哭泣。

paras.en: Sanders: Later on, there was time for Casey to actually express himself.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：后来凯西有时间真正表达自己的想法。

paras.en: Casey: It was only after the first few sessions that I had any real time to say what I wanted for a good amount of time in relative privacy. That said, it was pure joy, even though I wasn’t getting to say what I wanted to say in that moment. It was a profound moment for me. The possibilities for the near future, for me and the rest of humanity were overwhelming to realize.
paras.zh: 凯西：只有在最初的几次会议之后，我才有时间在相对私密的情况下在相当长的时间内说出我想要的内容。也就是说，这是纯粹的快乐，尽管我当时没能说出我想说的话。这对我来说是一个意义深远的时刻。对于我和其他人来说，不久的将来的可能性是难以想象的。

paras.en: Sanders: Things only got better from there. To set the scene here, during this session, Hochberg was in his office and Casey was at his home, sitting in his living room. Hochberg was watching Casey on a screen.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：从那时起事情只会变得更好。为了设置这里的场景，在这次会议期间，霍赫伯格在他的办公室里，凯西在他的家里，坐在他的客厅里。霍赫伯格正在屏幕上看着凯西。

paras.en: Hochberg: On the second session, came back and gave him the full 125,000 plus word English dictionary to be able to select from. That is, the decoders and the AI and the machine learning language models would be able to select from basically a full dictionary. And the first thing that he said was something along the lines of, “Is this thing on?” Kind of a funny statement.
paras.zh: Hochberg：在第二次会议上，回来后给了他完整的 125,000 多个单词的英语词典供他选择。也就是说，解码器、人工智能和机器学习语言模型将能够从基本上完整的字典中进行选择。他说的第一句话是这样的：“这个东西开着吗？”有点有趣的说法。

paras.en: The next thing that he said on the second day of using brain-computer interface, or the second thing that we decoded was, “I’m looking for a cheetah.” And it’s the second day. We know there’s all kinds of opportunities for decoding errors. And when I saw that, I said, you know, there’s no way that the second sentence on the second day of using an implanted brain-computer interface is going to say anything about a cheetah. You know, that’s obviously a decoding error and that’s fine.
paras.zh: 使用脑机接口的第二天，他说的下一句话，或者说我们解码的第二件事是，“我在寻找猎豹。”而且已经是第二天了。我们知道存在各种解码错误的机会。当我看到这一点时，我说，你知道，使用植入脑机接口的第二天的第二句话不可能说任何关于猎豹的事情。你知道，这显然是一个解码错误，但没关系。

paras.en: Sanders: Hochberg could see Casey on the screen, but he couldn’t see something really important that had just happened in the room.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：霍赫伯格可以在屏幕上看到凯西，但他看不到房间里刚刚发生的真正重要的事情。

paras.en: Hochberg: His four-year-old daughter had just walked into the room dressed as a cheetah.
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格：他四岁的女儿刚刚打扮成猎豹走进房间。

paras.en: Sanders: Here’s Casey remembering the same moment.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是凯西回忆起的同一时刻。

paras.en: Casey: Yes, I remember this time very well. It was the second session of talking that I experienced early in August 2024. My daughter was incredibly cute in her cheetah outfit. This was one of her favorite animals. They were going through a phase where everything they did was super fast, running from thing to thing. Everyone was thinking that it must have been a mistake that I could not use this language. It was so random. This was only from the people like Leigh who were not in the room with us. The researchers who were there could validate that, yes, I said this. I meant it because of the unique context.
paras.zh: 凯西：是的，这一次我记得很清楚。这是我在 2024 年 8 月上旬经历的第二次谈话。我女儿穿着猎豹装，非常可爱。这是她最喜欢的动物之一。他们正在经历一个阶段，他们所做的一切都非常快，从一件事跑到另一件事。每个人都认为我不会使用这种语言一定是一个错误。真是太随意了。这只是来自像 Leigh 这样的人，他们没有和我们一起在房间里。那里的研究人员可以证实，是的，我说过这一点。我这么说是因为独特的背景。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s one of those moments that many parents have. A kid does something cute, a parent plays along. But in this moment for Casey and his child, it was anything but ordinary.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是许多父母都会经历的时刻之一。孩子做一些可爱的事情，父母也跟着一起玩。但此刻对于凯西和他的孩子来说，这绝非平常。

paras.en: Hochberg: And she was born around the time that he was diagnosed with ALS. And one could imagine that because the voice that was coming out of the computer was a version of his own voice, and then the rest of the interaction was between dad and daughter. And it was between parent and child.
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格：她是在他被诊断出患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症的时候出生的。人们可以想象，因为从电脑中传出的声音是他自己声音的一个版本，然后剩下的互动就发生在爸爸和女儿之间。而且是父母和孩子之间的事。

paras.en: Sanders: The BCI had given Casey something priceless, a minute to play with his sweet little cheetah.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：BCI 给了凯西一些无价的东西，那就是和他可爱的小猎豹玩耍的一分钟。

paras.en: Casey: I was quietly confident that it would work the way it ended up working for me. I had done a lot of research and the thing was that the technology was on the cusp of a breakthrough. And why not me? I asked myself.
paras.zh: 凯西：我暗自相信它会以最终为我工作的方式发挥作用。我做了很多研究，事实是这项技术正处于突破的边缘。为什么不是我呢？我问自己。

paras.en: Sanders: Early on in the research project, Casey and his wife had been told not to expect it to work. This was an experiment and the outcome was far from certain. Casey, however, was optimistic.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在研究项目的早期，凯西和他的妻子被告知不要指望它会起作用。这是一个实验，结果还远未确定。然而，凯西却很乐观。

paras.en: Hochberg: So to me, seeing it work that quickly and that powerfully really, really emphasized that these are technologies that are going to be able to restore not only activities of daily living, not only key kind of instrumental activities of daily living, but they’re going to restore communication between parent and child. They’re going to restore communication between friends and family and care partners and health care providers.
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格：所以对我来说，看到它如此迅速和强大地发挥作用，确实强调了这些技术不仅能够恢复日常生活活动，不仅能够恢复日常生活的关键工具性活动，而且它们还将恢复父母和孩子之间的沟通。他们将恢复朋友和家人、护理伙伴和医疗保健提供者之间的沟通。

paras.en: Sanders: Because this is a podcast about the human voice, I’ve been asking people I interview what their voice means to them. Here’s Casey’s answer.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：因为这是一个关于人类声音的播客，所以我一直在问我采访的人他们的声音对他们意味着什么。这是凯西的回答。

paras.en: Casey: It means so much. I think it is the most important thing that I have lost in this whole disease.
paras.zh: 凯西：这意义重大。我认为这是我在整个疾病中失去的最重要的东西。

paras.en: Sanders: Getting it back, even in a limited form, is everything.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：收回它，即使是以有限的形式，也是一切。

paras.en: Casey: It was so amazing to be able to be understood right from the get-go and to be able to talk and respond, respond to my daughter, especially because that was lacking completely from my life up to that point.
paras.zh: 凯西：能够从一开始就被理解，能够与我的女儿交谈和回应，回应我的女儿，这真是太神奇了，特别是因为在那之前我的生活完全缺乏这一点。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey’s restored voice changed his life.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西恢复的声音改变了他的生活。

paras.en: Casey: It is the ability to parent my daughter. It is the ability to connect with my wife. It is the ability to make a wry joke with my friends. Timing is everything, and that is why having nothing, this is completely revolutionary. And to look back on my previous answer, it is something that really can still improve.
paras.zh: 凯西：这是养育女儿的能力。这是与我妻子联系的能力。这是与朋友开玩笑的能力。时机就是一切，这就是为什么什么都没有，这是完全革命性的。回顾一下我之前的回答，确实还有待改进。

paras.en: Sanders: At the beginning of the experiment, the research team had told Casey and his wife that they’d be able to try using the BCI for casual chats just a few hours a week. Those hours felt like a huge gift at the time, considering that they hadn’t been able to talk meaningfully for a long time. Here’s Brandman.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在实验开始时，研究团队告诉凯西和他的妻子，他们可以尝试使用脑机接口进行每周几个小时的休闲聊天。考虑到他们已经很长时间无法进行有意义的交谈，这些时间在当时感觉就像是一份巨大的礼物。这是布兰德曼。

paras.en: Brandman: As we kept coming to his house two or three times a week, things kept getting better and better. And it got to a point where Casey wanted to use the system to say all the things that he wanted to say.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：随着我们每周去他家两三次，事情变得越来越好。凯西想用这个系统说出他想说的所有事情。
